title: Excellent app, tucks all the boxes
body:
Shifted here from another habit tracker - Way of...   This app is streets ahead of anything else out there. It's sickly made, very flexible (habit to be done 2 times per week, etc) only on specific days, etc. 

The other unique feature is the concept of routines, morning, afternoon and night. The app then shows you stuff pertinent to that time of the day. title: Gutes Design und gutes Konzept, die Ausführung lässt zu wünschen übrig
body:
iPhone 12
Ich verwende die App jetzt seit über drei Wochen, am Anfang war noch alles gut und die App hat Problemlos funktioniert. Sie ist simple und verständlich aufgebaut, nach dem Konzept less is more. Das einzige was mit gefehlt hat, bzw. mir immer noch fehlt, ist die Integration von schlechten Angewohnheiten. 
Dennoch ist es seit vier Tagen so, dass die App nicht erkennt, wann ein neuer Tag beginnt. So stehe ich in der Früh auf und bin noch im Menü des letzten Tages, kann aber am heutigen Tag nichts ändern. Manchmal hilft Neustarten, manchmal nicht…
Dafür sind die 18€ (im Angebot) für ein Jahr schon viel… 
Also, liebe Entwickler, ihr habt eine gute App, doch sie gehört optimiert. Wenn diese zwei Kritikpunkte gelöst sind, ist es eindeutig dass ich 5 Sterne geben wird. 
Für alle, die überlegen das Abo zu kaufen würde ich empfehlen noch abzuwarten, ob diese Probleme gelöst werden.

title: Inzwischen ein Abo obwohl für die Premium-Funktionen bezahlt wurde
body:
Die Funktionen sind sehr gut und die App auch leicht zu bedienen. 

Allerdings gibt es einen Wermutstropfen. Ich habe die App bereits 2017 genutzt und damals „alle“ Premium-Funktionen über einen In-App Kauf freigeschaltet. Jetzt ist es auf Abo umgestellt und die Zahlung plötzlich nicht mehr einmalig. Das ist meiner Meinung nach nicht in Ordnung. Die ursprünglich bezahlten Funktionen sind nicht mehr nutzbar.

Wenn etwas ursprünglich als Einmalzahlung deklariert ist, soll es auch so weiterlaufen. Für Neukunden kann man das durchaus umstellen, aber für Bestandskunden, die sich bereits für das Modell entschiedenen haben (und das ein Kaufkriterium war!) ist das absolut daneben.

Für Bestandskunden gehört automatisch ein gratis Lifetime-Abo erstellt. Denn das wurde ursprünglich versprochen und bezahlt. Alles andere ist nicht akzeptabel.

Daher gibt es 5 Sterne und 4 Sterne Abzug für das Ärgernis und ca 30 Euro/ Jahr statt einmaligen 4,49 Euro.

title: It's ok, polished but lacking detail
body:
The UI is nice. The overall structure is nice. But almost every feature stops at 80% usefulness and just doesn't quite get over the line.

If you have a habit that consists of several steps that don't need to be tracked on their own; you're out of luck. There is a description field, but you can't even put a new line in it, let alone bullet points. Ideally you would be able to add sub items with check boxes.

If you have something that you only need to do monthly, you can only choose a specific day of the month. Ideally, you would be able to choose "monthly by the 14th" or "by the end of the month".

There are quite a few more of these small limitations that add up to this app just not quite being truly useful.

title: Solid habit tracking app, but buggy
body:
This is a good app - I’ve been using it for several months now to track and build upon my habits. I could never track habits in a journal just because a journal is not as accessible as my phone is, making this app very useful for habit tracking.

The interface is a bit buggy, though. Many times, when I try to mark a habit as “done” by swiping it, the app glitches and swipes another habit instead. This is a bit annoying as you then have to figure out which habit was incorrectly swiped. This happens nearly every day unfortunately.

I would also love more color and icon options for the habit labels. For example, the “MultiTimer” app uses icons by Icons8, which contains *heaps* of free ones. 

If these are addressed by developers I would consider upgrading my review to 5 stars :)

title: No iCloud backup or sync, extremely buggy app, limited support
body:
I’m extremely disappointed in this app. It has so much potential, but it’s been buggy and crashing from the very beginning.

MOST disappointing is that there’s no mention in the faq that iCloud backup is currently disabled (since they’re having problems with it), and therefore, you can’t save your data! I tried deleting and reinstalling the app hoping it would fix the crashes, and I lost months of data and dozens of customised habits I had setup.

If you lose or have to change your phone, or if you delete the app, beware that your data isn’t saved in the cloud and you’ll be starting fresh! 😬😬

SUPER disappointing for such an expensive subscription. 

If iCloud back up (and syncing between devices) gets fixed I might consider changing my rating, but it’s still pretty buggy and laggy even without...

Edit: so glad I just found other alternative apps at similar or better prices. “Daily planner” and “done” seem A LOT more user friendly. I’d been holding out waiting for the problems with this app to be fixed... but I’m now glad to be cancelling my subscription and be rid of this app :)

title: Terrible interface design. Canceled after 7 days
body:
This app just didn’t work for me on my iPhone 6s, with the current iOS. It is pretty crazy how hard it was to just mark off when you have completed a goal or habit. The interface would mostly do everything except what I was trying to do. 

I’ve never experienced anything this badly designed on an iPhone app before. I’ve used a lot of different habit apps and none of them ever made it difficult to mark off a completed item.

Sliding the item on your list to the right is supposed to bring up the numbers to select how many times you have completed the item. 

Trying to get this to work in reality was incredibly frustrating. It keeps going to the calendar, it was too easy to accidentally Skip the item and I was always having to undo...it would go to a different page...everything except let me mark it as completed!!!!

There’s no option for challenges like Taking a break from alcohol to configure it to automatically mark the day as successful. This meant that every time I forgot or gave up trying to use the frustrating interface- I got a failure message and had to start again.

Cancelled after trying to use for 7 days. I’m a developer with 17 years experience in interaction design. Can’t believe this passed any user testing. Appalling design.

title: It’s great!
body:
I’ve been using this app for a few days (free trial) and it feels like it was made for me. I’m a very visual person but bullet journals; post it notes or calendars stopped working a long time ago ago. Recently, due to depression , I felt the need to be more organized and productive and unfortunately Ive not been able to stay focused on the most simple things .. other apps can have all these reminder options or visual aids and etc however what I like about this one particularly is the fact we can: 
- allocate a certain amount of time for each habit 
- still tick it off as complete even without setting the timer (sometimes i forget to start a timer and by the time I’m done with a task I can just tick it off)
- having a timer on while you’re doing specific things allows you to understand the amount of time you spend on that activity and makes you focus more on it than if you just had a reminder And after a few days you start planing what tasks to do first based on the time you need for them so you’ll get into routines without forcing yourself into stuff as it happens with planners. 
- the fact you can have sounds on and off while the timer is on is cute. I don’t feel the need to get sounds for meditation so far as there’s some sounds in the app already.
Unfortunately I’m on the free trial and can’t  afford it yet but I can’t wait to see the graphs and all my activity laid out like that. Also be able to have multiple habits laid out. 

Thank you!

title: iCloud sync broken, fixed, now broken again
body:
The best habit app for my needs: It has a clean, beautiful interface and is functional and uncluttered with useful statistics.

I‘ve used this on iPhone for a while and wished it would use iCloud to sync across devices. This update happened a little while ago and has made it so much easier to get the productivity benefits of this app!

I was thrilled this week to see that the app now fills the entire iPad screen - it looks much better! I have an iPad Pro 12.9”, so there’s quite a bit of empty space that I think could be utilised to display more information on the one screen without having to go through menus, but it’s a great start.

The next thing I’d like to see is the ability to add notes to days where I miss a habit, instead of only those days where I skip or complete one. I’m far more likely to want to add a note regarding a habit I missed.

Update: new interface looks fresh and exciting! Love the new design work! Also a nice touch to give users options with the interface, as I suppose not everyone is always going to appreciate change. Options are good!

Update 2: iCloud sync not working again; won’t sync between iPhone and iPad

title: Solid app (with caveat)
body:
This is a great tracking app with clean interface and encouraging layout/wording. The reminders and settings are good and provide sufficient customisation with it being bogged down with too many details. 

(A tip for those looking to build good habits using this app: when you start using the app, don’t create all the habits at at once. It will play with your mind and make you feel as if you’ve already mastered all of them. There’s a psychology term for this but I forget what it’s called. Create new habits as you actually start to do them.)

My caveat is that I get premium features without paying for a subscription; I bought the app way back when it was a one-time purchase and the developer is awesome enough not to make me pay again.

title: Version 1.7: Constant nagging for an overpriced subscription
body:

CONS: 1-Constant nagging to upgrade to the paid version (“GO PREMIUM!”), and it’s a subscription, which is ridiculous for an app that doesn’t provide any content. 

2-As of writing, a 12-month subscription costs $19.49 - for that much you could buy two habit-tracker apps outright, and still have enough left over for a coffee.

CONCLUSION: This is a good habit-tracker, but it’s ruined by constant nagging and an overpriced subscription model. Look elsewhere.

It had everything I had been looking for in a habit tracker and, although advertisements did occasionally pop up, I didn't pay too much attention to it. That was until I got one notification in particular, however; "Upgrade to unlock unlimited habits." I understand the aim of making such an app with in-app purchases is to make a profit, but this is unbelievable. Limiting a habit tracking app to only five habits? Ridiculous. And, as much as I love the small snippet I've gotten, I refuse to pay nearly thirty dollars for an annual subscription. title: Subscription, really?
body:
It’s all very well to say that an App has a beautiful, simple interface etc etc but, at the end of the day, the question is whether it’s value for money. I’d certainly agree that it’s beautiful and simple. 

The reason I can’t give a glowing review for Productive is because of the subscription model. How can anyone think that almost $2/month is value for money for the functionality provided? Granted it would take a little time to get the user interface to look as nice as this, but this is about as basic as a application can get! I wrote the pseudo code and coded up a functional framework for this in less than a day, since I like the concept but refuse to support a subscription model where it’s not justified.

Subscription models should be applied when new functionality and improvements are released on a regular basis. Talk about age of decadence.

title: What I've been looking for!
body:
I've been searching for the longest time for an app to help me manage my daily routines. 
As a parent of small children trying to stay productive at home and work, routine is key. I've searched high and low for a task management app that allows me to set routine tasks for certain days so I don't have to juggle everything in my head. Dividing the day into morning, afternoon and evening and specifying the time allows me to manage my day between morning, work and after work without having a cluttered tasks list. Although it's not its intended purpose it's the perfect system for managing the routine lifestyle of a working parent. 
My only criticism is I would like to be able to also use it to manage one off tasks and add them to specific days. Currently I have to use a separate app for that. 

Love the interface and design.

There's only one thing missing: it would be nice if there was an option to set the first day of the week to Monday, since many countries have Monday as the first day. If I choose to run 3x a week, and I do this on Tuesday, Thursday & Sunday, it doesn't count as a streak/habit done because Sunday is part of the next week (according to the app). In Europe, it's not so it would be nice if changing first day of the week would become an option!

O erro em questão seria a hora que você completa um hábito e arrasta para o lado ele não completa e só faz o barulho e fica assim por um tempo, tendo que fechar e abrir o aplicativo novamente e na maioria das vezes isso também não funciona, ou seja é algo que você tenque deixar pra lá por um tempo… não recomendo para quer quer criar uma rotina com isso, não dá pra se dar ao luxo de deixar para lá algo que você usa para organizar sua rotina e outra coisa deveriam colocar a função de mover a ordem dos hábitos temos, tipo arrastar e deixar um acima ou embaixo do outro.

title: Widgets inúteis
body: Olá. Sou usuário premium, acabei de assinar pelo meu iPhone. Porém, me decepcionei imediatamente após assinar, pois percebi duas falhas em comparação ao Microsoft To-do que é gratuito: eu não consigo logar no Productive pela versão web, já tentei absolutamente de tudo. E o segundo erro grave são os widgets para iPhone: comparem os Widgets do seu app com os Widgets do Microsoft To-Do. Os seus widgets não tem utilidade alguma, pois são apenas quadrados pretos sem nenhuma palavra e sem absolutamente nada além de um quadrado preto. O que está acontecendo? Eu posso me arrepender e receber o meu dinheiro de volta caso vocês não corrijam isso? Grato. (Hello. I'm a premium user, I just subscribed through my iPhone. However, I was immediately disappointed after subscribing, as I noticed two flaws compared to Microsoft To-do, which is free: I can't log into Productive via the web version, I've tried absolutely everything. And the second serious mistake is widgets for iPhone: compare your app's Widgets with Microsoft To-Do Widgets. Your widgets are useless as they are just black squares with no words and absolutely nothing but a black square. What's happening? Can I regret it and get my money back if you don't fix it? Grateful.)

title: Me senti enganado e desinstalei na hora.
body:
O app parece ter uma boa estrutura, aparentemente bem desenhado, mas algo me indignou logo de início. 
Após as “configurações iniciais” o app me propõe 1 semana de teste grátis pra logo em seguida cobrar 112 por ano, o teste graros condicionado a assinatura posterior. 
Mas como eu vou assinar algo se eu nem testei? Ocorre que ao declinar da “proposta” logo em seguida aparece uma oferta de 48% de desconto. E se eu aceito de primeira? 
Creio que não seja ilegal essa forma de trabalho, mas achei no mínimo imoral. Não quis nem saber mais como era.

title: It’s OK, but there is space to become a better app
body:
since this is a productive tool and the idea is also to be a reminder of your activities it would be important if the open  habits/activities persist on lock screen till you decide to ignore or complete them... Currently the app shows the reminder once  and if you unlock your phone and block it again the reminder goes out of the screen... PLEASE CONSIDER ADD THIS FUNCTION ASAP.

Widget is good, but a persistent notification on the lock screen, just as the native reminders does would be awesome! Please consider this function on the next updates! Certainly it will be a five star app then!

Also after if you did not choose “completed” or “ignered” the all should express a OVERDUE HABIT status

title: Expensive app and discount if you try to cancel.
body:
Be careful. This app is very expensive for their purpose. Also, when I cancelled my free subscription that would cost me a full price a year, they offered a discount for more than 70% only because I tried to cancel. Which means they could have offered this price since the beginning, but they didn’t.
Now, every app wants us to pay subscriptions, but the world cannot work this way. We already pay subscriptions for everything. Netflix, amazon, spotify... People are not going to keep paying this app every month. It should be one price forever.

title: Parece bom, mas tudo nele é pago
body:
Usei o app por 5 minutos. 

Abri, criei três tarefas e atingi o limite da versão gratuita. Nesse meio tempo, vi 5 mensagens na minha cara pedindo para assinar. 

Um app que parece muito útil, mas é extremamente limitado obrigando o usuário a adquirir a versão paga para utilizar recursos simples que outros apps, até mesmo padrões já instalados no iOS, já permitem fazer. 

Além de pop-ups excessivos pedindo para assinar a versão paga a cada clique que você dá. 

Existe a avaliação por (apenas) 7 dias grátis, mas gostaria que o app fosse menos intrusivo ao me oferecer a versão paga e que me oferecesse um pouco mais de funções ou período de teste maior para que eu possa ter certeza que vou querer assinar ou não.

title: DESIGN FUNCIONAL, PORÉM...
body:
O design é ótimo, bem intuitivo, objetivo e de funcionalidade clara.

Porém o aplicativo deixa a desejar no propósito de ser um auxiliador de atividades. Exemplo:

- Beber água, verificar postura e alongamentos são atividades que devem ser feitas de tempo em tempo. O aplicativo não possui uma funcionalidade onde coloques “me lembrar de 30 em 30 minutos”.
- A técnica de Pomodoro funciona, normalmente, em intervalos de 30/5 ou 40/5, e também não há como inserir uma notificação/lembrete para quando chega nos 30 ou 40 minutos de atividade, para cumprir o intervalo de 5 minutos antes de retornar.

Entre outros detalhes.

Na verdade o aplicativo acaba sendo um alarme com um design bonito e um pouco de métricas. E só. Nada de ser realmente um auxiliador com lembretes realmente funcionais.

title: Scammy it broken system
body:
I was double billed by this company. 

I went ahead with the free 7 day trial to test it, at which point I was offered a promotional price of 24.99 for the first year. Like most professional apps, you’d think that this would then take the place of the 7 day trial and eliminate it as you’ve just purchased the year. 

Instead after the 7 days, I was billed the full 49.99.. So I paid twice for the same year. 24.99 and 49.99. 

Not sure if this is something they do hoping if enough people just don’t notice and rectify it they’ll pocket the money and it’s a handy little trick, or if they just don’t know how to run a business. 

If someone buys a year, you should not then bill them after a 7 day trial ultimately charging them TWICE for the same year of your service. 

Make it right.

Everything is horribly unintuitive. 

Some simple UI fixes would be 
1. widen the swipe regions on the left and right sides of the screen, when navigating between Morning -> evening I’m constantly skipping tasks by mistake
2. Allow a reordering of tasks once created. Even simply swapping task ID’s on the backend would allow you to change positions of tasks.

title: Stupid move going to Subscription
body:
I think the whole “hey let’s change our ‘buy once’ purchase option to a yearly subscription” trend is completely stupid. Given that most of us fork over subscriptions for Netflix, Prime, etc, plus mobile/internet fees… how much of the general population (excluding rich people) can afford to have any more subscription-based items?

And since almost every single Apple developer out there has now switched to this format, how many people do they think can actually afford to buy lots of apps that all have yearly subscriptions?

Since this stupid subscribe thing came on, I have not bought any app with this setup. I have gone out of my way to find a competitor who has a fixed price.

Now… I am pretty sure I bought Productive app a long time ago. I stopped using it a while ago, and when I opened it again to start re-using it, I saw this “you have to pay us monthly/yearly fees now to use our product. 

 So what am I going to do? I am going to delete this app, and find a dev that only charges a one-time fee. 

Boo urns to Productive!

title: Subbed for two years. In the end, not a 3rd
body:
This was an alright app for a bit of time but then it’s usefulness wore away. 

Two things really other me:
1 - after some time if you don’t swipe it stops reminding you. Maybe this is there to try to not pester you or something, and if so, it’s a terrible design choice. The whole reason I paid for this was to remind me of many little annoying things I have to do. I do not want to have to open an app as well as do those little annoying things. (After all if I wasn’t annoyed by them, I probably wouldn’t need the app in the first place) so this mechanic of it silently deciding to stop reminding me is terrible. 

But I tried to make it work. But then:

2 - the second, more, I guess, taste/choice based aspects that I don’t like are the little editorial comments on the reminders such as “just do it” “you can do it” “keep it up” etc. I wish I could turn that off. 

3rd, less important but still very annoying, is if you select a challenge and don’t click a thing within a 24hr window, the challenge sends you a “you lied” or “you didn’t follow through” message (those are approximate quotes: but it was something a little harsh sounding) and cuts off the challenge. Which if you were using, as I was, as a template for a cluster of good habits, just kills any enthusiasm and seems to be irreversible.

It’s like the app is needy. And if you don’t constantly tell it you’ve done the thing, it gets cranky. (Even if you do do the thing irl!) Then in its cranky state, throws a tantrum and just stops reminding you all together.  

That’s a deep structural flaw for me. Maybe others like it. I dunno. But given the other two issues I’ve had, it just made Productive less used and eventually I went back to the more reliable reminders app built into iOS. 

I’m one month one to a 12 month auto-renew, wish I had caught it in time, but oh well.

body: Having this app is like having a personal assistant/ life coach.  You build an amazing, productive routine, and the next day you wake up with the best life assistance. Soon one day turns into a week, then a month, and then before you know it you’ve had the most productive, transformative year of your life.  It might take a few days to get the routine perfected for your personalized, realistic life, but it is soo simple to tweak the routine as you go.  For me personally it’s actually a dream come true.  Thank you guys for making this app so fabulous.  Oh and if you ever have feedback to give about features you would like to see in the app... send them in!  These champs actually listen!!

title: GET HABITICA INSTEAD
body:
TL;DR: The app itself is great, but the updates are never properly tested before release, so it’s always buggy and broken. Customer service won’t always believe you when you report a bug, instead giving you really insultingly simple tips that imply “it’s not broken, YOU’RE just not using it properly”.

This app often breaks and becomes very difficult to use after an update, so much so that I cringe when I see it updating. It’s almost as if no testing gets done before release. Use a different app if you’re an adult with ADHD or you plan to use it to manage your entire to-do list. (Habitica is great!) It’s just not going to be there to help you every day.

*Edit in response to the developer response:* Trust me, I have, way too often, and almost always because of a bug caused by an update. No other app in my phone has me emailing support as often as this one. So I’D appreciate if I could trust it to work.

*Update*
I’ve been trying for three weeks to get a bug from 2.0.0 fixed. The bug did not get fixed in the 2.1.0 update even though I was told it was being fixed. This bug is causing old, completed one time tasks to remain stuck in the Any time order list, and I can’t access them from another tab to delete them. In fact, some of these old tasks could be described as zombies, because tasks I completed in OCTOBER reappeared. Since the 2.0.0 update, the list has gotten longer and longer as I complete more tasks and they don’t disappear/can’t be deleted from the reordering list. Three weeks later, customer service is trying to tell me there’s nothing wrong with the app, I just need to delete the habits I don’t want anymore in the habits tab, completely ignoring that already explained that they DON’T show up in the habits tab, ONLY in the Any time order list, and therefore CANNOT be deleted. 🤦🏾‍♀️

*Update*
It took a month but my app is fixed and finally functional again. Yay? I give it three stars now because I can actually use it without much hassle now. Two stars off for unreliability and issues with customer service. Otherwise, this app is fantastic.
Edit: I take it back. The fix came with a new bug. 🤦🏾‍♀️ I swear they don’t test before release. I’m taking my third star back.

*Update*
Screw it, I’m switching to Habitica. I’m not wasting hours of my time wrestling with an app that doesn’t work. One star, only because I can’t give zero stars.

title: Should include specific days for habits.
body:
I stopped using this app because it didn’t accurately portray my week. 

If you skip a habit, it doesn’t break your streak but prevents you from getting a perfect day. So if you have a bunch of weekly tasks, your schedule will always be heavy in the beginning of the week. When you see your overview of the week, it’ll always show in the beginning that you didn’t have perfect days which looks discouraging.

For example, if you plan to go to the gym on Saturdays, Sundays and Tuesdays, then run on Wednesdays and Fridays, Productive will just remind you to do both in the beginning of your week. Since I don’t plan to do both on the same day, the first few days of my week will always show that it was incomplete. 

It would be great if you can choose specific days when scheduling tasks instead. For now, I’ve switched over to Habit List but am hoping Productive will eventually fix this issue.

title: Free version has a limit of 4 habits
body: The habit tracker I used previously for about a year, had a major bug that made the application unusable. I wasn’t gonna wait any longer for it to be fixed, so I started looking around the App Store for a replacement. I was pretty excited to start using Productive as it was simple but not completely bare, with a clean, easy-to-use interface. After I downloaded the app, I immediately started setting everything up. When I went to add a 4th habit, I got an offer to subscribe to the premium version of the application. I click the X in the top left-hand corner and try again. Same offer comes up. It was clear this wasn’t an advertisement, and that I would have to pay money to use this application further. I get it, developers have to make money somehow, and they deserve it, but I can’t help but feel there are other ways they could have gone about making a profit.

body:

This app is worth paying for; the developers have done a great job and should be paid for their efforts. A single payment for the pro version would be more appropriate for this type of app. It doesn’t have renewed or updated content monthly, so why would I pay monthly? This app is not worth the ongoing payment structure.

title: App developers are not listening to their customers
body:

The product itself was positive but the customers were disappointed in the cost of the annual subscription fee of $18 in October. I continued reading the reviews and could see the same disappointment in Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun and July. Thought I would download to see what the price would be now as the feedback was “ Thank you, we are listening, we will revisit this when we update app”. Well, they did this by increasing the annual price to $30.99. I am also not interested in an annual fee. You are losing me before I even try. Your team should do an analysis of how many people you would get t the $5-8 one time buy range they said they would pay versus the ones abandoning the app. You might have gotten more in volume. It’s my prediction that without listening customers and doing the exact opposite of what they are continually asking will land you in the “apps that once were category”. author: It gets harder!

title: Subscription
body:
I’m honestly disappointed that it’s not a one time purchase and it’s a monthly or yearly subscription. There is no justification for a subscription. It’s not an interactive context course and it’s not like it updates every month with better or more features. 

You want people to pay 18/year to get unlimited habits (other apps already have this feature), to get stats (people know if they did better or not or how long they did it without this feature). 

why would you even need a passcode lock for the app. It’s not like people are gonna specially go on your phone (that will already have a passcode) and be like oh man I need to know what they’re working on !!! 

Better reminders? Just set an alarm on your build in phone alarm? Other apps send you notifications to do it for free? And you want us to pay 18/year for a “light” theme? 

Completely ridiculous. 

I would’ve paid a one time fee as I need more habits. Even if it was $18 one time payment. But yearly? Makes no sense. I hope developers rethink this app business plan. Something must be wrong if they have to charge 17/year for “premium” features that do not add value when other apps offer it for free.

title: Great app - surprisingly effective
body:
I got this app as a last effort to build strong daily habits and hold myself accountable to the goals I've set. The app was simple, user-friendly, and broke things down for me into digestible chunks. 
What I did not expect from the app was just how easily the habits were to form once I got started. There was just something about the notion of a "streak", where after I had completed my habits for a certain number of days in a row it became absurdly difficult to NOT do the habit out of pure self-competition and not wanting to lose my streak. I am now to the point where my daily tasks are 100% habit - I don't even think about whether or not I have the motivation to do them - I just get them done.

title: Near perfect mini-habit tracker
body:
This is the first app I've used that properly handles the psychology around mini-habits.

It allows you to retroactively complete an item (e.g. If you read after midnight you can still check it off, or if you forget to check something), and therefore the streaks are really useful and don't get broken by accident. 

The second power feature is being able to have a weekly task, or one on mon-wed-fri that is still tracked by streaks. 

This app has allowed me to remove my mini habits from Omni focus and keep that app dedicated to projects and one-off tasks.

title: Simple, engaging and effective, but some key flaws
body:
I really love using this app and feel motivated to improve my habits as a result. It’s engaging and intuitive, but I had to stop using it for almost 2 years due to a key flaw.
 
The app is really poor at storing stats, as any change to a habit results in all habit history being reset. As someone who wants to measure my progress over time, and change my habit goals, this is incredibly frustrating.

As an example, you track your exercise days and have a month of activity logged. You meet your goal of exercising 3 days per week, and a result increase the target to 4 days per week. The app will reset all your habit data if you make this change, and now you can’t see your progress since you started. 

This app is supposed to enable users to improve their habits and grow, but it fails at this when it feels like you are starting from scratch after every change to a habit. If they can fix this I’ll be a user for life, but it’s a dealbreaker

title: Productivity is a life saver
body:
For people with ADD /ADHD, as well as people who have an issue with breaking out of phone addiction or simply try to build up a routine and keep up with it without having to remember everything by themselves. This is like a manager that tells you what to do at the perfect time. I highly recommend this to everyone!

I have a small improvement suggestion: for people who bought the full version, like me, it would be cool, if "multiple reminders" were still coming even if they marked it as done earlier that day. I would like to remind myself to stand up regularly from my desk, also to drink a glass of water regularly - i am aware of the boost mode, but it is only available for one habit at a time which is not enough for me. I thought about creating the same habit with the same title multiple times for different times a day but I was wondering if there could be the possibility of an easier solution from your side! 
Best regards :)

今天我首次下载，其实还没有开始用，就提示办理一年的会员，奔着不像乱花钱的我，打算先体验一下app的各项功能，再去考虑花钱的问题。
因此我就毫不犹豫关掉付款的倒数界面，但是换来的是一个讽刺性的提示，原话我忘记了，意思是说我还没有做好改变自己的准备。这让我很难接受，我还没有开始使用，就是因为没有充会员就被定义为这样的人，我觉得很可笑。
你们开发一个软件，以盈利为目的，我可以理解，但是也需要给用户一个付费的理由，对不起我已经卸载了，希望你们能越做越好，也许不知道何时，我也共同进步，再也不需要软件来改掉自己的坏习惯。

（取消自动续费可以【设置】➡️【iTunes Store与App Store】➡️点击【你的Apple ID】➡️【查看Apple ID】➡️【订阅】

先谈谈最关心的关于扣钱的问题，登录时说有免费试用+到期自动订阅全年。本着尝试一下的心态以及考虑到可以在软件内取消自动订阅就同意了。不得不说软件设计真是个人才。但这圈钱的吃相未免太难看了点吧🤮…对自家软件是有多不自信啊…

再谈谈软件本身，本来是在Siri app里看到它的。使用后的感觉就是【我为什么不去用fabulous】，内容、功能和fabulous好像哦！一定是开发者一不小心想到了一起去呢！绝对不是你想的那样哦！u1s1要能提醒我喝水我为啥不用自带的提醒事项？我以为软件能给我更多这方面的知识也好小tips也好，结果就这？我为啥不去网上搜索健康生活方式，再对着那个用Siri在自带的提醒事项里一个一个加呢？（而且你的UI设计也没好看到哪里去吧🤮）

总之，就这圈钱的态度也想从👴口袋里骗钱？哈批快给👴爪巴爪巴

title: App good, support terrible
body: I like the app functions and design - it offers exactly what I need. However, almost every update messes with my habit settings somehow (e.g. old and new habits are not showing up in daily schedule, habits stats for previous achievements are reset etc). Support team only answer emails when they want. Once, after installing another update, the app simply wouldn’t launch. I have notified the support team and got a response that they’re aware of the issue and working on it. After 5 days the problem finally got fixed and I asked whether I’ll get a refund for these 5 days because I’m paying yearly subscription - no response. Also support team keeps addressing you in emails with your last name (e.g. “Hello Smith”), although everytime I write an email I use my first name in the signature (e.g. “Thanks, John”). When I pointed that out, again, no response. I’m now waiting for another update so that the app can work properly again. My conclusion - keep developing the app, fire testers and support team.

title: Hatte mir mehr erhofft
body:
Ich nutze seit zwei Jahren solche Apps und probiere viel diesbezüglich aus, um mich besser strukturieren zu können und Routinen zu erarbeiten. Auf diese App hier wurde ich durch Werbung auf Social Media aufmerksam. 
Grundsätzlich macht die App, was sie soll. Aber herausragend finde ich sie im Vergleich zu anderen Apps des Segmentes auch nicht. 
Einen halben Punkt Punktabzug gibt es dafür, daß die „Artikel“ nicht auf Deutsch übersetzt sind (mein Englisch reicht, aber nicht jeder spricht ausreichend Englisch) und die Artikel mMn nicht über das Niveau einer Frauenzeitschrift hinausgehen. Zudem merkt man sehr, daß die Inhalte auf den amerikanischen Markt bezogen sind, womit ich grundsätzlich kein Problem habe, würde ich im Abo nicht ordentlich Geld für die App bezahlen. Da hätte ich doch gerne das Gefühl, daß man sich die Mühe macht, die Inhalte anzupassen.
Weiterer halber Punkt Punktabzug für seltsame Maßeinheiten im Tracking, wie „Cups“. Es gibt sehr unterschiedliche Tassengrößen von 100ml-Finkennäpfe bis hin zu 500ml-Pötten. Wenn ich, wie empfohlen, „11 Cups“ trinken soll, ist ergo zwischen 1100ml bis 5500ml alles drin: nicht praktikabel. 
Noch ein halber Punkt Punktabzug für den Darkmode. Grundsätzlich bin ich Fan von Darkmodes, aber irgendwie erinnert mich damit die ganze App eher an Trading Business. Sicherlich auch bedingt durch die Statistik, die angelegt wird.
Die „Challenges“, bei denen man gegen andere und gegen sich selbst antritt, sind mMn irgendwie „lieblos“ gestaltet, darum noch ein halber Punkt Abzug. Zur Persönlichkeitsentwicklung reichen mMn die spartanischen Anweisungen ohne weitergehende Erläuterungen irgendwie nicht aus.
Auch wenn es schön ist, auch mal Fortschritte zu sehen, ist die App mir insgesamt für meinen Geschmack zu nüchtern gestaltet und zu wettbewerbsorientiert. Aber das ist Geschmackssache. Andere werden genau das sicherlich mögen, darum gibt es dafür keinen Punktabzug.
Ich habe daher das Probeabo nicht verlängert und bleibe vorerst bei meiner bisherigen App, die zwar auch nicht ganz das bietet, was ich suche, aber im ähnlichen Preissegment angesiedelt, meinen Bedürfnissen doch deutlich näher kommt.

title: Bitte beheben!
body:
Sehr schöne App! Nutze sie täglich aber vor allem um zu tracken was ich erledigt habe und nicht unbedingt um mich dran zu erinnern.

Das Problem ist das wenn man irgendwas an einer Gewohnheit ändert, der gesamte Verlauf gelöscht wird. Das heißt ich kann die Gewohnheit nichtmal von „Morgens“ auf „Nachmittag“ ändern, ohne das alle Daten dazu gelöscht werden.

Habe das grade leider herausgefunden und die ganze Mühe zum tracken meines Trainings war umsonst...

Ps: Ich wünsche mir eine Statistik wo man pro Tag, Woche, Monat und Jahr sehen kann wieviel % aller Gewohnheiten man erledigt hat.
Am besten in einem Liniendiagramm.

Übrigens könnte man noch viele andere Statistiken machen z.B. Welche Gewohnheit am meisten und konstantesten abgeschlossen wurde und welche Gewohnheiten man anscheinend etwas vernachlässigt.

Würde mich sehr über so ein Update freuen!

Die Zeiteinstellung und die damit verbundene Erinnerungs-Möglichkeit könnte man im Allgemeinen auch etwas Benutzer freundlicher gestalten. Sehr viele unnötige Buttons und Wege um überhaupt etwas einzustellen.

title: Ganz Okay
body:
Die App ist einfach zu bedienen, aufgeräumt und klar.

Aber stößt schnell an Ihre Grenzen. Wer zwei Geräte nutzt, viele Gewohnheiten und eine präzise Planung des Alltags vornehmen möchte, sollte sich eine andere App suchen. 

Eine Push Synchronisation ist leider nicht enthalten. Sofern ihr also mit zwei Endgeräten arbeitet, ist die App eher unbrauchbar, da die Datenbestände unterschiedlich sind (Sync über iCloud ist funktioniert auch nicht gut!).

Zudem ist die Aufgabenplanung leider sehr unpräzise. Wollt ihr z.B. eine Aufgabe im Monat zu einem bestimmten Datum erledigen („Monatsreview“) geht dies nicht. Ihr müsst diese Aufgabe als einmalig zum Monatsende planen. Die Aufgabe wird euch dann in der letzten Woche jeden Tag als fällig angezeigt. Die Folge ihr schiebt die Aufgaben von Tag zu Tag vor euch her.

Sofern ihr also mehr Aufgaben zu erledigen habt (2x die Woche Sport,  3xLesen, 5x früh Aufstehen...), wird es schnell sehr unübersichtlich, da ihr den Montag mit gefühlt 30 Aufgaben startet. Zudem stellt sich das gewünschte „Erfolgsgefühl“ nicht ein, da ihr gewisse Aufgaben immer wieder verschieben müsst.

Die App ist m.E. dafür geeignet in einem kleinen Umfang von fünf bis maximal zehn Gewohnheiten / Aufgaben auf einem Device (Handy) zu tracken.

title: Ok mit Verbesserungspotential
body:
Pro: Intuitive Bedienung, übersichtliches, klares Design, gute Gliederung der Gewohnheiten in den Tageszeiten. Viel Auswahl an vorformulierten Gewohnheiten, die man anpassen und durch die man sich inspirieren lassen kann. Natürlich kann man auch eigene Gewohnheiten frei formulieren. 

Zumindest in der Pro-Version (7Tage-Testversion) die Möglichkeit, Notizen einzutragen, unbegrenzte Eintragungen, Hinweise auf Steigerung der Leistung oder Hinweis, sich nicht zu viel vorzunehmen; Urlaubsmodus...

Contra: 
Challenges werden automatisch als ‚nicht geschafft‘ gekennzeichnet, wenn man es versäumt, vor Mitternacht den Haken zu setzen. Das ist demotivierend und damit kontraproduktiv. 

Bei der Auswahl, wie oft man eine Gewohnheit am Tag/in der Woche ausführen will, gibt es teilweise nur eingeschränkte Möglichkeiten. ZB für laufen/Spazieren gehen nur km-Angabe statt Dauer. 

Anmeldung erfolgt automatisch, besser wäre die Möglichkeit, eine Mailadresse zur Anmeldung wählen zu können. 
Trotzdem wird die iPad-App nicht automatisch synchronisiert. Man muss alles neu eintragen.  Das ist lustig und unnötig! 

Proversion startet automatisch, so dass man nicht weiß, welche Funktionen die Basisversion bietet. Die erfährt man erst, wenn man die Proversion kündigt und dann hat man sich schon an die Features gewöhnt. Klar, das ist gewollt, aber andere Apps zeigen, dass es auch anders herum geht. 

Daher aktuell 3 Sterne von mir. Mehr gibt’s, wenn an den aufgeführten Punkten etwas verbessert wurde.

title: Kleine Ergänzungen würden die App perfekt machen
body:
Die App ist schön gestaltet und sehr intuitiv zu nutzen. Die Überspringen-Funktion ist sinnvoll und etwas, was bei einigen Wettbewerbern fehlt. Drei Dinge vermisse ich, damit die App perfekt wäre:
- Bis zum letzten Update gab es eine Möglichkeit, eine helle Oberfläche zu wähle. Diese wurde leider entfernt, die App ist also quasi immer im Dark Mode. Ein systemgesteuerter Dark Mode wäre wünschenswert. 
- Die Tageszeiten-Funktion gibt mir gar nichts. Es sollte eine Option geben, die Aufteilung nach Tageszeiten zu deaktivieren oder standardmäßig die Ansicht "alle" aufzurufen. 
- Manchmal weiß ich, dass ich eine Gewohnheit an einem Tag nicht mehr schaffen kann. Es wäre schön, diese dann als "nicht geschafft" aus der Tagesliste nehmen zu können. 
Alle diese Dinge sollten recht einfach umsetzbar sein und würden für mich einen großen Unterschied machen. Ich bin gespannt, wie sich Productive weiter entwickeln wird!

title: Mehr Flexibilität bei Regelmäßigkeit wäre toll
body:
Ich habe Productive vor längerer Zeit gekauft und schon mehrmals ausprobiert. Die App sieht gut und liebevoll gemacht aus, entwickelt sich weiter, und hat viele nette Features.

Nicht so gut gefallen mir zwei Dinge:
1) Ich wünsche mir mehr Flexibilität bei der Regelmäßigkeit von Habits. Insbesondere eine Einstellung wie „Alle X Tage“ ist für mich notwendig, da ich bei vielen Habits genau so arbeite. Da die Woche eine ungerade Anzahl von Tagen hat, kann ich keine exakten Tage definieren. Dieser Punkt hält mich davon ab, Productive aktuell zu nutzen.
2) Die App hat z.T. etwas eigenwilliges Design, z.B. ist die Schriftart nicht die Systemschriftart. Andere mag das nicht stören, mir sagt das Design insgesamt nicht ganz zu. Damit könnte ich aber leben, wenn der erste Punkt gelöst wäre.

Fazit: wirklich gelungene App und vermutlich mehr als genug für viele User, aber das Fehlen ein paar weniger essenzieller Features macht sie für mich unbrauchbar.

title: Nette App das wars
body:
An sich eine gute Idee. Sich Sachen anzugewöhnen, leider aber nur die Idee. 

Man kann viel zu wenig machen: 

-Gewohnheiten bestimmte Werte zuordnen (Buch lesen heute xy Kapitel) 
-  negative Gewohnheiten fehlen (zB rauchen aufhören) 

- man kann keine Zeiten einstellen nur Zeiträume 

- man kann sich nicht z.B. Alle 2 Wochen an einem Sonntag erinnern lassen, sondern wenn man alle 2 Wochen anklickt ist die Gewohnheit ab Montags überfällig 

- Wochen und Monatsübersicht fehlt 

- man wird am nächsten Tag nicht erinnert wenn man mal etwas vergessen hat 

- und die größte Frechheit ist mal wieder das das Abo von alleine los geht 

Man könnte ja so kundenfreundlich sein und erinnern (gerade bei einer App die Menschen benutzen um sich Sachen zu merken) 

Zudem gibt es keine Erklärung was der Unterschied zwischen dem Jahresabonnement von 11€ und 23€ ist. 

Der Entwickler antwortete hier nur mit dem selben copy paste Text. 

Hab Rezensionen von vor über einem Jahr gesehen die hilfreiche Hinweise hatten was fehlt. 

Hat sich dennoch nichts geändert. 

Allen in allem kann die App viel zu wenig um den Preis zu rechtfertigen.

title: Ein kleiner Verbesserungshinweis
body:
An sich bin ich zufrieden mit der App. Gutes Layout, intuitiv und erfüllt ihren Zweck. 

Folgendes würde ich mir wünschen: 
Wenn ich einen eine Gewohnheit nicht jeden Tag, sondern zum Beispiel alle zwei Tage erfüllen möchte, habe ich noch nicht die richtige Einstellung für mich gefunden. 
Entweder ich stelle feste Tage ein, wie Mo, Mi, Fr und einen am WE oder ich wähle aus drei/vier Mal die Woche.
Wenn ich nun einen der festen Tage verpasse, kann es sein, dass ich meine Gewohnheit nicht jeden zweiten Tag erfülle. 
Habe ich die zweite Variante gewählt, kann ich die Gewohnheit an mehreren Tagen am Anfang der Woche erfüllen und hätte meine Ruhe für den Rest der Woche. Beides bildet „jeden zweiten Tag“ nicht für mich ab. Ich würde mir eine Variante wünschen wie in der Haushalts-App Tody: Sobald ich eine Gewohnheit erfüllt habe, die ich nur alle zwei Tage erfüllen möchte, erscheint sie nach zwei Tagen wieder in meiner To-Do-Liste und verschwindet erst wieder bis ich sie erfüllt habe. So hätte man den regelmäßigen Rhythmus (alle zwei Tage), selbst wenn man einen Termin verpasst und es um einen Tag aufschieben muss.

title: Great concept, obvious faults, too expensive & shady pricing policy
body:
I really like the concept and basic functionality of this app, but I think 24€/year is an absurd price especially as the app has obvious faults. For example, it shows me days as perfect even when only part of the tasks are done and the app crashes every time I click on "Help" or "More" in the menu. At such an enormous price you would expect not just a good idea, but an app that works well and a company that cares enough to give more than generic answers to bad reviews. (Also, for that price the statistics are very limited. Many other apps include graphics of progress over time.)
I find this disappointing as there aren't many well designed habit apps and at the moment this one seems to be the only one (for IOS 10.3) where you can add as many items and have them arranged by time of day

Edit: You can change your subscription to 11,99€/year in your Apple-ID settings before the test version expires. While that makes the product less expensive, it also shows an extrem lack of transparency in their pricing policy which makes the whole business model even shadier than I thought.

body:

In der kostenlosen Variante steht dir Platz für drei verschiedene Gewohnheiten zur Verfügung. Dies empfinde ich als voellig in Ordnung und ausreichend um die App zu testen.

Wer mehr möchte muss jedoch mindestens 19.99€ im Jahres-, 6.99€ im Dreimonats- oder 3.99€ im Monatsabo bezahlen. Für eine App in der ich, platt gesagt, lediglich in einer Art To-Do-Liste erledigte Dinge abhaken kann. Und sie mir dann in einem grafischen Kalender Tage anzeigt in denen ich keine, einige oder alle meine Vorhaben geschafft habe.

Für mich deutlich zu teuer! Eine Einmalzahlung im Rahmen des Dreimonatsabos wäre fairer.

title: Grundsätzlich gut, Abo Modell ein Witz
body: Ich finde die App von ihrem Prinzip und Aufbau gut gemacht. In der Free-Version können maximal drei Gewohnheiten angelegt werden. Ich wäre gerne bereit, mir die Pro-Version für einige Euros zu kaufen, allerdings ist die Pro Version NUR im Abo-Modell erhältlich. Das heißt man zahlt Monatlich einen Betrag für die App. Das finde ich lächerlich, schließlich handelt es sich hierbei um keine App, zu dessen Nutzung große Unterhaltskosten anfallen, wie etwa die Bereitstellung großer Mengen an Serverressourcen oder Cloudspeicher. Im Gegenteil, die App funktioniert denkbar einfach. Deshalb halte ich ein Abo-Modell für die Pro-Version für absolut ungerechtfertigt und gebe zwei Sterne.

title: Nur zur Hälfte durchdacht
body:
Die App macht was sie soll; soweit so gut. Hat man mal vergessen eine Gewohnheit als erledigt einzutragen; dann bleibt es ein unperfekter Tag. Es gibt nur eine tägliche Ansicht über die anstehenden Gewohnheiten, keinen Überblick über die Woche oder den Monat. Wenn man mal was ändern will (z.B. Erinnerungen) muss man in jede Gewohnheit einzeln um dies zu ändern. Mir ist nicht ganz klar (sieht man auch nirgends) wann ich erinnert werde wenn ich „Anfang/Mitte/Ende des Monats“ eingestellt habe und wie Anfang/Mitte/Ende definiert sind. 
Layout und Bedienung sind gut, aber umständlich um die Gewohnheiten einzurichten. Da gäbe es eine einfachere Lösung um das darzustellen. Für meine Zwecke ist der Abopreis definitiv zu hoch.

title: Motivierende Art die kleinen Dinge des Tages nicht schleifen zu lassen
body:
Ich habe viele Angewohnheiten, die ich regelmäßig mache. Manche täglich, manche wöchentlich, und so weiter. Bei vielen klappt das sehr gut, aber je unbequemer die Sache wird und je weniger ich sie gerne mache, desto häufiger lasse ich sie schleifen oder mache sie gar nicht.

Diese App ist nun dafür da, diese Dinge nicht zu vergessen. Man erledigt sie, und wird durch einen Haken und eine immer höher steigende Streak belohnt, wenn man es immer wieder macht. Das alleine ist Motivation genug, um diese Dinge nicht mehr schleifen zu lassen.

Für mich die perfekte Lösung.

Die App ist sehr gut programmiert, enthält alle Features die man so braucht und ist sehr einfach und intuitiv zu bedienen.
Die kostenlose Version ist vollkommen tauglich, wenn man nur wenige Habits pflegen möchte. Die Vollversion wirkt nicht aufgezwungen, und ist vom Preis sehr akzeptabel.

Einziger Kritikpunkt ist die fehlende Synchronisation. Zwischen iPhone und iPad unmöglich, und auch ein neues Gerät geht nur über eine gestrickste Wiederherstellung.

title: Well-designed habit/goal tracking app!
body: I tried out several habit/goal tracking apps in order to find the one I liked best, and in the end I narrowed it down to two: this app (Productive) and Strides. Both have their own advantages, so deciding which one is “better” would depend on your personal preferences. Productive has nice visuals and icons that help motivate you, is simple and easy to use, allows you to sort how habits appear by times of day (so you aren’t overwhelmed by all of them at once), gives you some nice options for viewing stats, and allows for some customisation. If you want to add more than 5 habits though you’ll need to upgrade, but the upgrade is not too expensive. So if you’re looking for something visually appealing, simple, intuitive and more day/time of day focussed, Productive is perfect.

title: Controversial
body:
I wave a subscription for some time now.
App has nice UI, simple functionality covering basic habit tracking needs, with some nice features.

What I don’t like: Developer focusing a lot on changing or improving UI, occasionally introducing critical bugs like habits become duplicated or some habits don’t show up at all after app update.
I would rather see more stable app, better habit statistics, habit editing without loosing all starts.
My point: I would rather see less UI changes, but making essential functionality work better.

Fortunately the reminder to buy it does not show up anymore every time I complete habits for a day. But now I see Hooray message like I am 5 years old. I actually want to leave the app and the only thing that keeps me is the almost three years of history.

title: Timer
body:
I love the app and I am a paying user. However , despite many messages to customer suppport for now several years the timer doesn’t work properly. 
For example if I am timing a task on my phone and at the same time I am making a phone call to complete the task , the timer stops working. 
Basically as soon as I get out of the app the timer stops. Which defeats the purpose of the timer because I can’t keep my phone open , on the app , while I am completing a one hour task. I need to use my phone . 

So I have to use my phone’s timer. It is very frustrating to pay for a task management app, and having to use another system to time.

I mean how difficult can it be to fix a timer?  I am sure a first year computer science student can do an app with a timer that works properly.

title: Good starting point. Needs polishing however
body:
iOS 13.6
Premium user

*Good point the numerous predefined choices of habits to choose from: gives plenty of ideas 💡 

*Several usability issues (THE thing to improve IMHO):
-difficult sometimes to know in what day/date I am in at a given time, or if I am seeing the morning/evening/all habits (I need to check this often)
-weird behaviors: when modifying the habit repetition frequency (for example, one day in the week for another), or the reminder hour, it happens to “ignore” the changes. After several try-and-fails, I finally manage to set the desired configuration
-if a habit comprises 3 or more actions , shouldn’t it appear since then as “omitted” just after the first action? (Even though not finished, we did not “skip” it)
-why habit calendars, graphs,... are not in the same colour previously set in the habit “theme”?

*Will we be able sometime soon to define OUR own challenges or to have them predefined such as e.g. read 2 books in 3 weeks, learn 100 words of a foreign language in a weekend, run 100km in a month,..

*The app rate button doesn’t work (so one has to go manually to the iOS shop)

* The app version release notes (in the iOS shop) are useless since they don’t describe what changes or improvements have been made or are going to be made

I really hope to see improvements in these issues in the weeks to come and even update my review in that sense (I take for granted that this is possible). Given the price of this app I feel a bit disappointed so far.

title: Excelente diseño, funcionalidades no tanto
body:
La app es buena, con un diseño fantástico, pero bastante mejorable a nivel de funcionalidades.

Ejemplo, una vez alcanzas el objetivo semanal, desaparece del día siguiente. Si lo amplias y no llegas, aparece “vencido”. 

Por otro lado, solo puedes editar los resultados 7 días atrás y si añades un nuevo hábito no puedes poner que lo hiciste ya antes, te obliga a empezar ese día.

Es por este motivo que finalmente he decidido pasarme a la app Strides, a pesar de tener la app Productive de pago.

Si buscas una interficie bonita y la posibilidad de usar contadores, entonces la mejor app es Productive.

 Si te importa más la funcionalidad de la app, entonces es mejor Strides.

title: Le faltan cosas
body: Cambio mi reseña después de tiempo usándola. La idea está genial pero le falta desarrollo. No puedes ver lo planeado para otros días. Hay muy pocas opciones para las tareas. Debería haber una opción para repetir la tarea empezando a contar el tiempo una vez finalizada. Si no todas las tareas empiezan los lunes o los días 1 del mes. Y eso es un agobio! Una vez hecha deberia pasar el tiempo de repetición y volver a aparecer. Si no, la haces a final de mes y a los pocos días ya la tienes otra vez en la lista, cuando la acabas de hacer. Muy mal pensado..   para el orden de las tareas hay que entrar en ajustes, cosa que es muy tediosa. Y en esa lista no puedes modificarlas, solo ordenarlas. Para modificarlas es en otro sitio. Vamos, muy complicado y engorroso. Que lo arreglen!!  No hay un buscador rápido parar encontrar las tareas. Tienes que buscarlas por la tediosa lista que no está en el mismo orden sino en orden alfabético, y no se puede cambiar. Más opciones! 20 euros al año deberían mejorar muchas cosas. Me molesta mucho la crucecita esa de vencido. Debería ser opcional. Por último, sería muy útil poder ver todas las tareas que tienes de un color, o todas las que se repiten semanalmente, mensualmente, etc porque en la lista no lo pone y hay que ir entrando en cada tarea para acordarte de los detalles.

title: Queda mucho por hacer!
body:
Esta aplicación es muy útil para el teléfono, Pero de momento...queda mucho por hacer en la sincronización con el Apple Watch. 
En el Apple Watch recibes los recordatorios lo cual está muy bien!! pero cuando quieres darle a completado ( en una tarea determinada )no se eliminan de la lista o Aparece como que no tienes tareas ese día, Siendo necesario coger el móvil para dar a esas tareas como completadas o poder ver qué tareas tienes.
 Conclusión :en el Apple Watch solo recibirás las notificaciones de que has de hacer una determinada tarea, Pero por problemas de sincronización, no podrás ver cuantas tareas tienes o darle a completadas pues no se borrarán de la lista. 
En tres ocasiones he mandado un mensaje informando de este problema y los tres he recibido la misma respuesta de un robot en el que se me da las gracias por informar y me dice que intentarán mejorarlo.
NO SE OS OCURRA HACEROS PREMIUM O OS ARREPENTÍS COMO YO!
A no ser que mejoren la sincronización con el Apple Watch lo cual la aplicación será excelente! Descargue la aplicación por el Apple Watch Y en lo que falla esta aplicación es en la sincronización con el mismo, por lo tanto no lo aconsejo.

title: Très complet mais pas parfait
body: J’ai testé un peu moins de 10 apps de routines et clairement elle est vraiment bien conçue pour à la fois être visuelle et ergonomique dans la gestion et le suivi des routines. Seul bémol selon moi est le manque de quelques features comme : une visualisation des progrès avec une vue sur l’année, la possibilité de choisir des jours spécifiques de la semaine (comme le week end) pour les routines « dans la semaine » ce qui permettrai de moins polluer les listes de routines des jours non concernés. J’aime beaucoup le principe des badges qui sollicitent le circuit de la récompense. Pour le widget qui indique le nombre de routine du jour, un petit plus serait d’y afficher le nombre complèté sur le nombre total pour y voir notre progression sans ouvrir l’app. Je note la version premium, pas que la version gratuite. Elle vaut son prix selon moi, surtout si les devs restent à l’écoute de la communauté.

title: APP NULLE JE NE RECOMMANDE ABSOLUMENT PAS
body:
1- App qui ne sert à rien sans le forfait payant (7,49/mois ou 35,99/an) et personnellement après l’ajout de 5 routines toutes celles que je voudrais ajouter par la suite sont payantes. Je trouve que le prix demandé est EXORBITANT je comprends que les créateurs doivent être rémunérés mais s’ils veulent que ça marche il faudrait sérieusement envisager une baisse du prix annuel et mensuel car cette app revient juste à faire une to-do list sur une feuille de papier. 

2-Trop de publicité. Rien que le fait que je change d’onglet exemple de « défis» à «statistiques» il y a une pub de 30sec-1min je tiens à dire que si le principe de l’app est de nous rendre plus productif/ive il serai bien de ne pas nous faire perdre notre temps 

3- Traduction française nulle a ch*er exemple pour l’habitude boire de l’eau dans la description " boire de l’eau TE hydrate" 

Ouille ouille ouille j’ai mal à la France. 

4- C’est dommage car il n’y a pas la possibilité de créer une habitude. 

5- l’onglet "découvrir" n’est disponible qu’en anglais c’est dommage car je suis sure que ça permettrai à améliorer la productivité de plein de monde en plus des anglais/américain en traduisant en plusieurs langues 

6- Je ne trouve pas ça très gai un arrière fond sombre, pas très encourageant. 

7- Mettre plus d’option comme celle du minuteur lorsqu’on «se brosse les dents» dans par exemple celle de «se lever tôt »en mettant un réveil.

body:

Français:
Visiblement l’abonnement de cette application est vraiment trop cher.
J’ai donc essayé Habitminder et c’est une super trouvaille. J’adore le widget facile d’accès, on peut mettre à jour nos Habits depuis le widget. 
Et bien sur celle-ci est trois fois moins cher que votre application.
Mais ce qui m’a vraiment poussé à ne pas utiliser votre application, c’est le fait que, quand on décide d’annuler son abonnement est bien là par magie on vous propose 70 % de réduction. title: Arnaque
body:
J’ai acheté l’application il y a 1 an pour 19€ J’imagine qu’entre temps les créateur on du se rendre compte que c’était plus rentable en changeant de business modèle cette fois-ci sous forme d’abonnement. C’est toujours mieux quand les utilisateurs doivent payer quotidiennement pas vrai ? Ils ne ce sont pas gêné non plus pour passer l’abonnement à l’année a plus de 30€. D’après moi c’est une très bonne application mais conçu par des escrocs plus intéressés par la quantité d’argent qu’ils peuvent soutirer au gens qu’autre chose. De plus la qualité du service n’est pas en adéquation avec qualité du service fournis. 
Cela reste mon humble avis pour ce qu’il vaux, je vous laisse vous faire le vôtre.

title: Bonne idée
body:
L’idée est bonne, mais l’appli est pas assez abouti. Je trouve que c’est excessivement chère je ne vois pas pourquoi il faut payer une trentaine d’euros pour ça, s’il y avait du contenu mis à jour régulièrement pourquoi pas et encore. Pour ça, ça devrait être un paiement unique et surtout pas à 30 euros.

Ma réponse au développeur :
Pardon mais je ne vois pas bien le rapport entre le prix et le fait de garder un lien avec les abonnés. Quand je vois que sur la moitié des commentaires les gens disent que c’est cher pour ce que c’est, c’est bien que vous ne prenez pas en compte vos abonnés et que les gens ont juste le sentiment que le rapport qualité prix n’y ai pas. 
Je suis abonnée à appli, mais contrairement à vous il y a du contenu chaque semaine et je sais pourquoi je paye et ils sont loin de faire raquer 30 euros à leur abonnés et sont à moins de 10 euros par mois tout en ayant un contact sur les réseaux avec leur communauté. 
Donc vous avez encore du travail à faire, avant de justifier votre prix en disant que c’est pour garder un lien avec vos abonnés. Trouvez un autre argument l’apat du gain plutôt, mais pas celui là.

title: Rapport qualité prix très moyen
body:
Le design est certes intéressant, mais je trouve l’ergonomie effarante. Les animations sont longues, ça bouge dans tous les sens. La mise en place des habitudes est laborieuse, et il faut jongler entre l’ajout (slide vers le bas puis 2 pages) et la modification de position (menu, orga, matin, puis drag). C’est hyper compliqué !
Le design est minimaliste, mais parvient finalement à être chargé tout en affichant peu d’informations sur un seul écran (iPhone SE).
Enfin, pour ce prix, j’aurais espéré une version Mac et iPad pour accompagner. 
Bref, non satisfait en l’état.

title: Free trial isn't free after all
body:
I genuinely wanted to try this app with the intention of an annual subscription if I found it usefull on a daily basis. Ratings and comments were good so I decided to trust the process.

During the free trial I found it easy to set up tasks and mark off as complete. You can use tasks and challenges already set up or create your own. I got excited when I spotted you could set up alerts and reminders and tag habits to habits. 

Unfortunately the alerts never worked for me and the app didn't support my personal requirements. I'm sure it will be great for others and paying one of the many subscriptions wont be a problem for them.

I cancelled my subscription following the guidance, giving 48 hours notice (24 more than required) before the payed subscription commenced. However I seemed to have been charged £5 and twice. The in app payment details are really cryptic and my bank is unable to identify where they came from. I know its this app and company as it was the only apple in app subscription within my apple settings. 

Don't bother with the trial unless you are happy pay something for a few days use initially.

title: The app is excellent but the customer support is robotic
body:
This is honestly a great app. Well worth paying for. It works brilliantly 99% of the time. How when it doesn’t work customer support is not great. I’ve had a couple of problems with it and the first response is always to ask for screenshots, then when I provide them I get “this is a known issue”. To be fair these issues do usually get resolved in the frequent updates. But it’s not very supportive. Recently I noticed they’ve got two subscriptions for me, so I emailed to ask about that. First I got about 1000 word email saying they were sorry I was leaving and to always contact support in the first instance - which is what I did! Then when I emailed again I got the “this is a known issue” response. It feels as though they’ve contracted out to a robot, I’ve lost faith in my ability to actually raise a question and get it sorted. I still think the apps great and hope that I’ll remain subscribed (once only) but I wish they’d train their customer support robots to answer questions.

Updated review 2024:
Customer support is now nonexistent. I have emailed several times only to get an automated response to check the FAQ for help. I’m dropping my review down to 3 stars from an original 5. The devs seem to have abandoned this.

title: Could be brilliant app but fundamentally flawed.
body:
Bad flaws. Poor customer service. And they haven’t addressed things people have raised here over 4 years ago. Too expensive for an app they don’t update or listen to users about. 

This would easily be a five star because when I first got this app I wowed so much as I went through the features and aesthetics that I thought it was perfect. But it’s missing a few things that mean I’m not going to subscribe. 1: I wanted to move other apps data here. I’ve been not drinking for 70 days and I wanted to add that streak but you can’t go back and add data to past days. Also if I accidentally miss a day or press something wrong and only see it the next day, I can’t add it. Essentially chains can easily be destroyed by little mistakes and all that motivation and effort in recording it lost. 2: I wanted to use the fast timer which lasts 22 hours for me. But it’s sooo silly that you can’t record two timers at once. And if I close the app totally the timer goes and a missed fast is recorded. If I want to continue my reading timer the fast timer goes off. Meaning the timer there is useless taking away my initial joy at how seamlessly designed this app is. 3: it does silly things like sometimes saying I skipped a day when I haven’t and this is demotivating. It also shouldn’t say a day has been skipped when your aim is 4/7 days a week for something. Maybe say that at the end of the week but not when you don’t intend to do it every day on the first place. 4: you can undo something which is great but only sometimes. It seems properly closing the app and reopening it makes it impossible to press undo. I had to remake new goals a few times in the first day to clear a skipped task I didn’t skip or something that was wrong. And when I changed things it said all history will be wiped. Meaning in future when it messes up I will lose all history and all that pride at my effort and the data I want to collect essentially for tracking my mental and physical health. So yeah lots of potential but I won’t be paying for this app yet. I’ll look for something cheaper or free that works better still.

title: It’s good but a few things I would change
body: I like this app. The interface is more visual and a lot cleaner and less cluttered than other similar apps. I have ADHD so this is helpful to me. There is one thing I can’t do in Productive that I would like to be able to do. I wish there was like a general task list area where I could dump all the tasks that are in my head but without setting a day or time on them yet. Like I know I need to create a dedicated area in my house for stretching but I don’t want to commit to doing that today for example or on a specific date. I just want it in a general list so I can free up space in my head but just have it in a general area until I’m ready to schedule it. I also wish I could create my own challenges rather than having to pick ones others are doing. With the challenges I also wish you could see what they actually entail before committing to them. Like with the bed time routine challenge - it turns out it’s just getting your clothes ready the night before. I don’t need that challenge as I wear the same thing every day. But I only found out that’s what the challenge entailed after I signed up. It’s easy enough to delete the challenge but that’s after I’ve wasted minutes signing up to it. Thats the opposite of productive. Other than that I really like the app. I wish it was more brightly coloured as I think it would help encourage me to access the app more (but that’s the dopamine junkie talking probably).

title: ⚠️ NOT compatible with iPad
body:
This is a great productivity app, there’s no doubt about it, and I use it daily on my iPhone.

However, my work role has changed, & I’m using my iPad more, but despite the advertising;
⚠️ this app is NOT integrated between your iPhone & iPad. ⚠️
Sure you can download the app on your iPhone & iPad (as advertised), but they are “2 separate apps”. 
Why the developer has chosen to mislead us before handing over our cash, and have the only app in the store that is absolutely useless being effectively a separate app on each device, is frankly ‘Bizarre’, and just lazy to not add that extra line of code, which really is that straightforward.

The potential is here to make something that is ‘great’, “Amazing”! But, it’s more about that feeling, that they have my hard earned money now, and I feel VERY disrespected. 

As a small business owner, I always think twice before leaving a negative review, and try give the benefit of doubt. But I am annoyed, & you would be too, if I didn’t inform you properly.
Because these guys clearly don’t!

title: Needs Work!
body:
Used to be a great app - but it got lost. 

The developers are too focused on the animation/graphics and making it look pretty than addressing the core functionality of how the app improves people’s lives or listening to their users. 

It’s not agile enough to reinforce creating good habits and can dishearten your progress entirely. Why should you loose your 300 day streak of Yoga and start from 0 if you forgot to take your Vitamins one day? 🤨 

There is a plethora of user reviews asking for the same functionality to be addressed and I myself have emailed the developers twice in the last 2 years. 

What did we get instead?...A new Christmas update where the background has Christmas Trees 🙄👍

The “Widget” continues the trend - a tiny single number of habits - with three quarters of the widget displaying a graphic of a hill and tree? 🤨 Surely that space could be utilized for analytics a little more...I don’t know...Productive!?

Finally - both the watch & phone app need to be streamlined, completing a habit should take 1 tap - not 4 swipes & 2 taps. 

After 2 years of waiting for it to redeem itself - I finally jumped ship to the Streaks app and wow! It’s so much better. Simple, intuitive, slick, agile, great app for watch & phone, the widget is productive and beautiful and it talks to Apple health so I don’t need to tap anything at all. It’s what I hoped this app could be. All for a small one off fee instead of a subscription model. 

I’m very sorry guys - I hate to give negative criticism. But I have to say and tell it how it is 🤷‍♂️

title: App repaired, trust destroyed
body:
I’ve been a subscriber of Productive since the very beginning. It was my go-to app for structuring and tracking my days. I had it open all day long. I depended on it, I was measurably less productive without it. 

Until that update earlier this month where the app would just not start. The developers confirmed they were aware of the issue. It still took almost 2 weeks to provide a fix. That’s way too long for a critical app like this. Imagine WhatsApp or your email shutting down for 2 weeks.

While the app wasn’t available, I rebuild my habits structure in Google Sheets. It’s flexible, syncs across multiple devices and - first and foremost - unlikely to shut down for weeks.

This is it. Thanks to Productive for the, well, productive years together, but now it’s time to separate. So long!

title: Generally great, need some improvements
body:
I’ve been using your app and it is an amazing app to help me track my habits. Really keep me in good productive mode. 

There are a couple of suggestions I saw other users also suggested, would be super helpful if your team can work on it: 

1. Can it keep previous checkin record after upgrading/updating the habit? I’ve been keeping good records for a few weeks and want to raise frequency and then all previous records have gone. This is very unhelpful that I lose all records. 
To keep previous record would be helpful when review periodically and analysis the behaviour. 

Perhaps if I keep habit paused but would that impact to avoid me get perfect day? Or could archive habit to keep records; then We’ll have to raise new habit with high frequency instead as interim. 

2. Can the habit still be the option to check in after I completed the week goal?  Eg: I set up “listen to radio” three times a week, I completed on Thus, but I also actually keep listening radio on FRI - Sun, would be good to leave check in option open so I can choose check in FRI-SUN.

title: Update is terrible
body:
Ever since I started with this app, in Jan 2018, the stats don’t work. When you delete or reset a habit, it removes your perfect day from the day you started the habit. But that’s not a huge issue for me.
I’ve had problems since then with the app crashing after some updates. But it’s a useful app and the crashing was fixed so I kept using it.
The new update to version 2.0.0 is dreadful. I opened it this morning. Rather than having morning, afternoon, evening and all day tasks in one list like before, I now have to scroll sideways from morning list to all day. And since it is the morning, it opens the app to the morning list, not the all day list, even though the morning list is empty (I set all my habits to be all day). The list of habits is now a smaller part of my screen so I can’t see as many on the screen at once. It also decided that all the weekly tasks for this week hadn’t been done, even though I did them on Monday (writing this on Saturday) and that I needed all my weekly tasks to have notifications (previously weekly tasks didn’t show notifications until sunday when it is my last day to do them). The update is frustrating to the point that I erased my entire phone so I could restore to a backup with the old version of this app. I’m either never updating this app again or I’m finding a different productivity app. Yes the update looks nice, but the thing that attracted me to this app over other to-do list apps was that it was simple. Complicated lists distract from being productive. And the update has just complicated things.
Two stars instead of one because the pre-update version is pretty good and useful.

title: Extremely helpful!
body: For a long time I had been aware of my habits, especially the bad ones. The same old habits that keep you stuck in the same old cycles and patterns in life. However the nature of habit is of course to do things on autopilot, and you only become aware of what you’ve been doing after it’s been done, and then get annoyed with yourself. I would always make strong intentions to create new habits and change old ones, but I would simply forget 5 minutes later after doing something routine, and therefore slipping into old habit patterns. I haven’t been using this app for long time as of yet, however already the reminders give me the nudge I need to take action and pull me out of my normal autopilot state. Each day once I have completed all of the habits I have set myself, I feel a great sense of accomplishment, and a renewed self-esteem. Big changes in life start with the first small step, and becoming more aware of self sabotaging habits is the first step. I really do love this app, and I would recommend it to anyone who wants to start reprogramming their habits! Thank you!

title: Not sure what I’m paying for
body:
I’m a developer. I understand the importance of recurring revenue for software so I was understanding that a todo app wanted a monthly payment. I know keeping an app working at all takes work, nevermind constantly updating things to work with all the new features Apple keep adding to their platform.

So with all that said: what am I paying for, here, exactly?

The app is getting more buggy over time, not less.

Apple added actions to notifications and the app followed suit but they don’t work - checking off an item via the notification does nothing! That’s several streaks broken right there for me.

Apple made the Apple Watch and Productive added an Apple Watch app... which also doesn’t work! Checking items off on the Watch doesn’t check them off in the app. Yet more broken streaks for me.

Oh, and now the app hung while I was swiping a task to complete it and now crashes immediately on launch, and I can no longer use it at all. Regrettably my journey with this app has to end there, even though in principle I was happy with it, its featureset, and the price. What a shame to make such a lovely app and fail because of bugs.

I was so pleased at the way I easily adapted to this app, that I simply had to ‘promote’ to the upgraded version. title: Great potential
body:
I am disappointed with this app, after paying for a subscription it doesn’t work in the way I want. I contacted support ages ago who were helpful but ultimately couldn’t help and it’s not been updated since.

I’d like my habits to be set up as a minimum number of times a week. For example one yoga session a week as a minimum. The problem is sometimes I might do two or three, but the app no longer allows you to continue tracking habits once you’ve reached the goal. I found a hack around it by using Siri shortcuts to trigger the habit which then adds it to the counter, but seems very weird you can’t do this manually. 

Also if you change any of the goals the stats will totally disappear. Going by what I said above I’d like to start with my goal of yoga once a week, start small. Once I’ve mastered that I want to increase it to twice a week. Now all the stats are totally reset, which is silly as you’re only increasing the target. I can’t imagine this use case is that weird? I would find setting a higher target and failing every week demotivating.

I love the interface and general feel of the app, I think it just needs to have some more comprehensive customisation. I understand that simplicity is a selling point, but there could be some advanced options for power users. 

Would love to know if these features are on your roadmap, I’ve gone back to a good old fashioned paper chart which works for me.
