title: I do like this app
body:
It’s easy to use, easy to understand. However, it is far from perfect: 

* The “free” version needs to allow more than 3 habits. How can you accurately gauge if you like the app when you can only list 3 items?
* You should be able to set days for your habits. At the moment, even with premium, I can’t see a way of setting a specific habit for a specific day, only a time of day. Which is no use. Being able to set habits further in advance would be good, like dentist appointments. 
* Daily and weekly to do lists would also be very helpful and would make the app more competitive against apps such as Habitica. 
* It should be easy to see what habits you currently have listed. I had several listed multiple times and I can’t work out how to see what habits I’ve already got. 
* It’s expensive! £20 a year?? Once the trial is over I’ll most likely be cancelling due to the above. Why would I pay a yearly subscription when I can get the same somewhere else for free or cheaper? Either a £20 one off price or a MUCH lower yearly cost would be better
* I’ve tried it several times over the last couple of years and there just doesn’t seem to be any changes. Almost like the developers aren’t really changing or improving anything or listening to what their customers are saying and for £20 a year, I’d want to see a LOT of upgrades and changes.

title: Updating to Premium
body:
There’s a lot that this app does do: it’s immaculate, easy to use & an absolutely great concept.  I struggle with making myself keep ontop of routine because in my job, it’s constantly changing.

However - I would recommend allowing a few more habits to be created without updating to premium. There’s no way I can try the app out properly with only three habits. I need more than that to get through the week! & because the ‘subscription continues until cancelled’ I do not trust myself to take a free trial - those of us with busy enough lives to warrant having a to-do app probably don’t remember trivial things like cancelling an app subscription! I might consider allowing a few more habits to be made on the free version OR setting up a cancellation feature. 

Also, this app would be absolutely fantastic if you had a simple to-do list feature also - somewhere to write one-off tasks as well as keep on top of things you repeat regularly.  Just something to consider (would be absolutely unparalleled if this existed).

I like to have no reminders so it’s not about not being reminded, it’s about having the power to update your habits as you go along or even exceed your habit targets whenever you want/ feel like it. title: An organised day!
body: I had previously used this developer's app 'Balanced' which also allows you to set up tasks and mark them as completed but in a more fluid way: you are just aiming to maintain a high percentage of completed tasks and the most urgent items to be done rise to the top of the list. I liked the app but found it a bit disorganised: if I didn't tick off the workout I did in the morning until the afternoon, then it wouldn't have priority again until the next afternoon. With 'Productive' you start by grouping your tasks into 'morning', 'afternoon' or 'evening' and they always show up at the right time, no matter what time you mark them as complete. This works much better for me and it is highly motivating to try to get that nice bright solid dot for a 'perfect' day!

title: Very good, simple habit-building app
body: A very well-made little app, and I appreciate the fact that the free version allows you to properly try out the app by tracking five habits before buying. I've docked one star firstly because I felt it was a little expensive for quite a simple app (especially as I really like its companion app "Balanced" as well, but don't want to fork out £6 for the pair), and secondly because there's some scope for development: for example, I was disappointed that completing a "perfect day" wasn't rewarded. How about an element of gamification to encourage habit-building? Even just a message saying "Congrats, a perfect day!", with increasingly enthusiastic messages if you string together a few perfect days in a row! These are just fairly minor suggestions for improvement, however: if you're looking for a solid, well-made habit-building app, I would certainly recommend this one.

title: Excellent habit app
body:
I had been using a tasks app (Things) to create recurring tasks before buying this. I have no complaints about that app. It is just that when you start your day with a dozen or so recurring tasks it really clutters up your task list. (Yes, I know that's what tags and categories are for, but sorting them every day??) 

I like a short and manageable task list. Moving all the daily stuff to a separate app just made sense for me. This app gets around the clutter in an excellent manner. This means that nothing daily and mundane is missed and my main tasks app reminds me of ongoing projects, business and non-recurrent stuff.

If you have a lot of recurring tasks, or are trying to change your habitual patterns then look no further than this app. Brilliant!

title: Surprisingly great
body:
As a 19 year old working student with so many things to think about & do in life it can all get to your head causing you to WANT to create new habits and be productive, however consistently failing to do so, you can find yourself in this scenario at any age & I can honestly say this app has helped allot.
Things such as mindful thinking, stretching, getting to sleep by 11pm, drinking more water, reading, working out, have all been made attainable by simply having this very neat schedule, complete at your own pace with no set time! I think its great as not actually setting a specific time and just a 'morning' 'afternoon' or 'evening' time gives you the flexibility and freedom to get it done without it feeling like a task. It makes habits seemingly ease into your life.
I would seriously recommend spending the extra £2.99 to upgrade as I did, even though I never spend cash in the app store aha. 
I hope this review convinces someone else to download because the app really does work in this surprising way :)

title: Good app but has things to be improved
body:
I've been using the app for a few months now and it's really cool to be able to track habits. I have the paid version and it works fine.

The only problem is if you want to edit a habit you lose all your data. So you basically can't change anything in your routine. That's an issue cause during our lives we do need to readjust habits sometimes. 

For example, I used to practice ukulele Monday to Friday, now I want to do it only at weekends cause I'm working on a new project. If I change it on the app, I will lose all the previous data. It's really annoying and I don't know what to do. 

Would also be great if you could add something that you don't usually do everyday, but you did that day. Example: I usually don't go to the gym at weekends, but this Saturday I decided to go. I can't add it to the app, so I can't tack that activity.

title: Best of all habit-tracking apps
body:
Productive is an elegant software that (finally) brings all of the best features of the different habit apps out there with its own flavour.

It has the simplicity and streak tracking capacity of Streaks.

It has the personality and self-care concerns of Fabulous (without the aggressive pricing practices)

It allows you to group habits by time of day, to schedule them in many ways and to track an habit multiple times a day. 

It has a pretty complete notification system.

It has timed/pomodoro type habits that can be paused and resumed at any time.

It’s overall pretty outstanding.

It also has an essential feature to me that many other habits app lack and unfortunately it’s its weakest piece: the Apple Watch app.

It gets the job done and allows you to check habits but it’s not at the same level with the rest of the app. 
Its Complications are not very useful, as the small ones don’t indicate any progress. 
It’s not possible to start a timed habit from the watch and the experience of using the app itself is a bit bland. There’s no sound feedback when you complete an app,  any animations to make things a bit more slick or any icons accompanying the habits. 

I think this is the aspect where Productive has the most room for improvement and they could learn a bit from Tangerine or Streaks.

But I still think it’s an unbelievable app, much better than the competition and I’m supporting the developer with my subscription hoping they will consider this feedback.

title: Molto carina
body:
È un app ben fatto dal punto di vista grafico e molto intuitiva da usare. Le quattro stelle sono perché non c’è la sincronizzazione tra dispositivi e questa è un’enorme pecca. Spero questa cosa venga sistemata a breve.
Per tutte quelle persone che si lamentano essere a pagamento:
- primo, non è obbligatorio, basta recedere e poi c’è la versione gratuita;
- secondo, vi danno fastidio le pubblicità? Allora pagate. A voi piacerebbe lavorare senza essere pagati? Non credo proprio. Se fosse facile creare applicazioni di questo tipo allora ve le stareste creando da soli. Quindi smettetela di fare i bambini viziati. Anche perché sono 35€ all’anno, circa 3€ al mese, ossia due caffè (addirittura con le offerte a volte costa anche meno di 20€ all’anno). Non vi sta bene, imparate a programmare e fatevela da soli.

title: Grossa occasione persa
body: È incredibile come la voglia di guadagnare scavalchi enormemente la voglia di aiutare o dare valore alle persone. Qesto è un servizio che ad oggi troviamo anche gratuitamente senza problemi negli store. Sta andando di moda la voglia di monitorare le proprie abitudini. Questa app è fatta davvero bene, caspita complimenti super meritati. Lo ritengo uno spreco enorme però perchè un app così ben fatta non ha bisogno di abbonati altopaganti, guadagnereste già abbastanza con il numero di registrati e sicuramente fare una versione gratis e una versione Pro a pagamento sarebbe una buona soluzione. Alla fine avete creato questa app per fare soldi e non per portare valore alla comunità, dove il guadagno poi lo avreste avuto ugualmente… mi spiace perchè è un programma molto ben fatto. Metterei da parte il soldo veloce, è molto più remunerativa la credibilità e il valore che portate sul mercato. La gente pagherebbe comunque per una versione pro. Ma così vi state bruciando una sfilza di clienti. Detto ciò spero risolviate il sistema. Così è un vero spreco e peccato.

title: Provate questa applicazione!
body: Sicuramente un app molto utile, devo dire che tra tutte quelle che ho potuto provare per organizzarmi questa è sicuramente la più piacevole. Essa è molto intuitiva e grazie alla sua semplice interfaccia, richiede poco tempo per imparare ad usarla. Tuttavia dopo averla usata per diversi mesi mi sono accorto di una cosa, ovvero il fatto che effettivamente  rispetto ad un’app basica come può essere promemoria di Apple cambia ben poco. Mi spiego meglio; le uniche cose che variano sono l’interfaccia (ovvero il modo in cui viene presentata) e le diverse e molto strette limitazioni per la versione non a pagamento. Non sono qui a scrivere per sminuire l’applicazione però vorrei far notare una cosa, ovvero il fatto che immagino la maggior parte delle persone che la vorrà utilizzare non deciderà di utilizzare il lato a pagamento, quindi per questo perché non utilizzare semplicemente l app promemoria di iPhone essa certo non ha un’interfaccia altrettanto colorata, ma effettivamente offre davvero molta più libertà rispetto a questa alternativa la quale in sostanza è semplicemente un app per promemoria. Detto questo per chi è giunto fino a questo punto vorrei dire in conclusione di scaricarla e provarla, perché secondo me merita davvero per la sua qualità generale.

title: Molto utile e piacevole (+consiglio)
body:
L’ho usata per 1 anno con abbonamento, per ora uso la versione free, comunque molto valida.
Rifarai l’abbonamento volentieri se ci fosse alcuni upgrade:
- migliorare la geolocalizzazione
- implementare la possibilità di dare un “voto” al completamento (oltre a segnalare se l’hai fatta o meno, segnalare anche COME, inteso con un punteggio numerico o una valutazione tipo bene/normale/male).
- statistiche e reportistica migliorati

Per il reato la consiglio moltissimo, si usa in modo facile e, se usata a supporto di una giusta mentalità, é una bomba a (quasi) qualsiasi età, anche già nella versione free.

Difetto decisamente noioso: non c’è lo swipe da sinistra verso destra per tornare indietro, bisogna cliccare in alto a sinistra sul pulsante “indietro”, ho un iPhone X e lo schermo alto rende questa pecca ancora più noiosa.

È da poco che uso l’app e molto probabilmente mi abbonerò.
Tuttavia metto una stella per il costo e per il fatto che fate pagare con un abbonamento.. ridicolo e insensato.

Sono uno sviluppatore, quasi quasi ne faccio una identica ma a minor prezzo, sarei curioso di vedere che succede.

title: 結局課金したので
body:
トライアルからキャンセルできず、仕方ないので課金して一年間使ってみます。

私は怪我の功名になればと前向きに捉えましたが、一般的には不快感を招く仕様だと思うのでやめた方が良いとは思います…

使い始めてみて、やはりデザインは良いと思います。まめに目にするものはデザインが良くないとキツいので。

すぐに感じた改善希望点としては、
1:タスクの並べ替え
2:タスクに付随できるメモ機能
3:タスクを前倒し消化した際の対応 
4:『二週間毎』等の設定が謎   の４点です。

1:  一日を３分割で表示しているので、
消化していく順番がランダムに表示されているのはとても不便です。

朝のルーティンなどを習慣化したい場合、細かなタスクが沢山あります。効率の良い消化順に並んでいれば、通知を待たずに消化していけるので、流れを身につけ易いと思います。

2:  タスクはタイトルだけの登録なので、細かなタスクがまとまっているような場合、具体的には何と何と何をどの順番でやるのかなどのメモが書けるととても助かります。

例えば『リビングの掃除』というタスクを作っても、出ているものを片す→埃拭き→掃除機がけ…など細かなタスクのまとまりである場合も多く、習慣化出来ていないものほど「えっと何からやるんだっけ？」というところで止まってしまうので、いちいち考えなくても済むように是非メモ機能を追加していただきたいです。

3:  今朝も『６時起床』と登録しながら５時５０分に目覚めてしまい、なんとなく通知が気になって６時まで待ってしまいました…
チェックを入れることで完了した感が得られるため、事前に消化出来ているものは、その都度消していけると有り難いです。

4:  まだ使い方がわかっていないだけかもしれませんが『隔週水曜日の朝』などの設定が出来ませんでした。日本語表示の誤りもあり、わかりやすく改善していただければと思います。

長くなりましたが、ここに書いたことは既に他のレビューでも書かれていることばかりです。以上の点が改善されれば継続課金でもお安い投資と感じましたので、是非とも改善のご検討をお願いいたします！

-------------------------------

追加いたします。
使用２日目の夜から動作の不具合が発生しています。

リストの入れ替えができないとほとんど使い物にならないことがわかったので、すべて削除して順番通りに登録し直そうと思いましたが、途中から全く削除できなくなりました。

リストの削除だけでなくデータの削除も出来ません。

更に、完了したタスクもチェックは入れられますが消えずにずっと残ったままになっています。

一晩経過しましたが状況は変わっていません。

一番大事なやる気が萎えてしまいます。
レビューも反映されていないようですし、とても残念な気持ちです。。

良いところも沢山あるので、余計に勿体なく感じます。

早急にご対応いただきたいです。

わざわざウィジェットから習慣を追加できる機能は使う想定がないので不要かと思います。

新しいチャレンジの提案機能が個人的にとても好きです。
この機能のために課金をしている割合が高いくらいです。

新しい習慣作成時やそれまでの習慣の訂正時に、反映が遅く同じ操作を2度しなければ多いのは修正して頂きたいです。

そしてアプリ内からの「フィードバックを送信する」が送信できません。
なのでレビューとして失礼致します。
よろしくお願い致します。

難しい修正もあるかもしれませんが対応していただけると最高です。

title: UI is a little bit frustrating
body:

I hate looking at the status that say: “Skip” even though I’ve completed it. 
I don’t remember everything from the walk through instructions, but am I supposed to? Because it feels like a test at school, and I got bad grade for not remembering it. I’m supposed to figure it out intuitively or at least have a chance of trial and error, to edit what I’ve tried....

Also, the pop up of premium member register keeps showing up constantly, makes it really frustrating, I want a smooth and pleasant trial first before I decide to invest on it. So for me the UX is not great either...

title: 使いやすいです、１つ要望
body:

課金ありますが、それでも使い続けたいアプリです。
１つ要望があります。
週１回の習慣を、前回完了してから１週間以内に完了したとき、「完了」することができません。
１週間経っていないので、まだタスクにならないのは分かるのですが、前倒しでタスクを完了させることもあるので、改良お願いします。
現在は、１週間に１回の設定を一度毎日１回に変更し、タスクを完了させてから、設定を元に戻しています。
よろしくお願いします。

title: 앱 자체 편의성은 있으나 소통은 안됩니다.
body:
리뷰들을 조금만 주의깊게 살펴보면, 구독 후 일주일 뒤 자동갱신(월단위도 아니고 무조건 1년 프리미엄 구독, 37000원) 으로 많은 소비자들이 환불을 요청하는 리뷰를 볼 수 있습니다.

결론만 말씀드리면, 환불은 이곳에 요청하지 마시고 애플지원페이지로 접속하셔서 환불요청 해주셔야 합니다. 
이 곳 리뷰쓰는곳에는 아무리 환불 요청 글을 올려도, 해줄수가 없습니다.

앱 자체는 깔끔, 습관 형성에 도움 될만합니다.

소비자들이 쓴 글에 공감없이 형식적으로 복붙해서 답변 남기는, 궁극적인 해결책을 애매하게 제시하는 부분에서 앱 신뢰도가 떨어집니다. 
그래서 별은 아쉽지만 2개에요...

설정 - iCloud 동기화
설정 - iCloud 관리

위의 2개 기능을 보고 구매 했는데,
허위로 기능이 보여지고 있습니다.

실제 작동을 안합니다.

동기화 한 상태에서 다른 애플 기기에서 어플 설치하면
기존 데이터 불러오지 못하고 새 어플 처럼 초기화 되어 있습니다.
마찬가지로
어플 제거 후 다시 설치하면
기존의 기록들와 설정 값들이 전부 사라 집니다.

이건 구매했을때 취지가 너무 어긋납니다.
환불해주세요.

작동하지 않는 기능은 화면에 노출하지 말아주세요.
구매할때 현옥 됩니다.

body:
2.0.0으로 업데이트 한 후 기존에 등록했던 습관들이 오늘의 습관에서 다 보이지않고 최대 5개만 보입니다. 오늘 이전 날짜들에서도 습관을 완료했음에도 계속 뜨는 문제가 있네요. 1년 37000원이면 적지 않은 구독료인데 조금 더 빨리 대응해주셨으면 좋겠네요. 
이미 문의하는 메일주소로 캡처까지 해서 말씀드렸구요. "문제를 인지하고 있다. 불편드려 죄송하다."고 답장이 오고 그후 감감무소식입니다. 아무리 연말이라고 하더라도 대응이 너무 느리네요. 이정도 심각한 버그면 이전버전으로 일단 roll back하는 게 맞지 싶습니다. 이미 프리미엄 구독은 취소 했습니다. 남은기간 잘 쓸 수 있게 이전버전으로 사용할 수 있는 방법이 있으면 알려주세요. 감사합니다.

body:
일년에 $12. 넥플릭스도 한달에 15불을 주고있으니 그정도면 괜찮다 싶어, 더 많은 긍정 습관들을 유지하기 위해서 구독하고 작년 7월 부터 쓰고있는데 이제야 리뷰를 쓰네요. 

매 주마다 달성하고 싶은 목표가 있어서 뿌듯해요. 앱에있는 실적 퍼포먼스 기록 향상을 위해서 매일 물 두 병 마시고, 운동하고, 명상하고, 일기쓰고, 스트레칭하고, 저녁마다 탄수화물 줄이고, 일주일에 한 번 마다 춤 안무 연습까지... 등 하고있어요! 무겁고 정중한 검은색 어플 디자인도 좋아요. 

아쉬운 점은 딱 두 달만하고 싶은 습관들이나 등을 못 만드는다는 것..? 안 그러면 만들어놓고 두 달뒤에 지우면 실적 기록이 사라지잖아요 ㅠㅠ 

그 외에는 매일 일상 습관 향상하는데이 많이 도움되고 있어서 매일이 뿌뜻합니다. 이런 어플을 개발해주어서 고맙습니다 ㅎㅎ

title: Productive premium subscription double charged me
body:
Доброе утро!

На днях я заметил, как с APPLE удержали сумму 7990 тенге, проверив свои Subscriptions, понял, что это сумма годовой подписки “Premium 1 year”. Ок, не проблема. Но потом, заметил, что есть два вида годовой подписки - Premium за 7’990 тенге и Premium за 3’990 тенге. 

Не совсем понял разницу, но так как стоимость за одну и ту же услугу была разная, конечно, выбрал ту, которая дешевле. Моя логика заключалась в том, что, возможно, за год пользования произошла какая-то скидка, о которой меня не предупредили и система автоматически сняла с меня старую сумму. 

В итоге, банк удержал с меня ещё одну сумму 3’990 тенге, а старую сумму, я не вижу, чтобы мне вернули. 

Проясните, пожалуйста, ситуацию для меня. 

С благодарностью и уважением,

Канат

title: Nice concept but have problems
body:
I like the concept of the app and the suggestions but there are things that don’t work exactly well. Changing the schedule of a habit is very annoying since it doesn’t save the first time, I’ve made it work after 3 or 4 attempts, also, this change will delete all progress you have in that habit, which is crazy. It could simply change from that day on, as a recurrent google calendar event.

I’ve noticed also, that is not possible to snooze the habit, like for example, reschedule it for another day, which could be helpful specially if updating the schedule of a habit doesn’t work properly and reset the its stats. 

The feeling I get is that there’s still work to be done to make it an stable and nice to use app, however the amount of money it costs don’t really reflect it... to make it clear, in my opinion the app cost is much higher than it should.

title: SEBGRO
body:
**Good:** The tracker’s user interface is the best I've used, with easy statistics and notifications. The auto time-of-day feature outperforms any other app I've tried, and it operates flawlessly.

**Bad:** The app hasn't received substantial updates in years, only bug fixes. It has limited Siri integration and offers just one Watch complication that serves as a quick launcher.

title: Great Stuff
body:
This is day three. I subscribed so I could get right into it.  

Love the interface and the approach. For example, dividing the day’s targets into groups of morning, afternoon and evening keeps the list small and enhances focus.  Very important for habit forming.  You still get configurable reminders so great idea. 

I had to spend a good 10 minutes setting things up and learning how it worked so that I was confident I was using it to its best.  I’d suggest this is important if tracking multiple things from the start is important to you as there appears no way to retrospectively create entries earlier than the create date. That’s one feature I’d like to see in a future release. 

I also wish it could also track the count of things within a task, like pushups for example.  

One thing it has that other products I looked at was an elegant way of tracking things that you want to happen in periods other than daily, and it not feel like you miss days. For example, a goal of swimming 3 times a week can be tracked and hitting it is great because you don’t have to “miss” the days in between.  

It’s easy to use, looks good, is well designed and after three days, I’m 100% on everything.  Wonder how long I can keep that up :)

title: An App that lets gives back your control in life.
body:
For years, I have been struggling with keeping “promises” to myself that I’ll do this and I’ll do that but to only realize after another few months, that I failed to keep those promises again. It’s been an actual struggle on my end and I desperately wanted to discipline myself given that the world is full of distractions. 

But soon later I came across this app, and it so far did help me form a good habit. Since I’m always on my phone everyday, it’s hard to miss these reminders as they pop up during the time you need them so I truly appreciate the development behind this app. However, as for the price, it’s too expensive on my end and I’m already a full time Program and Social Media manager but I did realize and said to myself...

“All those unproductive days would have been more costly than this”

and then I finally realized that, this was actually an investment rather than as an expense to improving my overall being.

title: Subscription
body:
The app is designed very well and looks really good, but that would be all if we’re talking about good sides of it. 

Unfortunately, the notifications wouldn’t work and occur on my phone, as i checked everything the issue wouldn’t disappear. 

But that wasn’t big problem, the REAL problem was being fooled by developer. I knew I was purchasing an app with a 7days free trial, and then (as was clearly written before I downloaded the app) I would have pay around 2$ monthly. I thought “well okay, 2$ is alright) but then suddenly around 25$ was taken from my bank account. I was charged for a ONE YEAR subscription and i wasn’t even informed about it. It might have been written somewhere, but it surely is just fooling people so they pay huge amount of money for the app. 

I had to contact the Apple Help Service, because I was really shocked and scared because of having NO MONEY left on my bank account. I’m glad they helped me, and downloading your app was a big lesson for me - I will check everything ten times before I purchase any other application (Productive - habit tracker was first non-free app on my phone). 

If someone have a lot of money then I even might reccomend this app - but to me, it is way to pricey and not fair for the customers to make them pay for one year without clearly telling them that.

title: Things to improve in order to stay
body:
I think I've tried every productivity and organization app, and this is definitely the most intuitive and useful. Great UI. 
However, in order for the price - quality relation to be worth it, I think they should focus on the motivational side more. Meaning that the stats part for example, is extremely limited. I would like to see all my habits together in a large table to see how well I am doing and compare the process. Not just today and the strike. The visual picture of your habits laid out like that will give more motivation to the user to continue. To have a bigger picture in mind. 
Plus, there should be a way to download your statistics and get more interesting insides.
Moreover, it would be nice to create routines with several habits inside. And you could also make a toggle to show the habits inside and their level of completion on that large table I mentioned. 
Thank you

title: КРУТО!
body:
Приложение реально крутейшее, очень очевидный и приятный user flow и при этом функциональная возможность просто космическая. И иконки меняй и цвет и картинки. Разделение на утро день вечер тоже хорошая задумка. Уведомления фоновые на иконки приложения также по периодам утро день вечер - гениально! Ну и конечно самое главное - статистика. 

Изначально скачал кучу приложений и начал заходить пробовать каждое подряд в итоге это приложение было третьим в списке, а дальше оставалось еще 4 приложения на тест, но я влюбился в это и даже не стал тестировать остальные. 

БОЛЬШОЙ минус - Самое дорогое приложение из всех которые я встречал раньше. И речь сейчас не только о трекерах и планировщиках, а в целом о всех продуктах App Store которыми приходилось пользоваться. А еще нет возможности покупки сразу навсегда.

title: Предложение по функционалу
body:
Добрый день. По функционалу все очень круто! Спасибо за труд! Сравнивала много приложений и выбрала ваше.

Прошу рассмотреть возможность добавить drug-and-drop для заданий/целей, чтобы их можно было сортировать в любом порядке, сейчас они располагаются строго в порядке их добавления (либо я не нашла как их перемещать)).

Например, на утро добавила цель пить воду, затем цель тренировок, они отобразились в таком же порядке списком на вкладке «Утро», но потом поняла, что удобнее эти цели в жизни выполнять в ином порядке, и захотелось их также поменять местами в приложении. Сейчас приходится удалять цель и добавлять ее заново, чтобы поменялся порядок.

Но вот некоторые недостатки, которые просто убивают это приложение. 1 - Почему то нет синхронизации между устройствами, на айфоне свои привычки, на айпаде свои, как бы я не пытался это исправить просто ноль реакции, создавал пользователя, заходил и выходил несколько раз, не помогает, причём на моём пользователе на сайте приложения вообще не подключены премиум версия, хотя я её покупал. 2 - Это постоянные зависания приложения и чтобы это исправить нужно приложение закрыть и заново открыть, причём происходят это зависания практически каждый день и по несколько раз, что раздражает просто безумно. title: Подписка
body:
Само приложение не плохое, но оплата по подписке - отторгает. 

Сегодня буквально каждое приложение пытается подсадить тебя на подписку. Сколько же нужно тратить в месяц обычному человеку, чтобы пользоваться 5-6 платными приложениями? Кажется разработчики уже теряют чувство здравого смысла с подписочной моделью. Spotify стоит дешевле небольшого приложения по привычкам..

Сделайте единоразвую покупку премиум функций и вы больше на этом заработаете.

Предложение купить подписку долбит при каждом включении приложения, что приводит не к удовлетворению от прогресса, а постоянному раздражению. А это быстрее приводит к удалению приложения, чем к трате  денег.

title: Ужасно неудобно
body:
Все задачи и привычки на день отображаются списком, который вмещает всего несколько задач/привычек на экране. Если задач много, приходится листать несколько «страниц», от этого сложно оценить общую картину на день. Если привычки ежедневные, зачем выделять на них целую строчку на экране?? Почему не разместить их все одной строкой из иконок в верхней части экрана?

Нет возможности создать отдельные списки или проекты, чтобы разделить задачи по работе, быту или саморазвитию.

Ещё минус — тема оформления не меняется, только темная.

В общем, приложение совсем не удобно и не оптимизировано под продуктивную работу с ним.
Очень жаль, что я не успела отменить подписку по окончании бесплатного периода и у меня списали оплату за целый год. Кстати, ещё и дорого.
Сейчас пользуюсь другим приложением, гораздо удобнее и в полтора раза дешевле.

И стоит в районе 3000₽. Один раз купил и наслаждаешься без ограничений одной из лучших игр на данный момент. В противовес программа, которую разрабатывали сколько дней/месяцев? Сколько единиц/десяток человек? И за это каждый год отдавать почти 2000₽? Мне кажется где-то кто-то явно с завышенными ожиданиями. Считаете я не понимаю ценообразование? Есть подобная task-management программа. С очень крутыми инструментами и возможностями. Рекламировать не буду, чтобы не заблокировали комментарий. Так вот стоимость программы ~500₽ на всю жизнь. This app is monetized in a very strange way. Instead of letting you use the key features in the free version and show you the value of the app, it boots you to payment screen whenever you try to set up a fourth “habit”, which is really not that much. You can only get a very small sample of what the app can do before being asked to pay - and the subscription is not very cheap.

title: Разочарование
body: Не самое плохое приложение. Выглядит симпатично, работает шустро, интерфейс (с оговорками, о них написано ниже) удобный. Но своих денег, на данный момент, не стоит. Объясню почему. У меня iPhone SE и iOS 12. Во-первых, некорректно работает виджет в центре уведомлений. В нем нельзя отметить выполненную задачу - пишет «не удается загрузить». К тому же нет возможности вывести туда весь список задач на день, там отображаются только задачи для текущего времени суток. Во-вторых, шрифт и размер иконок в приложении слишком большой для iPhone SE. На основном экране помещается только 4 задачи. Отступы между задачами тоже огромные. Изменить это в настройках приложения почему-то нельзя. Этот функционал обязательно должен быть. В-третьих, мне не нравится, что на основном экране отображаются только задачи для текущего времени суток и задачи, которые не привязаны к определенному времени. А остальные задачи скрыты. Я хочу видеть весь список задач на день, разбитый по группам, как на экране «сегодня».  То есть мне хочется, чтобы экран «сегодня» и был моим основным экраном. Каждый раз нажимать на него неудобно. В-четвертых, хочется иметь возможность добавлять обычные задачи, которые не повторяются во времени, как в стандартном приложении «Напоминания». Просто потому что пользоваться одним приложением удобнее, чем двумя. В-пятых, на экране статистики есть календарь, но почему-то нет возможности ткнуть на любой день и посмотреть список задач того дня и какие задачи были выполнены. Кстати, в календаре отображается только текущий месяц. Сейчас октябрь, а когда наступит ноябрь, то что произойдет? Октябрь удалится и его уже нельзя будет посмотреть? Если да, то это еще один минус. Хочу видеть картину за год. В общем, почините виджет, сделайте возможность менять размер интерфейса и дополните остальной функционал, тогда будет отлично.

title: Очень удачное приложение
body:
Приложение понравилось. У него простой интерфейс за счёт удачного компромисса в функционале: нет лишнего, нет и редко используемого, например, нет возможности задания количества и единиц измерения. Но для основной задачи приложения это и не обязательно. Интерфейс и инструкции написаны легко, со вкусом, умеренным юмором и мягкими манипуляциями😊. 

Имейте в виду, интерфейс и встроенные "привычки" представлены на английском языке, но привычки можно заводить свои, родные😊.  

В качестве развития предложил бы добавить элементы mindfulness, типа наглядной отметки нашей реакции на новые привычки, как меняется наше настроение, наслаждение жизнью.

title: Subscription!
body:
I downloaded this amazing app just to write to the developer as well as the Apple editors.
For Apple: keep pushing subscription based apps will end up loosing customers such as me who own 5 macs, 4 iPhones and 2 iPads under my roof!
We don’t mind subscriptions for some valuable & needed apps & services BUT pushing the principle for every single app in every category!
I migrated from windows since 2010 and convinced my family, my parents and one of my sisters to do the same BUT some times I feel you try to push us away!
For the developer: You have a really great app all around BUT what you ask is too much! Every app cycle is 2 years and we may accept a one year cycle for individual developers within a reasonable price.
5$ is the value, in my opinion, for such app. In fact it’s ONLY for this good one. I might stretch it further for 10 if the cycle 2 years at least.

Apple: we are ready to go pack to pen and paper if you keep up the good work!

We pay too much for subscriptions of everything!!!

Thanks to the developers for their response. If still convinced with the subscription model, I suggest you consider “Setapp”. All the best with your good work.

title: Good. But subscription good? Not that much.
body:
I like the app, it has nice features with good UI. But a monthly subscription for a habit tracking  app features? 

It’s too much, there are no need for extensive servers or continuous innovation or even that much operations. I need it to remind me of habits, with a check & track. Why would i pay monthly for that?! What are the huge continuous monthly resources are being paid due to my use?

I unfortunately, though I’m happy to shed more than the yearly subscription for a one time purchase, deleted it and looked for a purchasable option. 

Many thanks.

UPDATE: thanks for your reply. What i meant is, for subscription-based apps I expect a continuous resources and benefits. I’m subscribing in services from 10$ upto 200$, no problem, but i know there is a continuous benefits, rather than just using the same asset which is powered also by my phones’ CPU.

I don’t mind paying 10-20$ for this app, but it doesn’t make sense to me to pay monthly to rent this app where there is many do the same. And there’s limitations in how innovative the market can be.

title: Sudden forced subscription
body: I have used this app for years as a habit tracker, basically just a tally which could easily be kept in a text file or even a piece of paper would do, but I liked the simplicity and ease of use of the app. I guess over time the developer needed to make money to keep the app going, I have no problem with that. Reasonable ways would be to run banner adds or develop the app with new features, making those available as a one time purchase or as a subscription service. What the developer has done now is to completely block the app if you don’t buy a subscription. I can’t even access my previously tracked habits, it’s just a screen with one availably button forcing you to buy the subscription. I’ve never experienced such a behaviour from an app before. The price point is absolutely ridiculous- 49 SEK ($4.8). Per week. It would be more expensive than the following: Spotify premium, Netflix, 2TB icloud storage, my phone bill, my home insurance, my electricity bill, my internet bill. How the developer thinks this tiny app is worth more than any of the above is beyond me. It’s so absurd.

title: Prenumeration för 169:-/år i ett tight fält
body:
Gillar gränssnittet, den intuitiva och trevliga designen — känslan eller flödet är där och känns eget. Jag betalar mer än gärna för bra mjukvara. Har gjort och kommer alltid att göra. 

(Faktum är att jag inte *vill* använda ett verktyg utan att först ha gjort en pengatransaktion med utvecklaren…)

Dock, på en mättad marknad fylld med utmärkta val — någonstans bland todo-/att göra-listor, anteckningsprogram, produktivitets- och projekthanteringssystem — är en enklare app likt Productive med prenumeration per år problematisk för mig. 

Hade hellre betalat en högre summa en gång istället. Med så många verktyg på arbetet och privat, försöker jag undvika återkommande kostnader som är svåra att hålla koll på, såvida inte appen eller tjänsten är extra värdefull för mig. 

Things, OmniFocus, Clear, Due, Do, TickTick, Nozbe, Todoist, Planny, kanske till och med Notion, Trello och Basecamp… Alla dessa program hade man kunnat hävda att de ligger i samma kategori som Productive. 

Gillar er idé och tycker ni ska fortsätta med det ni gör. Fokusera på ett trevligt, tydligt och smidigt designat gränssnitt — samtidigt som funktionaliteten kretsar kring saker som skall göras (med fokus på rutiner och upprepade händelser).

För mig, hade jag först behövt ta bort ett gäng tjänster som jag använder idag och återkomma… :)

 — @celebritarian

Jag skulle alltså kunna ha en rubrik med mitt eget namn och mina aktiviteter där under. Sen skulle jag ha underrubriker med mina barn och min frus namn och deras aktiviteter. Man skulle bara kunna ändra sina egna aktiviteter till utförda osv. Med ett sådant upplägg skulle familjer kunna skapa familjeutmaningar och små tävlingar exemplevis då det gäller aktivitet och rörelse. Vidare skulle man kunna lägga till belöningar som familjen ställde in själv. Jag skulle tex kunna lägga in att barnen ska bädda sängen och duka av bordet varje dag. Den som når 30 dagar först belönas med något som familjen kommit överens om och som då blinkar och ger lite stjärnor i appen! Jag tror Garmin har ngt liknande i sin app till deras Jr klockor. En sådan funktion skulle absolut vara värd att betala för!

title: Just what I needed
body: Tried a lot of ways to get better routines and habits, this is exactly what I needed. Most productivity apps kind of requires you to have a fairly routine life to begin with- fixed work hours, every weekday the same from one week to the next. This app allows you to create good routines and habits even when your days can be very different from one day to the next, and unpredictable. I also find that the way it lists habits, and the notifications and app icon badge, doesn't add stress (which is normally something you're trying to get rid of). It's friendly to you, and super easy to use. The only thing I'm missing is ability to change week start day to Monday, other than that it's very flexible and customizable to individual needs. Got pro, and well worth it.

title: Good, but can’t keep historic data
body:
In general I really like the app, but the fact that all the historic data is deleted when you change the periodity of a task (e.g. changing the task from 2 times per week to 3 times per week) is a huge deal breaker. I only found this out when, after a few months of having a perfect record on a habit I decided to boost it from 2 to 3 times per week and found out all the historic records are gone. Sure there was some vague warning, but that doesn’t really help. 

I only recommend the app if you never plan to change the periodity of your tasks, but if you do its quite useless for keeping long term data as progress tracking in life log is not possible.

title: Gayet başarılı
body:
Uygulamayı çok uzun zamandır aktif bir şekilde kullanıyorum ve çok memnunum. Büyük bir çoğunluk pahalılığından şikayet etmiş ama muadili ücretsiz veya uygun ücretli uygulamalar da yok değil. Biraz araştırılsa herkes kendi bütçesine uygun bir uygulama bulabilir. Ben farklı bir çok uygulama denemiş biri olarak Productive i tek geçerim. Bence hak ediyor ücretini. Uygulamanın belki de en güzel yanı kendisini sürekli olarak geliştiriyor oluşu. Meydan okumalar, programlar sonradan geldi ve çok iyi düşünülmüş alanlar. 

Benim tek sorunum-mail de attım, alışkanlıkları aylık seçemiyoruz. Her ayın belli bir günü seçiliyor ama ayda herhangi bir gün seçeneği yok. Önceden vardı. Yazılım ekibi şu probleme bi el atsa nasıl mutlu olurum 🌸

title: Guys just let us experience the app please!
body:
Ok so, I have downloaded the app and you wanted me to write a comment just after 2 minutes. Then here is my comment: I do not have any idea what’s going on, if the app is useful or not, if it would be benefitable for me or not. Where ever I click, what ever I try to do within the app, read the habits and try to understand if the app is what I am looking for, a pop up appears and says: subscibe. when I close it an other pop up appears and asks what do I think of the app. Well I DO NOT KNOW because you do not let me experience the app! I tried to use the app for 10 mins, and all I did was closing the pop ups trying to sell me the product that I do not know or trying to get a good comment on the thing that I do not know.

We are not stupid really, just let us experience the app then I will decide if I want to buy it or if I want to make a comment on it. You do not have to remind me evey 20 seconds. Just because a popup appears telling me to pay a money, I will not do it.

title: 很多策略性的誤導誘使用戶付費
body: 只是被臉書廣告打到來下載看看，發現這個APP真的是心機用盡呢！登入畫面的兩個按鈕，其中一個是「230/一個月」另一個則是用鮮豔而明顯的按鈕寫著「免費試用」，但這邊要注意，仔細看在一旁有個小小的說明提醒「7天免費試用，然後以 970/年的價格**自動**續訂」代表著什麼？如果你沒有看到那小小的說明，你以為你只是在使用像其他一般的APP那樣是以試用的身分在瀏覽這個APP，殊不知因為已經綁上apple帳戶，在七天內沒有主動去帳戶取消訂閱你就會被扣款！而且預設扣款還是用他們最貴的方案970/年去購買！建議開發者啦！你們這個免費試用的CTA上面的文字不能這樣寫啦！好歹寫個「免費試用7天」這樣的文字也比較不會容易造成誤會！虧你們的App介面設計蠻美的，結果在這些小細節上看盡你們的伎倆！做APP不能這樣好嗎！使用者體驗在這個環節就輸光了，以後跟朋友提到這個APP只有滿滿的惡評，還奢望什麼Referral指標！

title: Overall Great but an unfortunate bug
body:
I went with this app after dabbling with more than a dozen other habit tracking apps because this one stands out for being powerful, simple, intuitive and aesthetically pleasing. Kudos to the developers!
However, I’ve come into a problem recently where the app seems to be one day behind. It’s 7:33 in the morning on a Friday, but the app seems to be stuck on Thursday. I can’t check off any items on the actual current day (Friday) which shows up in the app as “tomorrow”, which is frustrating. My time zone setting (Taipei) and actual time showing on my device is right. I tried to change the language to Chinese hoping that would fix it, but it didn’t work.
If it helps with the fixing, this problem seems to have started when I tinkered with “time of day” setting earlier this morning (a little past 12am) and set morning to start at 1am.
Update: going offline seems to have fixed it.

title: Nice but could be better
body:
So I bought this years ago but never used it and was checking out another app and figured I’d use this and compare it. What I would like to see here is device syncing. Calendar and Apple health integration for reading and exercise habits and with the calendar it can set you reminders and adjust if schedules change. A disappointment is that there’s no pre set habit for showers. Ok but not even an icon? There’s a duster icon but not one for a shower? There’s even a tooth icon for brushing teeth but no shower when many many depressed Americans don’t shower. I’m tracking cold showers btw not regular ones but anyways. I can’t remember what I paid but I couldn’t justify the current subscription cost for how basic it is and the features it lacks that other apps have. I know these guys have been around awhile so I’m hoping they continue to improve it and get ahead on the AI train. Oh one final thing. Because it doesn’t play well with Apple my size settings don’t transfer to the app and there is no way to make things larger. I can see and read most stuff with a little difficulty but some text is too small to read and. I ability to enlarge text to make it more readable but that’s not going to be a common issue for most but blind people use apps too lol

Edit: dark mode all the time is getting old quick. There is no bright light mode when I wake up and the dark mode widget looks really dumb during the day next to everything else not in dark mode.

title: Exactly what I was looking for
body:

Update after lots of use: The only reason I dropped my rating to five stars is that really often when I check off a task it stays frozen, that is shifted right with the check mark displayed. I have eight habits and it never makes it through all eight without freezing. To get it to register that the habit was done I need to hard close the app and relaunch it. That is a small daily annoyance that I end up doing a couple times each day. 

Besides that, in terms of function and design, this is by far the best app I’ve found, which is why I stick with it despite the minor annoyance of having to hard close it to register which habits are checked off.

title: Great App but Expensive
body:
I have used this app premium version for two months now. It has been amazing. It is exactly what I need. A habit tracker where I can actually analyze the data to see which habits I still need to work on. 

I gave it 4 stars because I’ve been having issues with its timer feature. If I turn on the timer and move to another app, the timer stops working. If I play music or a video, the timer stops working. It’s very frustrating especially since I like using its Pomodoro feature to complete tasks. It throws my data off. 

Another feature that needs to be fixed is displaying data if you completed some of the work. There are some goals that are time based. For example, if the goal is 30 minutes a day, but you only completed 20 minutes. It would be nice to see it in the stats section. You only see if it is completed or not on the calendar even though you have a symbol for some done. 

Additionally, I wish I could export my data to an excel file. If I’m tracking my goals this would take it to the next level.

I know that many have complained about the price increase. I am paying about $35 a year for it. This is pricey but I think it’s worth it. Now if it jumps up to $80 that would be really steep.

title: “Mark a habit as incomplete”
body:
I think there should be a feature where you can mark that a habit was not completed. There is a feature where you can skip a habit in special occasions, and there is a feature where you can mark that a habit was completed. I understand that if you don’t do either of these then the app recognizes it as an incomplete habit but sometimes when I go back to previous days and see that a habit is not completed, I can’t remember if I just forgot to mark it as complete or if I actually didn’t do it. That’s why I really think there should be a feature to mark that a habit was not completed instead of just having that be recognized by the app if you don’t mark it at all. I don’t want to just skip a habit and have it say that my streak continues. I benefit from the punishment of losing a streak. That’s why I want there to be an additional feature to mark that a habit was not completed. Maybe it could be a long press on the habit or some other type of gesture. 

Thank you for your time and for considering this feature. Other than this feature, I would actually give five stars—but this is a huge issue for me that is make or break for me.

title: Account/Subscription Management is Non-Existent
body:
The core of this app is sound. It helps keep me on track with my productivity and habits when it works. Having said that, there are many flaws on this app that make me regret getting a subscription. 
1. There is no cross device functionality for my account. The habits you create and track only exist on the device in which you created them. So I can’t track my activity on, say, my iphone if I mainly use my ipad to track my habits. I assume the developers don’t want to spend the resources for backend storage and account management. Either that or they’re simply unable.
2. Related to above, there is no central place to manage my account or even tell which account a device is logged in under. When I select the manage subscription item in settings it tells me to log into the apps site to manage, but the website offers no such ability to manage anything.
3. The Pomodoro tracker is absolutely atrocious. It is completely useless. The timer won’t continue to count down most times when you minimize the app. So you will long be done with your first phase when opening the app only to see that hardly ten seconds have passed since you last minimized. I strongly suspect this is developer error(relying on background running when ios can kill it at anytime, vs. using local notifications). Hint: Use remote notifications for this when/if you get a backend running.

The design and UI flow is really great, however, this apps potential is being limited by these severe issues. 

At this time I cannot recommend this app to anybody.

title: Almost the best, but behind on the times
body:

If you’ve got a great set of habits built for yourself on the iPad, but then leave the house and think you’ll be able to track those habits on your iPhone or Apple Watch, you’ll be sadly mistaken. And that’s a huge drawback when you are someone that relies on a wide variety of devices in various locations to get your daily things done. After researching other options, I will be switching until this necessary feature is implemented and no longer hindering workflow or habit tracking.

other suggestions include:
-being able to mark additional times you completed a habit beyond the goal number
-ability to split screen with other apps

title: Where’s my subscription details?
body:
I have been using Productive since 2016 but NEVER, mind you, gathered myself to stay accountable.

End of last year, I decided to change that. Habits were looking good. I changed my phone and reinstalled the app.

To my utter disappointment, all my data was gone! To my surprise I couldn’t even find my subscription on Apple. So how was I on Premium (how I know is because I was able to add unlimited habits), but not have them synced ANYWHERE?!

I reached out to support, and they just apologized and repeated what I told them. No resolution.

Regardless, I restarted my habits and I’ve been going strong till now, but I’m so afraid that I’m gonna lose all of this, whenever I change my phone again. For this reason, I’m very disappointed.

And somewhere, via some email, I know I am being charged, and for the life of me, they’re not able to tell me where it’s going from. How am I supposed to know when they don’t even know? This is super disappointing!

But on the flipside, I’m obsessed with the app, and I love how easily I can track my habits. Yet, I’m reconsidering another app due to paranoia from the above reasons.

Then I quickly discover that the pomodoro will stop running whenever a notification pops up. Every. Single. Notification. Do you get a lot of notifications? You do?! Wow, me too!

I've been using the premium version of this app for around a year now, and I'm very happy with it. It's intuitive, simple, customizable, and the sound effects are great at reinforcing the reward of completing habits.

My only complaint is with some errors regarding habits that aren't daily. The streak is really important in motivating me, and so I've ended up just removing all my weekly habits, which isn't ideal.

In spite of that, I highly recommend downloading this app and trying the premium version.

title: It’s fine. Too easy to ignore it. Should be more annoying.
body:
I am a full time college student with ADHD and narcolepsy, so needless to say it is very difficult for me to remember to do literally anything even with the truckload of medications I have to take. I was curious about this app because it seems to have good reviews. Don’t get me wrong, I do like this app quite a bit: especially the built in pomodoro timer which is very useful for homework. However it is too easy for me to forget about this app because it doesn’t remind me to use it often enough. 

I have found myself ignoring the app for several days before remembering to use it again. I wish there were an option to make it send you lots of notifications over and over until a certain task is completed. I need more than just one reminder notification which I can easily swipe away and then continue procrastinating.  

For example, I always forget to brush my teeth so I wish there was a more forceful and annoying reminder/productivity app that could make my phone send me hundreds of notifications over and over every morning until I do it.

I think for a person with a normal level of executive functioning this app is fine as it is, after all most people wouldn’t need their phone to vibrate and make noises incessantly until they remember to brush their teeth every morning. 

But I really wish it had the option to send nonstop reminders until a task is completed, for those of us who are very sleepy and forgetful and need an extra push to be able to build a consistent daily routine.

title: developers please read!
body:
after testing extensively over several hours other habit tracking apps I found this one to be the most fully featured in terms of statistics and things like an in app timer. The widgets are clean and good enough, there is a more section, and the ability to pause habits. However there are some major shortcomings of this app that has been available for so long that I think would make it much better. 
1. overflow timer - would be very appreciated. It’s very difficult to edit entries to show the time that was spent versus the time that was scheduled in the habit. also, it doesn’t show the edited time in the statistics after the fact. I would love to be able to set the timer to start for example minutes read and if my time exceeds what was scheduled it would automatically update and show in statistics.
2. bad habits -there is no proprietary bad habit set up in the app as of now. It’s easy enough to mark don’t smoke as completed if you don’t smoke for that day. But what if it is some thing like cut back smoking and you want to mark every time you have a cigarette so that that data is available in statistics and so that if you are trying to cut down from 10 cigarettes a day you can see when you only had nine and passed your habit but also when you only had three and did even better-even so when you failed the habit and had 11 but when you also failed the habit and had 20.

thanks guys!

Only if you complete a day do you get reminded the next day - that means the initial stages of building a habit are made harder by this app. That’s a bad approach. Saw last night’s notification this morning and used it to mark the task done for last night? Nope, you marked it done for tonight. 

EDIT: The point below is wrong, there is indeed a way to create a task that repeats every Sunday. The option for that is under “Daily” and not “Weekly”, which is why it was a little difficult to find.

Look, it seems like a decent app, yet they’re purposefully trying to rip you off. The instant you go to cancel you subscription, suddenly you get prompted with a 50% discount. Then, the moment you proceed with canceling, they pop-up another 70% discount for only $9.99 per year. Guess what? That just means $9.99 is the REAL price they are willing to sell their product for. Everyone else is just a sucker in their eyes who they get to rip-off for 4x the real price, 

Don’t be a sucker. Use another app.

The interface is overcrowded and involves so much tapping around that, again, I’m not sure how this aids my productivity rather than cutting into precious time I could be doing meaningful work.

Pros: Group challenges to try new habits, great scheduling options for various habits, enough progress stats (for me at least)

Cons:
 1) Would LOVE to have family sharing option. 
2) Would be great to challenge friends/family who also use this app.  The group challenges are a great idea but you complete them individually.
3) syncing across personal devices is not an option or available as far as I found. 

All in all it’s a great app. I have found it helpful and dare I say I have improved personally since I started using this app. If you are looking for a task manager or scheduler look elsewhere.

title: Super Useful App
body:
I’ve been using the Productive app for a few months now and I’m enjoying it so far. It’s nice to see you progress on habits and for me it’s an opportunity to recognize what I accomplished today. I can be a little hard on myself sometimes so it’s nice to spend some time looking at what I did do versus what I didn’t.
That being said there’s a few things I think would be a major improvement to the app.
1. A way to either organize a the order that you see your habits so that you can easily follow a thought out routine. Even better would be a way to group habit based off specific routines (ie morning/evening routines, pre-workout routine, cleaning routine, study routine etc)
2. A goal setting interface. I think habits and goals work together. Often bigger goals require completing a task on a regular bases.  I imagine a goal page that shows all of a persons big goals, under the bigger goals would be smaller goals or single tasks that lead towards the larger goal and the habits that contribute. For example one of my personal goals is to push 300lbs on the leg press. On a goal page I would be reminded of that specific goal everyday and then I could click it and see all the milestones (like hit 240lbs, then 250lbs etc) that lead up to that goal as well as a single tasks related to the goal (for example: research proper nutrition for improved strength training) and all the habits I’m doing to achieve that goal (like workout, stretch, drink water etc).
3. More icons for habits also would be cool.
Overall genuinely enjoy the app and would like to keep using it. Just had some ideas on how to improve the user experience. Everything it does include is amazing. Challenges, articles, widgets, and the habit stats are invaluable.

title: So Much Potential. Needs Updates
body:
Love this app. Best one I’ve found by far. I’m a premium member. The interface is nice, it’s easy to use. However, there are a few areas that I needs improvement in. I’ve listed below as what it needs to have and what it could offer:

NEED -

- Per week, month, and year options. Currently you can only do per day. What if I say I want to practice yoga “twice per week” or “meditate 90 minutes per week”. Only way to do this now is to create a habit for the yoga and tie it to two specific days and complete them on those days. I don’t care about some habits occurring on a specific day as long as I do them that week.

- Reset on habits when making changes should be optional. This one is a killer and SO ANNOYING. Currently, if you make any changes whatsoever to the habit it resets your progress. What if I’m exercising Monday and Wednesday and I want to add Friday? Yep. That will reset your streak. Even though I’m ADDING another day to my habit (the opposite of failing) you lose your streak. title: The Best Habit App (for me, personally)
body:
I I have tried a great many habit-tracking / goal-reaching apps in an effort to inject some accountability into my journey towards being a more productive person.  But like New Years resolutions and the friends you made in High School, they all kind of fall away after the honeymoon period of “Wow, look how much work I’m putting into myself, yay me” wears off.

This app is, for me, not like that.  I’ve fallen off the bandwagon many times—for sure—but I always come back.  Maybe it’s the icons and the minimalist-but-with-depth design philosophy, maybe it’s the way features keep being added (maybe it’s the infuriating choice to push a subscription model… Probably not that), but Productive is just eminently charming and friendly.

It’s the perfect middle ground between overwhelmingly dense, all-in-one productivity/reminders/scheduling apps like ToDoist or Due and hyper open-ended checklist simulator apps like Clear or Bear.  ‘Productivity - Habit Tracker’ makes me happy to start and maintain habits.

(Disclaimer: none of this may apply to you; hacking your brain is a science of one—you do you!  Find what works!)
author: Ink Runner

title: App Makers Have Lost Focus
body:
I used to love, love, love this app. It had a gorgeous, simple design that was the epitome of iOS elegance. And it worked perfectly as a habit tracker.

Now the app is completely bloated. Instead of just tracking whatever habits you choose, now it has pop-up animations that encourage you to build on your success by taking on more habits. It also suggests challenges for things like fitness and intermittent fasting, all in the service of getting you to take on more habits. And the last straw for me is it now recommends articles about habits, seemingly to get you to take on more habits.

I don’t want any of these things, and I definitely don’t want an app that I use only to track very specific creativity and mental health habits to suggest that my real problem is that I’m not doing enough intermittent fasting! Instead of feeling good about tracking the things I want to accomplish, I feel the app now just reminds me that I’m not doing enough to “be better.” Instead of being self-directed, the app feels now like it has a perfect “me” in mind and will keep pushing me toward that hollow ideal.

This app is supposed to help you stay focused and get things done, but now it’s just a distraction to me. I used to use this every day and now I don’t want to open it at all.

title: They need to learn about User Experience
body:
I have been using and paying for this app for a while, and it does what I need if I set all the settings right, although I’m annoyed that they keep popping things up every few months to try out some new feature, as if I’ll say, “Yeah, this system I’ve set up for myself has kept my life on track for the past few years, but let’s shake it up and try something else just for fun!” I wouldn’t complain if it was just a thing saying, “Hey, we added this new feature, want to try it?”, but usually the screen only has one button that takes you into the screen to start adding some new kind of habit (like the Challenges).

I recommended this to my mom a year or so ago, and I was shocked at how much the onboarding process has gone downhill. It prompted twice to buy the app before even showing her a tutorial that forced her to add a habit she wasn’t interested in, mark it done, undo it, etc, and then it prompted so often to pay for it in that first day, that she didn’t use it and decided not to pay for it.

Yesterday I sent an email to report a bug. I got a response today from their tech support trying to get the bug to resolve on my phone by reinstalling rather than tackling the actual bug, and so I instead installed the app on a new device to reproduce it, since their history with maintaining user data is pretty poor and I was not going to risk losing all my data over a bug I could work around.

But onboarding experience is even worse now. It took me like 5 minutes to just get into the app, and I ended up force quitting and reopening the app to get out of the tutorial. I was prompted 3 times during the onboarding/tutorial to pay for the app before I’d gotten a chance to try out the free side of the freemium model (as far as they knew since it was on a new device), and then as I tried to test the bug, I was interrupted several times by the pop up to pay for the full version.

So I no longer recommend this app. It’s trash. I think it’s bad enough that it’s worth me making an app for myself for what I want out of this. (Not to mention that the streaks don’t even mean anything since historical data often randomly gets gaps inserted that weren’t there the day before, breaking long running streaks. I’ve never missed one of these for the past 706 days, and I haven’t changed my habits for 437 days, and yet my overall streak is only 411 days. It’s clear the developers either don’t use the app, or they only use it to look for bugs and don’t actually care about it.

To the devs: if all the extra prompts to pay are an attempt to convert more people from free to paid, you’re going about it wrong. One prompt during the tutorial, cutting down the tutorial to just a couple screens, and then waiting to prompt for at least a couple days would convert more free users into paid users because they would get a chance to try the app first, and they might actually like it if they get a chance to try it. Prompting multiple times before they get a chance to use the app will either push them away or at best (for you) get someone to pay who doesn’t actually use the app, which is obviously morally wrong.

title: Good but annoying!
body:
So here’s the deal - I tried the app for a week. I actually really liked it based on function and all that, and I would say it was successful in helping me complete the habits I was looking to complete and track.

My issue is with the way overly persistent upgrade popups almost every time you click anything in the app, and that they went subscription based. Literally every 15 seconds of use in the app, you’ll see a full screen pop up asking you to upgrade. A)Way too much of our world has become subscription based! Its great for profits but it’s crap for consumers much of the time. I don’t need another leach with auto draft capabilities on my bank account. B)I don’t need syncing which means I don’t need to interact with servers, which is half a developer’s explanation for subscriptions usually. C)I’m happy to buy apps that are expensive even if it’s a one time purchase. I’ve even spent upwards of $50 and $100 on productivity apps in the past. But I got to use the version I bought for as long as I wanted - it wasn’t a recurring subscription.

Unless it’s truly an ongoing service like Netflix or Apple Music, or Dropbox, I’m not willing to engage a subscription.

So I like the app a lot, but won’t be using it and will look for others. And if I can’t find one, I’ll use paper or a spreadsheet on my phone.

title: It’s fine. But annoying.
body:
The entire app is set up to be some silly competition with yourself. I just need something to keep track of the things I want to try and hit in a day — I’m not trying to guilt trip myself because my “streak is broken.” There doesn’t seem to be a way to turn this off, which is absurd. So it’s a great interface and user-friendly that way, but if you’re not interested in feeling bad about yourself every day when it brow-beats you for not completing your “habits,” I’d look elsewhere.

ETA: I was feeling pretty cranky when I tapped this review out, but as my year subscription comes to an end, I still won’t be renewing. I appreciate the response that some things can be turned off, but respectfully — most of them can’t be. And the edits that are offered often don’t work. Trying to update days that you’d like existing habits to appear on your list is hit or miss (usually miss — it doesn’t stick. I end up having to delete habits entirely and enter them anew to make any changes at all). The orientation of the app is toward creating new daily habits and competing with yourself. If that’s your thing, do it up. But if the developers want this to be for a wider audience, then group all of those notifications into a “challenge” interface, and give the rest of us an option to turn it off. I’d love this to be a task-tracker without the game aspect, but it isn’t.

It only took me a few minutes to figure it out because it is SUPER easy to use. Productive keeps your tasks and habits super easily organized without overwhelming you. You can set times, durations, and goals on all your tasks. It is easily customizable and honestly makes me excited to get my tasks done for the day! Honestly, the makers of Productive, thank y’all so much!

title: Great and easy to use but...

The many options you can do like setting something weekly, putting on a timer, be able to differentiate the habits and reminders is very cool and convenient.

But I needed a remind app that really gets what I need to remind me in my head. The simple notification I get on my phone isn’t enough, there’s no in-your-face remind option that can get me to go do what I need. I want a loud annoying alarm to tell me to get to what I need to do, I want pop up notifications 24/7 to remind me until I click that check button, I want the app to remind me through text as well. 

Just simply seeing a notification once or twice doesn’t cut it, and the fact that it just stops sending notifications after a week of not going on the app isn’t very good either. 

If there was an update to add alarms and annoying notifications I would definitely come back to this app.

title: Glitches, crashes, poor sync across devices
body:
I’ve been using this app for about a year and half now and I’ve had many problems. Nothing just works how its supposed to. My completed tasks aren’t being synced across my devices, so if I click completed on my Apple Watch or iPhone, my iPad won’t reflect it, and vice versa. Sometimes it will sync one completion here or there but its very unreliable. I can mark every task completed on my iPad and hours later my iPhone has only realized I’ve completed one or two tasks. My devices haven’t even synced some completions from a month ago. This defeats the purpose of having it on separate devices if they won’t sync properly... as well as the whole idea of tracking habits.

On to the next problem: the sometimes working Apple Watch app. Probably 50% of the time the Apple Watch app is non-responsive or just crashes when you open it. I’ve had days where I can’t open the app on the Apple Watch. Yes... everything is updated and my settings are set to sync across devices... things just don’t work. I can’t believe I’ve paid for two years of service that works this poorly.

EDIT: Now even a year later it still is not syncing anything between my devices. In fact, I don’t even see an iCloud option in the settings anymore. I think they gave up on the syncing.

title: Great app w/room for improvement
body:
I’ve had this app for years and have used it on and off, it helps me get on track and I recommend it.
I really like the app for keeping track of all the daily things I want to get done, and especially things I’d like to do only once a week or month, like calling my grandmother and taking the time to plan my month out at the beginning of each month. 
I can check them off and then won’t be reminded again until the next week or month. 
It’s easy enough to use. 
I just have one rather large problem with it. It can be really discouraging the way it only gives you credit for “perfect days.” I just started the habit of drinking 8 glasses of water each day, I’ve achieved 5 glasses, 7 glasses etc, but in my stats, it’s like I drank no water at all. It’s really dissatisfying. 
A big motivation for me is feeling accomplished when I can see what I’ve done.
This app would be perfect if it notified me “you’ve completed 50% of your morning habits today! Keep it up!” Or if I could see I’ve almost reached my 8 full glasses of water almost every day this week.
With how I use the app, it’s almost impossible to achieve a perfect day, but it’d be nice to see that I keep up with over 70% of my daily habits each week. Or I do 100% of my nighttime habits.
That’s something I would change, along with how sensitive the buttons are, I’m always accidentally swiping habits left or right when I’m just scrolling through them. It’s annoying.

title: Invasive privacy policy - glad it lost all my data
body:
I used to love this app. Nice UI and great use of icons. I even paid for the premium features.

Then after the last update, ALL my data was lost. Habits, prefs, all gone. It found my Premium status, but lost everything else.

So I had to delete the app and reinstall. When it walked through the setup, I decided to read the privacy policy. And wow, I’m glad I did. 

IMO, this app collects far more personal data than is needed for a habit-tracking app. Personal info, browsing, location, and more — even your unique device identifiers — AND SHARES IT. They’re part of a “family” of companies and share your data between them and with partners. And I couldn’t find any way to opt out.

If someone needs to take meds, or exercise, or anything personal at all, I’m not okay with knowing they’re potentially sharing or selling my info to companies and ad networks and who knows what else.

Productive has become unreasonably expensive for what it does. It’s just a habit tracker. And with their very invasive privacy policy, I won’t be using it. Make your own call, of course, but I urge you to read it. I deleted Productive, and will be looking at apps that specify that your information does not leave your device.

title: An app created by sadists
body:
Update: I have written to customer support 5 times and they still have not resolved this issue. The most recent time is 12/13/2020. 

With this app if you don’t meet your goals this app tells you that you didn’t succeed and it suggests that you change your goals. It sends this message every —single — time you miss even one goal. It does it over and over again. I wrote to customer service for help. I asked them how to turn off the discouraging message. And their answer was “we’ll consider making that change in future upgrades.” Which, I guess is something. In the meantime they have made my money be wasted.

This is what I wrote to customer service on the 5th try on 12/13/2020:

I hate being told repeatedly by this app that my goal “streak” is broken. It isn’t. I just didn’t put it in the app. It’s a negative thing to say and it discourages my being productive. 

It’s a big thumbs down just when I’m opening my app to be productive. 

Please don’t write back again and say how you’ll let the developers know my feedback. Please try to get me a target date for fixing this. 

I paid good money for this app years ago and I really like it. It does exactly what I want. Except for this nasty, negative message that the developers added in 2019. 

Every time I get that negative comment about my streak being broken from this app it puts me in a sour mood. And I wanted to reach out and let the company that produces it know. This productivity app is harming my my ability to be productive.

body: Not very organized. Also, they do have “challenges” that you can join that is similar to what I’m referencing above but there does seem to be a way to create a custom challenge or even to just remove the ones that they have.  It would be nice to have full control to customize what I want to do.

title: I Love it but Glitches Make it a Chore to Use
body:
I do really love this app. I use it as motivation to get things done when my depression extinguishes all self-motivation. I immediately subscribed to it and would have rated 5 stars in that first month. 

When I first got the app a few months ago I noticed a couple of small glitches that weren’t really problematic and just restarting the app fixed them. If you slide to complete one task quickly after another, two of the first task will appear in the completed tasks instead of the two separate ones. Sometimes the app lags when I’m trying to complete a task so I have to slide it multiple times and that can result in the above happening; which is frustrating because I have to restart the app to be able to undo that second task that I haven’t done yet. Little mildly frustrating glitches like that. They have been getting progressively more common to the point that I now have to restart the app three to four times every singe time I use it. It’s almost non-functional.

The reason I’m here on the App Store today looking for a replacement for this app and leaving this review is because of a new glitch that made its appearance a couple day ago. If I edit a task, even without saving the changes I’ve made, it turns on the “Set end date or total amount” function and I can’t turn it off. This makes it to where the next time you complete that task it automatically removes it from your habits. Luckily it can be salvaged and reinstated but doing so resets all of the data on that habit making it brand new. I have “solved” this by setting the end date of all of my tasks as Dec 31, 2099. That was exhausting and infuriating. It took nearly an hour to do and reset all of my habits back to new as if I’d never done a single thing in the three months I’ve had this app. Now I need to make more habits but do not want to have to do that for all of them.

That glitch was the final straw, I cannot continue using this app until it is fixed. Productive, as it is currently, is practically unusable and attempting to use it just results in anger. I am incredibly disappointed that I’m having to switch to something else because I adore Productive.

However the fact that the app is completely unusable (wont even open!) for like a week or more after each update is unreal. I figured out that this was the case years ago, so have consistently delayed updating for at least a few weeks after each update release on habit (ha). However, I accidentally updated a mere week after release this time....and now the app once again won’t even open for me. While forgivable for a fairly new product team, it’s crazy that this is still the case ~a week after an update years later. Why not roll back a version so we at least have something workable to use in the meantime? Also don’t release updates until they’ve been extensively verified and tested for bugs.

title: Good app but could be better
body:
I really do like this app to keep track of certain habits, but it could be better. 

1. There is no way to edit the frequency of a habit. For instance, in the beginning I wanted to workout twice a week. Now I’m at a point where I’m working out three days a week. I can’t add the third day in because it’s set for twice a week. And if I go in and update the habit to three days a week, it’s going to erase all of the previous times I’ve completed the habit and start over from zero. This is super annoying and seems like something that could be easily fixed on their end. 

2. I can’t retroactively add days I’ve completed something once I create a new habit. Let’s say I decide today that I want to start tracking my workouts. So I create the habit today. Well, I worked out yesterday and the day before. But I can’t input those, because I just created the habit today. Also seems like an easy fix. 

If they fixed these two things, I would rate it five stars.

title: Good at tracking, bad at measuring
body:
I was looking for something to track my habits which is distinct from having a todo list or planning a day hour by hour. This app perfectly fits that paradigm.

UX is amazing. In some ways I found myself preferring how the app does things over my own methods. I like thinking of habits in terms of time of day, although you don’t have to label them as such.

Another nice thing is that habits can be measured with different metrics, for example, walking can be measured in miles, studying measured in time, making your bed is a single instance, etc. But this is also where I ran into problems.

Some of their default habits mandate a particular type of metric which you can’t change, so I had to create my own version.

Time-based habits have a timer you can run, which is great, except that you *must* run the timer in order for it to count; you can’t manually input time spent.

Even worse is that the timer doesn’t run unless the screen is on and the app is running. Great idea, but its execution renders the whole feature worthless. I have to track my time externally. That’s not good for an app that effectively mandates a paid subscription.

This app’s free features are so laughably limited that using it without a subscription is completely impractical. If they want to essentially force people to pay for a subscription (in not so many words) then it needs to be flawless, and it isn’t.

The app as a whole is good, but definitely run the free trial before committing.

title: Latest update has terrible UX
body:
Edit: Updating back to 5 stars because the UX has been improved, I’m sure many people enjoy the fancy UI but there is now an option to have a no frills. I have had some issues with habit data not saving properly for the current day, though, when checking habits off sometimes

Old review:
I agree with some other reviews I’ve seen: this was an update for the sake of updating. It has “fixed” things that were not broken to begin with. The UI used to be minimal and easy to use day to day, but now forces its paradigm of time-of-day habits. Sure, I have some habits for the evening, but a lot of anyone’s habits aren’t strictly for one time of day. It is more difficult now to just get this app to show me what I want—a simple list of my habits for the day. All day habits are now all the way to the left, the app has unneeded animations for what it is (essentially just a simple to do list style app), and the bottom bar UI now centers on adding a new habit, which is one of the actions I’ve used the least. This is making me regret subscribing to this. Maybe I can find a different app that is just simple and elegant, and doesn’t get in my way.
