title: Slick UI, Little Substance
body:
Everything looks great in the UI, but it actually doesn’t functionally behave like a goal tracker. 

For example, here’s how I would track “learning algebra” through the UI description provided by Productive

“I want to have 8 reps of studying algebra repeated every week as often as once every week” 

Now in actually tracking that goal on day 1 I enter in I’ve done two reps for learning algebra. (In my case these correspond to pomodoros). Now day 2 comes around and I want to track more Algebra. That goal has been removed by Productive. I can’t input any additional Algebra studying on day 2. Why? Because Productive makes bad assumptions about how you’re using the app, highly constricted to its views about what goal tracking is. So if you didn’t get all the reps for algebra in on Day 1 well you just have to wait another week. Bruh..

So for as pretty as this app is, don’t expect anything more than a elevated to-do list. Don’t buy this.
author: Adam Smoove

title: Free version is unusable
body:
This app bills itself as a free app with optional in-app purchases, but that’s a complete misrepresentation. The app is almost unusable without a subscription. It’s a complete money grab. Literally every time you navigate away from it or change screens, it directs you to pay for a subscription. 

The subscription page that pops up every five seconds is set up in a misleading way that indicates a “free trial” (that auto-subscribes you for a full year’s price) is the only option to continue using the app for free. You can X out of the subscription page in the top left corner without agreeing to the trial, but people who aren’t tech literate won’t realize that.

I downloaded the app because my mother wanted to use it but couldn’t get it to work. As soon as I saw the subscription page, I asked my mother if she’d known she could skip it without starting a trial, and she told me no, she’d hit the obvious yellow button that said “free trial” instead. I helped her cancel her subscription and delete the app. There are much more functional free productivity apps out there that run on ads without tricking people into thinking they need a recurring subscription to use them.

title: Great UI but buggy (updated: might be iOS issue)
body:
It’s pretty intuitive at first, but when you get deeper into customization, you run into oddities and bugs. For example, it seems to be pretty aggressive about resetting streaks when you make edits to habits (understandable, but the rules around this could be more clear). You edit a habit name, and it reorders it. Sometimes things don’t get saved. Sometimes they get reordered at seemingly unpredictable times. 

And worse, I’ve only just fully set up a bunch of habits, and all of a sudden my Today shows up blank, rendering the app useless because I can’t actually see or complete the habits I spent so much time setting up. It worked well when it was working, but I am less than a month into using Productive and now it’s broken.

Update: Rebooting my iOS device seemed to fix the issue so I just raised my original rating to 4. I also had noticed another app having issues (Alarmy wasn’t showing an alarm going off), so I’m tentatively chalking at least the major issue above to an iOS problem and not a Productive one. Will report back if other issues persist or not.

title: Works well, but expensive
body:
First off, I hate hate HATE that this is a subscription based app, and doesn’t just use a one-time payment. And the monthly cost is relatively high as well.

The functionality of the app isn’t bad, but the price is completely unjustified. Since using it, I’ve found other apps under the Productivity category that do everything this app does and more, and only charge a one-time payment that is even less than this app charges per month.

The free use of this app is just an illusion as well.
First off, the app REQUIRES you to subscribe to start using it. You can choose a 1-week free trial as your subscription and then cancel it, but the actual free version at that point is so stripped of features that there’s no longer any point to it.
Second, if you don’t cancel the free trial before the week is up, either because you forget about it or just don’t mind paying to try it another month, it automatically charges you for a FULL YEAR.
No where in the app does it tell you that it defaults to charging you for an entire year in advance once the trial is up. The only way you can find out is either by getting charged, or seeing your subscription price when you go into your device subscriptions list to cancel it.

I’d bet this app makes most of its money by underhandedly charging people for a year in advance once their trial runs out. As far as I know, that isn’t even something that can be refunded which makes it all the more malicious.

Just use one of the many superior and reasonably priced apps instead, which aren’t run by sociopaths.

title: Save Your Money with the Due App
body:
Pretty disappointed after 2-3 days of using this app, I was less likely to do the tasks I set out to do because the notification system was so weak. I was hoping for an app that would make me more likely to do things like reading or journaling, and this app just wasn’t useful.

I recently paid $6.99 or so for the “Due” app, a one time charge for a persistent reminder app, while it doesn’t track my “streaks”, I can go back and look at my completed tasks.

For this app to be worth $30+ a year, there have to be more features than setting a notification, and tracking the frequency of completion. I’m frustrated that I could select a date for which I wanted a particular habit to begin-for example, putting $ into my savings account after my paycheck is deposited. Setting that habit alert to begin on my next pay day makes a lot more sense than just setting it as a biweekly goal with no set date to remind me. This goal gets lost in the shuffle.

If there were more meaningful, specific notifications that didn’t need to be set up separately as an add on option in the additional settings, I’d be more likely to use this app. If this app allowed me to snooze/reschedule, or just had more cool features, I might consider paying $12 a year, but no way would I ever pay $29.99 for a glorified reminder app.

title: Good and Bad
body:
I have a love/hate relationship with his app. I’ve used it for years and it has helped me to build some great habits. When the app works, it’s the best tool out there. I’m not a fan of subscription models, but thankfully I got in early enough so that my premium purchase carried over, which is much appreciated. 

The problem is that this app often fails to work properly. Over the last few years of use, there have been numerous stretches where the notifications and reminders simply stop working after an update. A habit app that doesn’t remind you of your goals is simply useless. I have contacted the developer a few times with the same response: “we are aware and working on a fix.” I appreciate that, but when the same issues reappear constantly, there’s something wrong with the development process. 

I wish this app were better. I want it to be better. But sadly, it’s mediocre at best.

title: Poor Syncing
body:
I love the look and general functionality of the “Productive” app, but the syncing from one mobile device to another is extremely slow. Make a change on my iPhone and it might take an hour or more for the change to appear on my iPad Pro with the devices sitting next to each other. The reverse is also true. 

Quitting and then re-opening the app multiple times on each device appears to help but obviously that’s a hassle and shouldn’t be necessary. At the same moment, my “Things 3” app will do that syncing right before my eyes (in 10 seconds or less).

I emailed Apalon support and their response was to describe the requirements for syncing which I had met from the beginning. Nothing was said about knowing they have an issue, implying that it is was just me, which I doubt. I recently retired from 25 years in hi-tech and was a teacher at Apple for more than 8, so I generally know what I’m doing with apps and devices. 

Mobile app syncing delays of over an hour are unacceptable in 2020. Support team, please respond to this review and tell users whether this issue is being addressed. I’ll give you 5 star ratings and high praise when you fix the syncing. Thank you!

Update on 5/4/2020: Received a reply from the developer (Apalon) today, but it’s likely just a form letter. Nothing said about my specific concern. Just a general statement that the company is sorry for the inconvenience, and that they are always trying to improve their app. On the bright side, at least I got a reply even if it’s from a computer rather than a real person. Ah, the world we live in these days.

title: Great concept, a little glitchy
body:
Second Edit: The app crashed until I uninstalled it and reinstalled. Best guess it that I had it passcode enabled and that wired to Face ID. Don’t do that. In fact, it hasn’t misbehaved at all since removing the passcode. Some horrible person might see my habits, but at least *I* can see them. 

Original review:

I’ve been using this for a couple of days, which is plenty of time to get the gist: the concept is clear and very well implemented. The somewhat cartoonish UI works for me—I find that the visuals give a pleasing sense of space to the UI and make it seem friendly—but you may find it, well, cartoonish. If you can’t abide it, turn on “minimalist interface” in settings. It’s perfectly functional and still attractive. 

It can nag you mercilessly if you want it to, or it can be quieter. It accommodates one-off tasks seamlessly. For the timing of habits, dividing the day into morning, afternoon, evening, and all day is simple and reflects how we experience our days. You can also time the bejeezus out of your tasks, giving them multiple timers and target occurrences—a “goal” in their nomenclature. Being able to pause tasks is welcome and also reflects facts on the ground. The canned quick-start tasks are thoughtful and meaningfully organized. All good. 

The app has also been glitchy, both on an iPhone and an iPad. Occasionally it hangs on the loading screen; once in a while it elects not to display the list of habits, although it correctly counts them as you scroll horizontally through the parts of the day.  Not deal breakers, but curious behavior for  an app running on modern hardware.

And syncing appears to poll at a leisurely pace, so updates may take a while to propagate across devices.

title: Developers Begging to Buy
body:
I have maybe written 2 reviews in nearly 12 years of using the App Store. They were positive. This is negative. When you open the app they spam you to buy. Close the prompt. Try it out first, before I buy, like we all do. Second pop up to purchase with a count down timer for a “deal.” Close it. Click a few more buttons. Another purchase prompt. Close. Another. Close it. Pick it up the next day. Pop up to buy. Close. Another and another and another and another and another. 

Let me be clear, the app seems WONDERFUL. I would gladly buy it. Worth $15-30 a year? YES! But this begging. I’ve never seen anything like it. I suppose they do it because it works. That’s sad. At this point, I wouldn’t buy it for .05 cents just on principle. *if your app is good people will buy it; if you must spam and beg at this level adherence to stick with it must be low*

title: Helping my life
body:
As someone who with ADD, a tool like this is super important.   Building routines and habits gives me some effectiveness, and this app helps me do that.  

I would like to see these enhancements:

   1.  An “at a glance view” of the entire month where you can see all the habits you have scheduled.  My therapist likes to see a summary of what I’m doing and when and I feel a quick zoom out of the entire month would help here.  

2.  The export feature is not working.  I get some Json structure but it’s all blank.  Would be fun to integrate the data on my own personal apps or other apps 

3.  Custom name tags assigned to the colors (like Trello has).  An important use case for that would be assigning the different role categories to the habits you create.  Roles of your life, for example “Husband, Father, Manager,  Personal”.  As explained in “The 7 Habits of Highly Effective  People”, categorizing your tasks this way helps make sure you keep appropriate balance in the different offices of your life.  Sure you can keep track of that mentally by different colors.  But naming those those colors gives nice explicit reinforcement.

4.  More icons for the habits.  (Current ones a great though)

title: Good idea, buggy implementation, annoying “resets”
body:
I downloaded the app earlier in January, and really liked it on my iPhone so I ended up buying the annual subscription to get the extra features.

I really like how it keeps track of my habits and reminds me to do stuff, but I find it very inflexible in terms of changing your habits as you go (which I would think is a very valid use case).

Say, for example, you start with do something x times a week; after a while, you may want to do that more frequently.

The app lets you change that, but then seems to delete all the previous entries (with a non-so-specific prompt because it tells you it will “update the stats”, not that it will “delete the stats”), which is pretty infuriating.
I would rather it resets the stats but keeps the entries if it cannot handle different stats for different periods of time (based on goal changes).

Outside of the resetting-habits issue, there is another issue which makes it a bit more annoying to use: the app never syncs with my other devices (iPad) through iCloud, even though the setting is supposedly “on”, on both iPad and iPhone, tried to enable/disable a few times to no avail, and email support wasn’t that helpful in telling me to try things they have in the FAQ section which I’ve already tried before contacting them.

Especially considering this is a paid app (can’t really think that most people can effectively use the free version), I would expect some higher quality there.

title: Sad Fall from Grace
body:
I ditto the recent reviews about all the problems. It’s sad because this use to be the undisputed best app for habits...
I don’t know if there’s a new developer or what, but I’ve never seen an app go from quality to crap so quickly. 

They keep adding beautiful design and wonderful features without testing it  out at all. Every update something new breaks, and it’s finally surpassed the annoying phase and entered the completely non-functional phase. 

This app is essentially like using... a Ferrari without an engine... a computer without a CPU... a bike without wheels... etc. 

They have had 5 separate updates since the 2.0 bug-filled design refresh, and every single time something different breaks: 

- First, the streaks were lost. I said fine, at least I can still check off habits daily.
- Next, the apple watch app stopped working. I said fine, at least I can still use the phone app.
- Then the app slowed down to the point where I had to wait 45 seconds to check off a habit. I said whatever, I already paid for it, might as well use it.
- Now, all my habits are paused and cannot be resumed no matter what I do. I literally CANNOT USE BASIC FUNCTIONALITY of the app. 

I even emailed offering to be a beta tester, and was given a generic reply that didn't address my specific email. 

Apalon should offer some reward/compensation to their paying subscribers for sticking with them through this 4 month fiasco. 

I like many others really loved this app, and perhaps I've been naive to ignore all the missteps. But it's finally dawned on me... I'm paying for a premium product that malfunctions more than any free app on my phone. 

I already emailed them numerous times about issues and I recently paid for an extra year. I don't know what else to do :(

body:

I’ve been using the premium app for about seven months and there have already been at least three times when I’ve had to resort to paper tracking to keep up my habits.

To the development team: date math is hard. You need a quality assurance team. Do unit tests and beta testing. Don’t be in such a rush to push new features out the door. In order to make habits stick, your users need stability. The updates released in the last seven months that broke things have all because you’ve been too hasty to push out an unnecessary feature.

I am canceling my subscription.

title: Do NOT trust this app for long term goals
body: If you want an app that you can trust with your personal growth, this is not the app. I used this app to track some very personal and meaningful growth, with over 820 days (that's over 2 years!) of perfect days. I succeeded in meeting my goals Every. Single. Day. for more than two years. What happened? Apalon made an update and wiped my data. I'm now back at zero. I'm devastated. My stomach is in my throat. Do not make the mistake I did in trusting them with your goals. Do not trust them to track your progress. Use Google calendar, or a physical journal, or anything else. Do not trust them long term. It might work today, or day 800, but eventually you will wake up and find your progress gone and with it your sense of accomplishment! Note: I did reach out to support. They replied after a day, saying "We're working on it." From there I didn't hear from them. I have emailed them two more times, without a word back, which was over a week ago. I'm beyond heartbroken. Again, do not trust this app for any of your long term goals, you will regret it. Eventually they will destroy your data.

title: Used to be good app
body:
Update(19-feb) : 
It’s been three weeks since the sorting habits is broken . After spending a long valuable time sorting the habits , it’s really unacceptable to see them go back to random order again . How long will it take it fix issues which were once working fine ? 

Original review :
I am a paid member of the app for a few
Months now and been a regular user . The app used to be simple and very useful , where you can create new habits and sort it with ease,  I used as my reference to get an idea of how my day must be sequenced.  . A recent update completely broke the sorting functionality and completely jumbled up all the habits that I had kept sorted until now . I contacted support and reported this . I got a response on how to fix it again . I spent 30 mins  to sort all the habits manually once again as it was broken by the update. But once I went to another screen in the app and back , the sorting went away again and it’s all jumbled up again  . This is Extremely careless of them especially for something people pay lots of  money for.  

Another clear indicator of their carelessness is when you go read their version history - none of them describe what the actual changes in the new version is . They copy paste the same genetic description  for every version .

Updated:

Tried twice more to reorder my habits , and it again went back to jumbled state . I have spent 1 hr so far just to sort the habits but giving up

title: Not worth the $$
body:
At first i was excited to use this app. It seemed exactly what i was looking for. A task management app that would operate daily to keep me on my toes when needed. If you’re considering this app, let me break it down:

Consistency: If you are going to be actively on it, daily, and i mean daily.. then this may be for you. It’s an app that organizes reminders (basically). When you’re active on the app, then it will be active with their reminders too.  If you’re not active, unfortunately, the reminders are inconsistent. Sometimes they’re often, sometimes they’re not. If you’re someone who forgets to do something, for literally a day, then forget it. The moment you stop, This app will NOT follow up and hold you accountable to your tasks. You will end up going days without using the app. A waste of money. 

If you like analytics, you can see your performance overtime. I like that. However, still a 4 star app at most. 

Overall, this is Something you can save $$ by doing it yourself in your phone. Set your own reminders in your phone with alarms and that will be more consistent then this app. At the end of the day, i would prefer to have my money back then use the app. This may be for some, but for me, it’s a hard NO right now. 

Good luck and Enjoy!

title: Great focused tool, one minor gripe: surface the Notes, please
body:
I have been using Productive for about 2 years and I find its focus on repeating habits generallywell thought out. I use it most days for key reminders. The interface is clear and easy to use. I think for the vast majority of people looking for a habit tracker, it’s great. 

The one minor criticism is that in a recent update, the Notes field has gotten buried in the interface and I have to work consciously to find it. 

I might be an edge case, but I use the Notes field for several of my habits to review key aspects of the habit. For example, I keep a daily habit of reviewing people in my life who have some sort of challenge: I want to see their name and their challenge so I can decide if I need to check in or do something. 

To get to the Notes field now I have to make 3 presses: 

1. Click on the Habit detail (>).
2. I have to look around the details page, see nothing that looks like a note, and remember to click on the ellipsis (...) on the upper right of the screen.
3. Click the Notes icon. 

That’s 3 clicks and several seconds of having to remember where to look for the notes. I wish the Notes were surfaced more easily, such as 

One other minor observation: when I have a Notes field visible, the new interface with the big blue + symbol obscures the last line or two of the notes: I have to physically drag the note upward to be able to see the last two lines, then they spring back below the blue + symbol. This seems intrusive and counter-productive to me: if I open the notes, I want to see the notes. 

I think if the Notes interface issues I outline above were fixed, I’d give this application 5 stars.

Thanks.

For example, I have been trying to get better at Spanish I have a habit set for each morning. That’s all fine and well, but now that I’m really getting into it I would like to change it to twice a day, once at night and still once in the morning. title: Best purchase I’ve made on the AppStore.
body:
This app succeeds where physical, paper planners fail. Over the last 15 years or so I’ve bought many planners and notebooks geared towards tracking goals and staying on task, and I’d use them for a few months (if that) and they’d get retired to a desk drawer to be forgotten. I’ve decided the reason these fail me, or I fail them, is because they are so tedious. This app takes the tedious work out of the equation.

My favorite things about it:

The repeating of tasks.

I can make tasks repeat on specific days or  x amount of times per week or even biweekly.
Reminders and timers.

I can set several reminders and even a duration.
Tracking progress motivates me. (Really, it’s the best.)

A habit I track is “No soda today!” I have that set for evening daily and if I made it the day with no soda, I mark it as done. It tracks all my successful days. But if I have one, I skip it, it breaks the streak, and here’s the thing: in the past this would have really de-motivated me to cut back, but with this I see right there that I was able to go however many days, which doesn’t allow me to forget my success and I know I can do it again, and I want to. I love love love that. 
The design/interface.

The colors are nice, the style is minimal, you aren’t overwhelmed with text and nothing is an eyesore. 
Siri Compatibility.

What I would like to change/see added:

Categories.

Ability to create categories to assign habits to if I want, and a page to view just those categories. It would allow us to isolate just Exercise, or just Skin Care, etc. That would help me a lot. 

Overall, I think this app is great in every way. The yearly premium price of $30 is consistent with the cost of the cute planners on Etsy, only those pale in comparison to the abilities, ease, and potential of the app. It’s a great value and I highly recommend it.

title: update regrets.
body:
I had LOVED this app from day one. I began using it not long after the release years ago. This evening I updated the app and am extremely upset about the changes. 

• The format is very different. I don’t know how to best describe it. One word would be complicated. Another is perplexing; why is there a sloth (?), trees, a sun, birds, a moon, ... ? Why did they get rid of the minimalistic list on a single ‘page’? The format is mind-blowing (and not in a positive way). 
• I can no longer find the setting that gives me the option which background color I want. Now, it is dark grey/black by default. I hope I am missing something. And because of the grey background, my icons can no longer be grey. 
• I reset all of my stats to zero yet the app displays that I’ve had 27 perfect days from January 1-31, 2020. Today is January 1, 2020. I have not marked a single habit as complete and I have not traveled to the future and back.
• All of my weekly habits are not displaying as they did before. Some are simply not there. Yet they are listed in the habit menu.

title: Please untorpedo the interface
body:
Thank you for fixing the weekly habits bug. I got my streak back.

The minimalist interface option is a nice thought, and I appreciate it, but it doesn’t actually fix the problem. The sloth isn’t the issue. I like the sloth, it’s adorable. It’s not the sloth that makes the interface unnecessarily complicated, it’s the layout.

I don’t reliably check in with this app during every section of every day. I don’t have time for that. I check in the morning to see what my day looks like and in the evening to make sure I marked everything I did. I always need to see my full day schedule and I never need to see separate pages for afternoons and stuff. It keeps opening into the morning section instead of the full day, giving me an incorrect idea of what my day needs to look like.

Your product description suggests this app may be helpful to adults with adhd. Please think about what that user experience might be like for a user with attention and focus issues. You open the app, you see what looks like your full day schedule. You forget to check whether it’s actually your morning schedule instead. You think you have your day sorted. You happen to open the app in the late afternoon. You’re now panicking because you to-do list is not what you thought it was. Swiping around through a day is a huge extra step, and it’s pretty disorienting.

It’s a shame because the simplicity of the interface was what set this app apart from the competition. It’s why it was my top recommendation for habit tracking apps.

I’d really love to see a minimalist interface that’s actually minimalist as an interface instead of the same overly complicated multipart swipe mess but without the art. I liked the art. I want a minimalist option with only a daily list and none of this swiping around to get to it, or the horrible possibility of accidentally swiping off of it into a different view without noticing.

I’d rather like to keep the sloth though if it’s all the same. It’s really adorable.

title: Pretty helpful, kind of frustrating at times
body:
So, overall I like the app and will continue using it.  There’s just a few quirks that kind of irritate me at times. 

1) The display and graphics are just a little too “cute” for my taste.  I find that all the encouraging phrases, sunrise diagrams and rainbows are distracting from the point of the app.  It’s supposed to help you accomplish habits...I don’t want any frills to get in the way.  

2) The second issue is that if you change anything about a habit, you lose all stats on it.  So for example, if you have a habit that used to be “anytime” and you want to change it to an “evening” habit, you lose all previous completion stats.  Why is that?  It makes it feel like you can’t really edit habits, you’re actually just deleting it and starting new because you now have no stats to look back on, which is honestly pretty discouraging.  

So yeah, it’s a helpful app and I’ll probably keep using it, but if I come across something better that’s more professional looking and allows for more customization, I’ll probably switch over.

title: Version 2.0. Not so good
body:
12/20/2019: Well, the developers released a whole new layout for this app, and in doing so kinda ruined it. Now I have this useless sun and moon graphic at the top of the screen, which is pretty much a waste of space. Additionally, I now have four lists to manage and have to keep sliding left and right between them. Completely useless. 

But there is more. Lots of the menu options don’t work, and...  when you upgrade you’re existing habits will not all display correctly. Say bye bye to any streaks you had. If you really need your data for anything important, you’ll want to get it out of this app. 

While I’m always open to improvements and change, this app has taken a step backwards when it comes to appearance and usability. It’s unfortunate. Between the new layout and the apps continuously occurring bugs, like a few with every release, I cannot recommend this app any longer. 🙁

————————————————————

11/12/2019 Update: DO NOT TURN ON PASSCODE LOCK, it causes the app to crash at startup. Customer service was responsive to my emails for help, but ultimately I fixed the startup problem myself. Deleted the app and reinstalled. After reinstall, all my data was gone, but after leaving the app open for a few minutes, it synced to iCloud and everything was back. Note, I had iCloud sync turned on prior to app breaking, so my data was already in the cloud. 3 stars as this issue really shouldn’t have happened to begin with. Again, turning on passcode lock caused the app to crash startup, the don’t turn it on. 

11/09/2019: Well, the latest update has rendered this app unusable. It crashes at start up every time on iOS12. Useless...

title: Train Wreck
body:
This app was fantastic, and a cornerstone of my life. After all, I use it to organize my day every day.

And then something happened. They released a new version: a slow motion, unending train wreck beyond imagination. They apparently did no testing whatsoever before unleashing the new version on its unsuspecting users.

One of the key features what is the ability to put the habits in order. For example, you might 1) get dressed, then 2) go to work. The ability to sort habits is broken, this is a known defect, and this defect renders the app useless. If for example, my daily plan starts with 1) go to sleep, then 2) clear email, that makes no sense.

But the worst defect is when it started deleting all my daily habits. I put a lot of time and care into designing these: The name, icon, color, and daily order.

Then all my habits suddenly vanished. Not only did I lose a valuable tool that was the cornerstone of my day, but I had to go through that work all over again. I added my habits to the app again, and they disappeared again.

Again, this is a known defect. Their tech-support is prompt, and any problem they will reply to you and tell you “we are aware of the problem and we are working on it.” 

But that doesn’t help, and the problems persist. It might be OK to release an app for buying wine, or editing selfies, that has bugs. But when your app is called productive, and I’m assuming for example used by people in business, it is inexcusable to release such a buggy app.

I finally gave up and deleted the app. I might try it again -Cautiously - say in six months, when they have gotten their act together, and actually bother to test out the app before they unleash it on their users.

title: Clean, Simple, Effective with One Design Flaw
body: Productive is a simple app for building effective habits. It easily lets you create custom, repeating to do lists and track your completion. It was exactly what I was looking for without anything I did not want. My only complaint is that several months ago they added the feature to see what tasks are due tomorrow, but those tasks cannot be completed until tomorrow. While this makes some sense, the app has no problem letting you complete tasks after the day they were due. I like this feature and use it to catch up when I fall behind, but I hate that I can’t get even a day ahead when I know I have a busy stretch coming up. It’s almost as if the app is subtly designed to support you when you fall behind, which is great, but not encourage you to proactively avoid falling behind in the first place, which is unfortunate.

title: Well designed with spotty execution
body: I’ve been using this app (with premium features) for years because I haven’t found another app that is as good as this one for tracking habits. That being said I’ve looked long and hard for an alternative. My issues with the app are 1) in that it has below average integration across devices. I have an iPad and it doesn’t load all of the habits from the phone into the tablet. It will load some but not all. It also takes forever (if it will do it at all) to sync with me marking a habit on one device. Example. I marked a habit complete around midday on the phone and the iPad app never registered it so it still showed up as incomplete in the iPad. And 2) if you’re relying on it for an accurate “perfect streak” count look elsewhere or track with a red X on a calendar. You can have a million perfect days in a row and the app arbitrarily decides to not track some days in the streak. Which is weird because the counter for “days complete” is accurate but the streak counter is completely random. Again. Best I’ve found and does a lot of things right. But I’ve also been looking for an alternative for a while.

title: I wish it had a skip function without penalty
body: I like this app.  I have been using it daily for a couple of weeks.  Every day, when I complete my tasks, I enjoy marking them as done.  If I don’t get around to doing a task, I break my streak.  That’s fine.  But what about days when I’m traveling?  I can’t do some tasks because I’m not at home.  I have no way to tell the app, that this task should not be counted for today.  I can only mark it “done” which feels wrong when I didn’t do it.  Or I can “skip” it, which breaks my streak, which feels unfair since it wasn’t possible.  It needs an “excused” choice.  Some way to say I didn’t do it, so don’t give me credit, but I also didn’t fail to do it, so don’t penalize me.

I have been using this app for about four years now; two years on my old Android phone and now two years on my new iPhone. (Though I didn’t transfer over the habits from my past phone so that is why I only say two years of progress was lost.)
This is extremely frustrating as I had a long streak going only to have the slate wiped clean. I have contacted the developers in the past about recovering broken chains before (as one day, I marked every habit as done except for one and didn’t realize it until about two weeks later) but they said they cannot do anything to recover the chain. 
So I am going to uninstall the app. I really loved this one and think it is very helpful but the developers should consider implementing a recovery program in case glitches like this happen again in the future.

title: It was my go-to for years! Until...
body: I’ve had this app since 2016. It really helped me get back on my feet during a difficult time, so to me, it was a game changer. It was one of my most reliable apps, but alas it has one major flaw that made me look elsewhere for a habit tracker 4 years later. Recently I got an iPad and two Apple Watches, and the syncing between devices just wasn’t smooth at all. Sometimes it didn’t happen altogether. The iPad was left out most of the time, and when that happened, it usually ended in habits being duplicated on all the devices. It also took some effort to get it to sync when I switched watches in the morning - on the watch it would say “syncing” and nothing would happen until I messed with it on my iPhone. This process would take me 10+ minutes. Overall, this is a great app if you only use it on one device, but across several devices, some major bugs still need to be fixed.

That alone helps me not to feel overwhelmed, which is a problem I have with the everyday mundane stuff I usually put off. I love how you can very simply change the order of your habits without inputting the the time they need to be done- I don't like the pressure of racing the clock for mundane stuff. And if you do need reminders, you have the option to create them for each habit. If you fall for this “trap of an app” by making both the mistake of initially downloading it and forgetting to unsubscribe from automatic renewals before deleting, you will need to request a refund from Apple Support as developers don’t have control over account payments - how convenient for them.  

My request for a refund was denied immediately despite going to support the day of the charge. I also submitted an accidental subscription renewal, and have yet to hear back or see my money returned.  Until I do, or if I don’t, I won’t be using and/or trialing apps from this developer moving forward.

title: Great Tool
body:
This app has helped me, far more than any other on the App Store, to take control of my life. It has been especially useful in creating a healthy lifestyle, and to conquer depressive habits I had never been able to. 

The accountability the app brings is one that is lacking in pressure. If you end up not being able to complete a habit, you don’t get negative feedback. Most habit forming apps on the App Store have negative feedback when you are unable to meet your goals, which can become quickly frustrating and cause more self-criticism. Other apps on the market will send an obnoxious amount of reminders, that eventually become easy to ignore. Rather the app uses as many, or as little, reminders as you want. You can choose which days of the week and what time of day the habits need completed by. With the Premium feature, you are able to create as many habits as you want and gain access to more fun settings. For me, the amount I paid for the yearly subscription was worth it for the changes I have seen in my life.

The only problems I have found is in the weekly section. You don’t get the option of choosing the day of the week for habits in the weekly tab. I have a plant I water every two weeks, always on Saturday’s, but there is currently no way to specify this option. Because I can find no other problems, and because of the personal help this app has provided, I am giving it 5 stars.

title: Now only 3 habits for free. Down from 5.
body:
So I don’t normally write reviews but I thought I would mention something about this app because of how unusable it is in the free version. I see a review from Jun 24th of this year that complains that you could only make 5 free habits in the free version of this app. Apparently in the months since then this company thought that was too generous and have now lowered that to 3 habits total. 

While they can totally do that within their rights, everything about this app screams money hungry. Going from 5 to 3 habits is one. The other is that they deceptively try and sign you up for a subscription by saying that it’s free. They also prompt you to subscribe every 3-4 screens. They also limited LIGHT MODE to a paid feature. Are you serious? 

I’m an iOS developer and I know exactly how little effort it takes to build light mode and dark mode into an app. The design is nice but the features are not worth nearly what they’re asking for it.

Eventually they will make it so that you can open this app make 1 goal and then they’ll only show you the subscription screen. They would be so much better off if they just charged once to everyone for a lite version of the app (say 10 habits) and then premium subscribers get unlimited habits. This is not a $15 per year app (the 50% discount they offer everyone). Please do yourselves a favor and don’t try and nickel and dime your users. It’s just super distasteful and makes people upset.

I understand that subscriptions are a much more stable business model and that they’re the way that Apple is suggesting apps go. I also understand that the work that has gone into making this app look and feel clean and crisp is harder than some may assume. It’s difficult to design simply. Unfortunately this app doesn’t get to shine like it could because of the business decisions for marketing it.

title: Helps establish new routines
body: This app is very helpful with establishing and tracking new routines. I enjoy the color scheme, and the ease of swiping a task right or left to indicate if it has been completed or skipped for good reason (such as being out of town). I included some basic things that I’m already good at doing (taking vitamins and medication every day) so that I will always have something to mark as completed, in order to give me momentum, and to stack my habits. From what I can tell, the highest frequency you can track is 3 times a day. If you want to track number of ounces of water you drank, or how many times you did something else, I don’t see a way to do that. The Tally app would be better for that. Also, I like the any.do app for tracking and scheduling one-time tasks, including projects with multiple subtasks. For making and tracking big goals, Strides might be the app for you. Having recently entered a new phase of life, this app, Productive, is my app of choice for creating and tracking good habits and routines.

title: Getting worse with every “update”
body:
I’ve been using this app since the “premium” version was a one-time optional payment. It was simple, clean, and did the job of counting how many times I completed a given task. Lately, it’s been degrading harshly as the developers try to add silly bells and whistles. 

- Items I have scheduled to do X days per week “break” their streak every Sunday.
- Two items duplicated themselves for no reason. 
- All day today, since updating the app, “Today” has been tomorrow and everything I’ve yet to do today is marked as missed. 

Stop adding pointless “improvements” to an app that worked just fine before - you’re breaking it. I want my streaks to carry over week to week more than I want an annoying “way to go” pop-up every 50 item completions.

UPDATE: I just changed how many times I wanted to do something in a week (which I do frequently with some items for my own reasons) and ALL my previous data for that task (HUNDREDS of completions) has been erased!! What are you doing?!

UPDATE 2: Just had a reminder chime (at 23:30) for a task for which I never set a reminder. And there’s no way to delete it! You’ve completely broken what used to be a fine app. At this point, the only reason I haven’t given up on you is the hundreds- and thousands-long streaks of which I’d like to keep a record.

author: hja91

title: Just wait for iOS 13 Reminders update.
body:
The app functions properly, as in its not glitchy or broken, but this is like a Palm-Pilot-era reminders app, with no in-depth features or capability. It’s basically Apple’s Reminders with the ability to see how many times you’ve completed each task on a calendar. It’s absolutely not worth the deceptively high subscription fees. (I say deceptive because they threw 3 different prices for the same thing at me within 2 minutes of opening the app). It doesn’t even have simple features like proper cross-device syncing or a library of tasks to choose from. That’s right, you have to create every task completely from scratch, just like Apple’s Reminders, just like a PDA from 2003, down to manually choosing things like background colors and icons pulled from some free to use clip art gallery. 

I would have just deleted it and moved on but they have some sleazy hoops to jump through when you open it for the first time that aim to trick you into signing up for a “free trial” that auto-renews a week later for $30. If you don’t fall for it then they throw another screen at you offering the same thing for $15 (but only if you take the deal within 59 minutes, lol). They even put a countdown clock ON THE HOME SCREEN of the app after that like those awful Clash of Clans type games 🙄

So yeah, those practices rubbed me the wrong way so I felt inclined to leave this completely honest review about what this app is and isn’t. 

Bottom line, if you’re interested in paying a premium price for a full featured and innovative productivity app then there are MUCH better options available. Better yet, just wait a couple weeks and use the improved version of Reminders in iOS 13.

title: Really annoyed 🙄
body: Ugh is all I can say for this app. I downloaded this thinking it was going to change my life and make me a better person. But unfortunately, the only lives changing here are the ones of people that pay the app for more habits. I could only create like three or four habits until it reached the limit. That really annoyed me, and it's the reason I gave this app one star. But to be honest with myself and the developers, without the habit limit, I probably would have given this app five stars. This app really has a lot of potential, and I have nothing against the developers, it's just that this app didn't live up to its potential. First up, you all know my good friend the habit limit, the layout also is one of my worst enemies, I hate simple layouts, even though I know most people love them, and I'm not quite satisfied with the way the icons work, maybe instead of icons, you could maybe have a drop down box with topics like "Workout" or "Around the house" on it, and it would immediately add an icon to the side of a habit, it would just be easier than looking through each icon and seeing which one corresponds with a specific habit. One more thing I need to complain about, who needs a to-do list app anyway? The only thing u might need it for is the notifications. But u could literally just take a pad and paper and be done with it! Like seriously! But there is one good thing we can salvage from this wreck of an app, and it's the coloring. I know, so LOOOWWW, but I love the black background and the standard colors, I might not love simple layouts, but I love simple colors. That's all I have to say for this app, and I wouldn't recommend it for someone who isn't willing to spend money on something you could do on a pad and paper. Sorry, but this app could have been so much better, but it didn't live up to the expectations I had for it.

title: Deceptive Pricing
body:
Developer not honest about the price. The actual price, a $33.00/yr subscription - which you’re only told about upon downloading and starting the app- is way too high for this app.

UPDATE: as a business, when you are accused of wrongdoing or dishonest business practices - specifically deceptive pricing - the appropriate response is NOT to reply by stating the obvious ( i.e., “It is up to you to decide whether or not you want to get a subscription”...obviously it’s up to me, it’s my money) and ignore the consumer’s actual complaint or invite the consumer to purchase your other products (i.e., “You can always check out our other apps”...why would I want to purchase something else from the very same company that I just accused of wrongdoing or dishonest business practices??)  I’d appreciate it if you address the actual complaint of deliberately deceptive pricing - of which you have been accused several times by reviewers in the reviewer feedback. You can correct the situation by changing your dishonest practice of deceptive pricing - not by offering the user a canned, deliberately disingenuous response.

title: Buggy, buggy, and oh yeah, BUGGY!!!
body:
I downloaded this app and paid for a year subscription based on all the neat feature and thousands of positive reviews. After hours of setup and fine tuning of my habits I began to use it and thought it was pretty good. 

But then I tried to use the timer function for a habit. I had set the timer for a habit to 40 minutes and turned it on, and about m hour later I went in to check how much time was left since it felt like it had been too long. Turns out the timer doesn’t work it you leave the app or lock your phone. It just stops and then picks back up when you open the app again. I submitted feedback and was told they would consider adding the feature at some point. Why even bother in the first place guys?

Then as I used the app more and more, I found my habits were starting to show up randomly as “Overdue,” even though ALL previous days habits were marked “Done,” or “Skipped.” So I reset the stats and started over. Then it happened again, and then again this morning. 

You can’t be productive, with Productive, because you will spend all your time trying to figure out why the app is behaving erratically. Year subscription? Guess I’ll chalk it up to a learning experience, delete the app and go back to Reminders, which is getting an overhaul in iOS 13 anyway. Enjoy the $30 guys, you won’t get another dime from me ever.

They said ok we got your refund and cancelled your subscription but you’ll still have access to the premium you paid for. Which I’m still thinking is ONE YEAR. Next time I launch the app, it says “oh no, you’re premium has expired”. When I signed up and bought the premium, it did NOT say the $14.99 was monthly. It said $14.99 for ONE YEAR. So be aware. After I exited that page it asks if I want to turn on notifications for the app. I did not get an option to skip or exit out of this page, and as I just exited out of subscribing or starting a free trial I thought it VERY ODD that it was asking me about notifications. So I hit continue on the notification question. Again, I have not provided any agreement to sign up for a free trial and have NOT subscribed. I select I do not want notifications as at this point I just want to delete this app, but I first want to make sure this shady SHADY app didn’t somehow  set me up as subscribed without my consent. So after I made sure the notifications were turned off this app that I exited out of subscribing and did NOT request a free trial for, did NOT give consent or any of my personal information is now allowing me to set up tasks?!?! How is this possible when I did NOT subscribe or agree to a free trial?!?! Am I suppose to believe that this app is registering its downloaded as free trial participants and subscribing them upon downloading the app?!?! I certainly did NOT consent to that. I exited out of the question I want to delete the app. So my question is am I going to be charged for a subscription I did NOT consent to? Am I going to be charged for a subscription when asked if I wanted I deleted the screen? I truly hope I will not be charged for downloading an app, exiting out of a question about subscribing, and then selecting I don’t want notifications for an app I was trying to delete within ten seconds of downloading!

UPDATE:
After one week, I’m still really liking this app. The interface is appealing and easy to use once you figure out where all the features are. The notification flags are great for keeping me on task. My days have gone much more smoothly and my kids are getting really great at knowing what to expect during the day for the past week. We have far fewer struggles and see much better behavior from them. I’m Type B when it comes to schedules — even though I thrive with one, I have a hard time staying on task by myself. I’ve done yoga every morning for a week! I’ve even had enough time to go to the gym. By myself. With two kids at home with their dad. Seriously! So glad I found this app.

title: Good
body:
This is a good app. But it is lacking a few things:
- The ability to mark something as NOT done and thus dismiss it from your list for the day (or whatever period). This is the case for those habits you’re working on of NOT doing something (i.e. quitting something), and when you fail to NOT do whatever that is. It’s not helpful that they linger in your list all day until you can’t remember for sure anymore if you did or did not do the thing.
- Habit history should not reset when you make minor tweaks to the schedule—such as changing a habit from morning to afternoon. The app should kindly handle such adjustments rather than nuking your history as though you had changed from weekends to weekdays or something so drastic.

I’ve only been using this app for about a day, so I really can’t tell you anything about its usability, or whether it has bugs, or whether it’s going to work for 6 9/10 days and then poop out on the day that you start paying, I really have no idea about any of that.

title: (UPDATED) Poor sync, worse service ruins fantastic app for me
body:
The 6/3 “Developer Response” and private email I received are useless, so I lowered my star rating from 3-2.

I reached out via comments after many months of direct contact. I don’t know if the developers can’t or won’t solve the issue (hard to believe they can’t), but I’ve lost patience with their continued apologies, gratitude, and requests for more patience. 

I have yet to witness any  attempt to “resolve the situation.” In fact, now I’m not sure they even understand the problem as the email referred to making the sync work “faster” and “more reliably.” When something does not work AT ALL, both speed and reliability are irrelevant.

I received the private email Friday and replied immediately. The public “Developer Response” yesterday is the only info I’ve received since. Nothing is resolved. Is it even undertstood?

From the email:
“We do hope to come up with a solution that will fix the problem and improve your experience with the app!
Our team hopes for your understanding and patience.”

Nope. I’m out of patience and mostly because I sincerely do not understand.

--------------------
ORIG POST 5/30/19
I've been using Productive for a very long time--nearly three years. For the most part, I love it. When it works, it works very well. It's not nor should it be used as a task manager except for tasks that you want to become habitual. And for that, it totally works. I love getting that little rush of dopamine every time I check-off a habit or see my 96-day streak or whatever. Achieving a "perfect" day also is surprisingly not just satisfying but exciting. And I have found the recent updates to be very good too, particularly the new slider at the top to switch between the current part of the day versus the entire day.

I don't remember if the app already had the ability to sync via iCloud when I began using it, but I seem to remember it didn't. Instead, I believe it was added at some point, and I was so happy. Now, I could use Productive on both my iPhone and iPad seamlessly. And that was the case for quite a long time. And suddenly, it wasn't.

I would give Productive five stars if it wasn't for their inability to make the sync work correctly (in ways that every other app I have that syncs via iCloud appears to do seamlessly). But even worse is their piss-poor customer service around this issue. Not only have they been unable to solve/fix it, they have provided me with either damaging help or no help whatsoever.

I first encountered this problem between 6-9 months ago, I think. I contacted Apalon via their support email. On the plus side, they are very responsive; they generally replied within 24-48 hours. They suggested I make sure that iCloud sync was turned on. They suggested I delete the app from my iPad and reinstall it. Since it should be syncing to iCloud, the data will just repopulate. As the syncing had worked for a while, all the habits were listed on the iPad, but the historical data was incomplete because it wasn't receiving updates. And if I marked something complete on the iPad, it wouldn't affect the iPhone app. After deleting and reinstalling the iPad app, nothing came back. The app simply remained empty. 

Their next suggestion was to delete the iPhone app and reinstall, and again, nothing should be lost because it's syncing with my iCloud account, right? If you look at the options under "Manage iCloud," along with 'iCloud sync" are options to "Export data" and "Delete data." One might think that if you can export data, there might also be a way to later reimport that data. So I decided to export the data before deleting the app. I would say, "Good thing I did," because of course when I reinstalled the app on my iPhone, no data returned.

But then, when I contacted Apalon support again, and I told them that their suggestions hadn't worked, but I had exported my data and maybe they could tell me how to repopulate it to at least one of the apps, I received nothing more than an apology. They ignored my question about how to use the exported data. They wouldn't say it couldn't be imported. They just won't say anything. I've asked multiple times.

Eventually, I had to restart from scratch, and after doing so, the sync worked again. For a while. Until it didn't. I wrote them again, repeating what had happened before and asking about using the exported data. This time they made no suggestions. They just apologized again for the trouble and said they were looking into it and appreciated my patience. Well, that was over five months ago.

And then, suddenly, the syncing did begin to work again. For a while. And then in March, it again stopped. This time, I only deleted the iPad app, and upon reinstalling it noticed that if I added a task via the iPad app, that task WOULD sync back to the iPhone, and any changes made to THAT TASK on the iPhone would sync back to the iPad. However, any tasks that already existed on the iPhone still won't sync with the iPad, and any new tasks created on the iPhone won't populate to the iPad or sync. 

Obviously, I wrote Apalon about this again, and most recently, the response I received was as follows:

"We're deeply sorry that it takes such long time to fix the issue.

We do hope for your patience till we get this resolved.

Apologies once again and thank you for using our app."

I'm not a programmer, and I'm sure there's plenty I don't understand about what's happening under the hood. And yet, again, this is the only app that syncs via iCloud that I've ever had this kind of long-standing, unfixable issue with. And that maybe wouldn't bother me so much if Apalon would at least figure out a workaround (like, a way to reimport exported data?) or explain what's going on and why what must be a pretty basic part of Apple's developer kit is so broken on their app that they can't fix it.

It pains me to start over with a new habit app, but I think I'm finally ready to do so.

title: Game changer, or rather a habit changer
body:
To understand, I’m a 33...or is it 34...year old man who struggles with ADHD having been diagnosed in the early 90s when no one knew what ADD or ADHD was. Most still don’t, but many think they do. It’s a real condition and is hard to grasp what it’s like for most folks. But enough of that. 

I came across this app looking for a better Reminders app to help me track to-do lists and other idea lists which are scattered amongst Reminders, Keep, One Note, and Notes. I didn’t even know there were apps for “habits,” but I know I function better with structure and routine. 

As I’m getting older, and due to the stress of my career (law enf/public safety), it has gotten harder instead of easier. Some grow out of ADHD or at least the hyperactivity, but not me. I have weak coping skills compared to the additional stressors my career has induced over the years. I often hear, “Maybe this isn’t a good fit for you,” but have proven many wrong over the years. 

However, I’m struggling again and this app has been a true game changer. I only have to remember to check this app and with my wife’s old Apple Watch it has been a dream. 

I set every important thing I want done according to morning, noon, or night as well as once a week, two weeks, etc. 

By default, the app shows only the items for your current time such as morning habits. For example, waking up on time. Check. Eat breakfast, brush teeth, take meds, get dressed, walk dogs. Check—and so on. 

On Sunday evenings once a week I take the trash out. On Monday, anytime, I bring the empty can back behind the house. 

This app is great. I have a different app to keep track of To-Dos, but wish I could do that in this app as a separate feature or function. 

But for creating a routine and sticking to it for the most part...it definitely helps. I’m able to be as vague or as detailed as I want concerning my daily/weekly/monthly tasks and truly feel good checking them off. It also shows statistics on a per task/day/month basis so I can see my progress. It would take years of practice at the same routine for me to accomplish ALL of these things I add daily/weekly and never stray or forget them. 

With this app, it’s taken a week. My wife even said she’s noticed I’m a LOT more productive and she’s happier for it. 

No, this won’t solve ADHD or focusing issues. It will, however, aid in a powerful way that carrying a notepad and pen in my pocket each day (when I don’t leave it at home by accident), in a tremendous way. 

The only thing I ever have to do is one simple task: check my watch/phone. The rest of my regular day is laid out for me in a way I can do more with my time and just get things done. 

Sorry for the long review, but it’s been so effective I just had to share my experience. Feel free to use this as a testimonial. My name is Brandon by the way. And thank you!

body: When I see a new and interesting app I can’t help myself- I download and try it. But this is the app I always find myself coming back to ever since I first downloaded it about six years ago. No other app has been as easy to set up, enjoyable to use, or useful. And every time I come back to it there are more features! Useful features, too, not ones that make things more difficult or overwhelming: they integrate smoothly into what is already there. The only reason I ever stop using this app is because I am so bad at sticking to a routine. But when I put forward the effort, this is the only app I have found that actively encourages me. Just the idea of using it is enough to help me recommit :) And I have never regretted buying the full version, which is not the case with so many other apps. Give it a try and you’ll understand why the ratings are so consistently good.

title: Shameful there’s no free option at all
body:
So sad. This app used to be free but now you can’t use it at all without shoving out $30. I don’t understand why it’s so expensive as the only changes I’ve noticed is geo tagging habits? I understand it’s only $2.50 a month but my mind still can’t justify why, seems just desperate. Wish they introduced any free option, maybe with ads. But not having that option at all, even with limited functionality, is very disappointing. It just seems like, it’s all about money and that’s it.

Also saw a note that if you paid before ($3.99 for unlimited use) you can restore that purchase. That’s great for some people but my Apple ID is different. Sounds like I’m out of luck.

UPDATE//free option is available—when prompted to try free before subscribing just click the x to be taken to the app. Wish this was clearer, there should be something that says “try free option”. Either way, happy it’s free. The aesthetic and modern vibe of the app is great but that shady little trick about subscribing is disappointing

Make it clear, make it plain, smoke and mirrors is for the Friday night comedy show, not my personal life.  I downloaded just to find that there is a 7 day “free” trial, after which the subscription price takes effect, but you can cancel, oh but wait, cancellation takes effect 24 hours after the last use of the upgraded.....  and you lost me.  If I want to read ramblings I can just click on some random privacy policy in anything at all. A waste of m time, and I want to be compensated for wasting my time that I should have been using to do chores and be productive, like the name of your highly elusive 1 star app.   So I deleted the app, but now I’m combing through my account settings to see if you somehow hooked into my Apple Pay for some strange subscription that I don’t even want any part of!  I have a note pad! It costs $.25! Give me my time back!

title: Small price to pay
body:
If you want a habit and nothing else is working I highly recommend this app. I’ve read so many books on the psychology behind building habits and this app touches upon those same principles. Being able to make a streak is extremely rewarding and instead of doing something to achieve a reward you are competing against yourself. Being able to check something off as completed is very satisfying. The app really is best used in premium but if you’re serious about your goals then you can spare the cash. In my case, paying up the money is actually more motivating because I want to make sure I don’t waste it by ignoring my goals. 
Overall, great app. Wish you could go into more details as far as times a reminder happens but it’s a good investment in yourself.

Hi Patricia,

Maksim

I would like to see though, a feature where I can make a task as ‘optional’ or something to where if I don’t do it/skip it, it wouldn’t count as a negative strike for it. Or maybe have a justification block come up to explain why I can’t do a task. For example:
I have a task to hit the gym in the morning but sometimes I can’t because I have to go into the office instead to get some work done which makes me then ‘skip’ it. But for those days I have another hit the gym task set in the afternoon just in case I can’t make the morning one. So at some point, one of those hit the gym tasks is going to be ‘skipped’ since I’ll do the other one.

Unless I’m missing a setting or setting these up completely wrong I would like to see this feature added so it doesn’t seem like I’m always skipping something.

title: really helpful
body:
The Productive app helps me to reconnect with my executive function as perimenopause destroys my sleep and gets me down. I’ve been a DIY CBT junky to stay on track and build better habits for decades, using paper lists and a shared online calendar.  My daughter recently described me as “the executive function” of the family, but I am using many new props to retain that title and the Productive app has become key. 

As the Mom of a family of 4, I support others in their meals, sleep, hw, their own CBT weekly shifting routines, Rx management, etc. Importantly, the app reminds me to do immediate things for “me”, resulting in health benefits for me, which benefit the whole family. Putting yourself last might not be the hangup of most users, but it is mine: with my busy friends and family, having an electronic, well-intentioned nudge in my pocket (the Productive app) is good during this time of life.  

The Productive app lets me set up and modify task lists for morning and evening routines and free floating daily or weekly tasks. It gives me pop-ups - yes, they’re irritating when I’m off-task, but that’s the point. I love the calm, black background color, bright colors and quirky symbols for tasks. I love the flexibility of changing my tasks as some become habits needing no reminders. And of course I can define new tasks as part of my routines to acquire habits I hope to eventually do automatically. I suppose it’s the sticker chart I never had as a kid.  

Again, in the cognitive assault of perimenopausal sleep deprivation, I rely on the Productive app to do what used to be super easy. It reminds me of the background stuff that has to chug along for life to be smooth and satisfying - stuff I never used to have to list out.  For example, the app is supporting an earlier bedtime, longer walks with the dog (I need more steps), making the time to enjoy my tween, and time spent actually preparing vegetables rather than time capsuling them in the fridge drawers - these are all tasks I define ranging from the trivial to the emotional high stakes stuff.  Checking off the tasks on my phone provides moments of reflection during my days, which helps me file away those good times with my kids, the dog (and all those fresh veg). The app is my medium-term background memory. Best of all, it highlights “streaks” of completing tasks consecutively: this is like an electronic pat on the back, which right now I relish. 

Will I keep using the Productive app when perimenopause ends and I’ve got a new normal?  Wrong question: it’s super when I need it during this transition, which is right now!

title: Helpful for Reminding/Bad for Data Tracking
body:
I’ve been using this to set goals to increase meal prepping, eating cooked meals from home and working out. I love the actual checklist part, but the way the app tracks data doesn’t make sense. If you complete all of your daily goals you get a filled in bubble for the day. If you have a goal set for 3x/week, the days that you do that goal will be filled in but the days that you don’t remain hollow. I think at the end of the week if all of your weekly goals are met that all of the bubbles for that week should become filled in to show you had a perfect week. 

Additionally, I don’t understand how the streaks work (yes I read it in the app). Sometimes if you skip a habit or don’t do it, it will break your streak (which makes sense), but then I’ve also had it happen where if I have perfect days in a row somehow my streak has been broken. 

I really wish the data collection piece made more sense so I could get a more accurate picture of my hard work.

body: I love this app for tracking habits. The premium version is well worth the price, especially if you consider the cost per month of the annual option. I’ve been trying to start a bullet journal, but have struggled with motivating myself to go through and physically set up the format myself to track each habit, with this app it does all the work for me and has a nice design. I wish there was a little bit more flexibility with scheduling monthly habits, like if you could pick an exact day of the month when something needs to be done, or the number of times per month you’d want to do something, similar to the layout when setting weekly goals. Another feature I’d like to see is the ability to “overachieve” on a goal. Like if I set my gym goal as a minimum of 3 times a week, it would be nice to be able to mark it done if I go a fourth time in order to track progress and help reevaluate goals later on. I’d especially like it if this was a feature able to be turned on or off depending on each habit. Overall this is a great and easy to use app that helps me stay motivated and productive.

title: Yes, please.
body:
This app is exactly what I needed. Hi-tech yet clean and simple, impressive design with intuitive functionality. 

I love the soothing charcoal backdrop and how you can customize every goal — from everything between daily and monthly in frequency, down to the color and icon associated with every goal. Goals can be any number of times per day/week/month, and you can assign them for a general time or for morning, afternoon, and evening.

Spring for the premium, it’s worth it. Getting to see your current streak of days with all habits completed, your best streak on record, and your total number of “perfect” days is so motivating. 

Thank you, Productive, for inspiring me to live my best life.

title: Very Helpful and Encouraging
body: I don't often take time to write reviews, but I am sincerely enjoying this help! It has been so helpful and easy to use. I love how easy to customize this, and if you miss or skip a goal for whatever reason its not degrading. Rather it encourages you to keep going, and do what you can to succeed with whatever size goal/task/daily chore/project/new habit you recorded. I have tried other apps similar before and have been very disappointed, and then ended up losing interest and feeling more defeated by not getting something done. If you are a personality where you need to record your tasks or enjoy the satisfaction of crossing something else off from your day this is for you! I will admit that in the free version I only had the ability to record 2 goals/habits, which was not close to what I was hoping for. The company offered a timed promotion that Im not sure if it was only over the holiday or just as a new user I got a chance to upgrade too. However, I decided to give it a shot as it was only $12 for the full year which was easily affordable and I am really loving the fact I did. I highly recommend!

title: Great app for building/maintaining good habits
body:
I read “The Power of Habit” and wanted an app that would help me build good habits. You need a trigger and a reward for each one. While you are taking the time to naturally build these (eg, the trigger, such as going into the bathroom in the morning triggering several habits in a routine; the reward, such as a great trip to the dentist because you’ve been flossing), the app provides an easy trigger and reward system. 

The trigger is the notifications. I have turned off ALL other badge notifications. The first new habit I am committed to building is responding to this app / tracking my daily habits. Even if tracking means I mark the habit as “skipped” for the day. I am recording the data and setting goals for the year. 

The reward (again, this is scaffolding until my new habits’ natural rewards take over) is the feeling of accomplishment from tracking the data / marking things “done.”

100% completion on my daily workout habit is my big goal. 80% completion on everything else is my other goal. I will not change my set of habits all year - I’m trying to automate these behaviors, so consistency is key! December of next year I will think about what I want to change for the following year, practice all month, and set a new 100% goal. 

In 3 months I have a reminder set to review my notes from Power of Habit, along with my data from this app, and look for areas of improvement (as well as celebrations!) I imagine I will set another reminder after that to check in on my progress again in another 3 months. Humans are good about planning the next 90 day period but much longer than that, and the reminder won’t mean much. 

Hope this has been helpful for someone out there! And thank you to the developers for this great app!!

title: Okay but Very Very Basic
body:
Update: I would like to add to this after using this app for six months. The devs do not care about the users. The only reason I bought this subscription is so I could export my habits. You cannot do that at all! Yours notes are not in the back up! So if you get a new phones you’ll lose them. 

It’s a worse app than I thought; at least for me. What is the point of tracking habits if they can’t be exported. They might as well not recorded. 

————

So when I first installed and it asked for 19.99$ subscription pa I just quit it. I don’t have space for subscriptions anymore. I would happily pay 20$ as a one off but I’m not paying it again next year. 

Having said that it is a good app. It is evident that time and though was spend in building this. But not a subscription. Sorry. 

So a few days later they gave a limited time 50% offer which bought on an impulse without having tried the app for a few days. I was ready to delete it just didn’t got around to it. But then they said 9.99$ for a year. This doesn’t mean the price was just too high I just desperately needed an app which does what this does to an extend and don’t have the time to develop one myself atm. I still would not consider subscription at a lower price. And I will definitely not renew this. 

So on to the review, the subscription model gets me going... it is good concept. The UX is well enough designed though it can be improved to be more fluid eg there’s no 3D Touch support, sliding back doesn’t work, pop ups don’t close with slides/flicks or taps etc. Most people might not notice these things but I do. I’m lazy. 

I haven’t  had the chance to try out the stats parts but it seems just a simple chain. I’ll export all my habit when I need to analyse them so I don’t mind the simplicity. 

I imagine the dev just added notes part in the end doesn’t consider that an average user uses it often enough. I do. So that need to properly incorporated. 

There’s loads more quicks. So it might fit your needs but if it doesn’t it doesn’t. Luckily they at least let you try it before you buy. 

It’s things like these that dev can’t be blamed for not thinking about them but should be blamed because this has a subscription model.

PS: Dev if you read this, know I mean no disrespect or disparage you or your work. It is good. You should be proud of it. And thank you for the 50% off offer. You’ve given me time to build my own and knowledge of what I need. Don’t worry it’ll pretty different and won’t be published. It would have a very  niche use

If any of the developers are seeing this, PLEASE increase the number of habits available for free. At least to 5 or so. So many college students want to use this app to try and organize their life but only having 3 free habits available isn’t enough. We’re forced to look for other apps that offer many more habits, but in much less quality.

Despite only using this app for 20 minutes I still gotta give it 3 stars because the design is outstanding. Everything is so organized and easily accessible. The small things you can do with each habit put this app superior to all other habit-tracking apps, but so many of us decide not to use it because there’s only 3 free habits. If anything, at least make the subscription options cheaper. I know there’s many people who use this app already and pay for premium just fine, but there’s a ton of money-challenged people out there that really want to use this app so much :))). I know I can just put in my three top habits to track but I can’t exactly choose, haha. They all seem important to me. 

If you’re out there living a stable life and income, this app is for you! It’s definitely the #1 habit-tracking app if you pay for premium. From what I hear, it’s totally worth it.
