title: Kinda Good App.
body:
In the past few days I’ve been looking for an app that could serve as a calendar and time tracker. After trying out various calendars, I’ve decided that the original calendar that came with my iPad is the best and most straightforward one and requires the least time spent on scheduling. However it doesn’t track my time on my activities. So I got this app to track my time. 

What I find this app to be missing, is a calendar where I can see my schedule as I make it. For a person with ADHD, it is hard to visualize a schedule in the mind, it’s kinda like doing the “bara book bara boom” then never go on that vacation because I forgot about the whole thing. In the same manner I can schedule my intentions and even if there is a sound to remind me, if I can’t look at it on a visual timeline, the sound just feels like a reminder for something I’ve already forgotten and my self confidence gets shattered. Also, I can’t send my schedule from Productive to my Apple Calendar but I can send it to Apple Notes, which makes no sense. There is absolutely zero purpose for my calendar to hang out there in a form of a text “to read later”.

Another thing is, that you can only put down things you will definitely do again and again over time at the exact same time. So this app is excellent for reminding me to take my medication. But if I want to clean my kitchen floor, I only have the option to schedule it with the same time and same day in in mind for the future. There is no “one time” scheduling on Productive. I could make a schedule for repeating unspecified “house chores” but then I won’t remember or know which housework I want to do when the time comes, so I have to use my calendar for that.  I usually make plans for such things only a day or two in advance and these chores don’t follow any time pattern. 

What Productive is good for, are things that you want to be sure you are doing at the same time and same day every time you do them. It can be every day, same days a week, or for example, activities done every Wednesday each month. So what I use it for, is going to sleep at the same time every night (I need discipline to go to sleep), waking up at the same time every day at the same time and make sure my dog and I take our medications on time every day. I have two other activities on Productive that I want to make sure I make happen every day for 6 hours, 5 times a week. I would recommend that you don’t over schedule your Productive with activities, because you will still need time slots for your calendar. If you load all your activities on Productive, you will live like a robot. There are things that I need to do once in a while and they can’t interfere with activities on Productive. Since I live in a remote rural area I have to spend a day each month shopping for- and stocking on food to last for awhile. This shopping trip does not always fall on the same day or date and interferes with my Productive schedule. I guess that means I have to cheat once a month because there is no flexibility in the schedule on this app.

What is really good about Productive is that it’s simple to use (although the usefulness is quite limited in my opinion) and it is Siri activated. 

The improvements I would most like to see is: 1) the ability to sync this app with my Apple calendar, 2) a bit more control over the timing of the schedules I create in Productive.

title: Missing obvious features

Also, there’s no way to set actual times to accomplish your tasks. You simply have morning, afternoon, and evening. Nor is there a way to set tasks that require many instances of completion during a single day. For example drink 10 cups of water spread out over the course of a day. The app Daily Tracker allows you to do this, but that app also fails by not allowing users to establish overall goals and track progress towards that goal. 

These tracker apps annoy me by not really advancing their functionality. 

There are many other ideas I have that would make this app flexible and a true resource. As it stands, the premium version isn’t very good. Might as well be free, but I guess they’re selling how pretty and easy to use it is. And that’s true, it is pretty, and easy to use.

title: Great App
body:
I find this app highly motivating to help me establish new habits in my life. I love the simplicity of the design. 

This app has literally helped save my life. I’m a recovering drug addict, who lived for years practicing unhealthy habits. As a part of my program of recovery, I began to utilize your app to teach myself how to practice healthy habits. I made a list of ten things that I was going to try and do every day and entered them into the app. 

While I can’t say that I’ve completed all of them every day, I can say that I’ve completed at least 90% of them every day. Out of the past 28 days, I’ve performed all ten habits on 24 days. Those healthy habits have gone a long way to helping me stay clean for the last month. 

Many people, who I share my experience with about using your app, ask what ten habits do I try to do every day. I’ll refrain from sharing that list, because I believe the habits we choose to shape our lives are personal.

By using your app, I’ve come to realize that some things in my life are nonnegotiable, such as, staying clean. Thank you.

title: Underhanded
body:
I use this app daily, and I do see how it is helping me be more productive. However, they’re a bit cheeky when it comes to adding a habit. Supposably, you are allowed to have five free habits, which for a long time, I did. I myself whittled it down and then up and down again over time, and it wasn’t a problem. Until this past month. Now, I have three and want to add, but whenever I try to add one to the three I currently have, it takes me to a page that only gives me the option to pay for unlimited habits. I have looked all over the entire app repeatedly, and there is no option to add a habit any other way then to pull down, and when I do, as I said, it gives me no option but to add a free habit. I contacted support on this, and here was the reply (no explanation, no apology, no offer to restore my original 5 habit allowance): 
Hello Lily,
Thanks for your feedback.
Unfortunately some users might indeed have only 3 free habits in the free version.
Thank you for using our app.
Best regards,
Natallia

(Addendum: as for developer’s response to this review seen below, they clearly misread my review. I was getting 5 free habits for several months, and suddenly & randomly, those 5 free were limited down to 3. Nowhere in the free version did it indicate that this would happen after several months, mind you, not after a one free month trial. I am currently in touch with Apalon support, and twice now, they’ve admitted responsibility, acknowledging that the issue was within the app dysfunction. But it took many back and forth emails to get to this point. And now, I see the reply below.)

body:

title: Cut free version’s options in half — unhappy
body:
I deleted this. I do NOT appreciate this recent trend toward subscription models — it’s unsustainable for me and feels ridiculous for an app to charge a continuous fee for something I don’t consider essential. Handy? Yes. Crucial to my wellbeing to the point I’m going to shell out money every single month for the rest of my life? No. Would I pay a one time fee? Absolutely. 

I was okay with the free version with the 5 available habits, but after the most recent update this was decreased to THREE! I’ve been using the app for years, on the fence about supporting a subscription model, and then they slice the free options in half. I’m unhappy with this decision. 

I cannot afford subscriptions to all the apps I use. However, I am perfectly okay with adds for “lite” free versions or paying a one time fee for a quality app. If the pricing model changes to a one time fee I will happily pay and redownload. 

As of now I do not recommend.

title: Quite a good app
body: I especially appreciate this app, since the calendar it has tracks when you do things and when you don’t do things. This gives you a satisfying cross-off of the days of the week you do the things you planned, making you feel compelled to keep up the task instead of putting it off another day. That being said, all of the features (in the free version at least) besides reminders can be done using a regular calendar, which would give you an even more satisfying cross-off since it is being done physically. However, I would still recommend this app, for people who are still struggling with procrastination, since it isn’t the laziness but rather the will, and personally the will has kept me going with this app. The only downside is that I think the not free version is quite a bit expensive, especially for a mere habit tracking app, and especially considering that all of the features it has and offers in the paid version could be done with other apps that are free (like apps that come with an iPhone). Nevertheless, this is still an amazing app and it has helped me with habit tracking.

author: Keegan Cooke

title: My Main App
body:
I have paranoid schizophrenia, and having a stable routine along with medication and therapy is essential to my recovery.  This is hands down the best app for creating and maintaining a daily self care routine.  Being schizophrenic it is hard to stick with a routine.  I am always forgetting what I need to be doing.  Not anymore with this app.  I use this app to remind me of the things I need to do each day.  For projects I use Things 3, for one time reminders I use the standard reminders app, and for appointments I use the basic calendar.  I keep these four apps in a folder called Daily. If I see a number over the folder, I know that something needs to be done.

What I like most about this app is nothing has a time that is set in stone.  There are three periods:  morning, afternoon, and evening.  This gives me needed flexibility, in case I am having a bad day.  Also these periods keep me from becoming overwhelmed by looking at a whole days worth of tasks.  (Although you can look at the full day if you need to).  There is also a satisfying sound when you swipe a task complete.  This app has worked wonders in my day to day life living with schizophrenia. If you don’t have a serious mental illness this app will still be extremely handy.  If you do have a serious mental illness it is a necessity.

title: Missing one key feature
body:
This app is very good, as the other reviews attest. However, it has one major flaw in my opinion.

Let's say you have a habit you want to do 3x per week. Now, if you are having a great week maybe you decide to go for 4x that week. No joy. In this app, once you hit your goal of 3x the habit effectively disappears for the rest of the week. So, it is impossible to track any extra days.

I suspect this is what other people are referring to when they say that this app is useless for tracking. The fix (IMO) is to let a person choose whether to show or hide a habit once the weekly goal has been met. I can see where the "right" answer may vary from habit to habit. So, ideally you could set this as appropriate on each habit.

For example if I have a goal to read 4x a week, I should still be able to at check it off 5-7x a week to reinforce my habit. Put in an option to have completed quotas greyed out at the bottom marking them as “done” but still doable. Also, the stream system needs to be fixed. If I make a habit today, then delete it, I cannot “finish” today. If I go back to yesterday and finish a weekly task and it eliminated it from today’s options, I cannot “finish” today. It ruins the streak. Ruins the whole reason of using the app.

You have to cancel your subscription through a link that’s not easily found in the app, that takes you to the Apple support site and you have to cancel through that platform instead of within the app itself. If you do not cancel before the 7 day trial is up, you are automatically charged the premium subscription fee and that purchase cannot be canceled (ie no refund). Usually apps will refund the automatic charge if you cancel within a day or so of when the free trial ends. This was not the case, and I feel like I was swindled into paying $20 that is apparently non-refundable, which is extremely unsettling. Beware of this.

title: This is a killer app
body:
I am beginning to love Productive. It is a customizable app that makes it easier for you to build and stick to habits.

I started trying this out for a week and didn’t use it very much, because the app is really valuable if you dedicate time to customizing it and using it. When my free week expired, it auto-bought the year membership, so I thought, fine, let me give it a second try. Boy am I glad I did.

I use Productive between 1-3 times a day, which makes sense: the app has 3 built in reminders to do tasks (morning, afternoon, and evening). It has been a tool I’ve used to put into action the morning and evening routines I want to do on a daily basis. It has also helped me figure out what habits I am building effectively and which ones I am not, because I see how many days in a row I’ve done something and it’s a signal to me that my system is broken if I lapse more than a day in a row. It also helped me to realize that being specific and actionable is super important because there is nothing to “do” on an item that is general and vague.

All in all, I’ve started to recommend this app to my clients and think if someone is a self-starter, they will appreciate this and might even love it!

The one thing I hope Productive improves is adding more images to assign to habits. They have a large list, but to boost it further would be great.

Bottom line: worth the $20!

body:
I'm 16 and I got this app to keep track of chores and other daily habits I often forget. It's exactly what I needed. I'm not trying to schedule my day down to the minute or even the hour. And I needed an app flexible enough that as long as I complete my habit that day, it doesn't break my streak, but still keeping certain habits to certain times of day.
I like that you can schedule an individual habit for multiple times a day instead of having to create the same habit 3 times, each time scheduling a different time. I also enjoy how customizable it is, how you can choose the icon, color and order of the habits. My favorite thing about the app is the general scheduling. There are 3 times to schedule a habit to; morning, afternoon and evening. And you can choose between which times each of these apply. Even if I miss a habit during its schedules time, it isn't counted as missed until the day is over, which keeps my motivation for the streaks up.  It's the perfect level of simplicity for me.
My only complaint is that I have to pay a subscription for more habits! I don't really care about whatever else comes with premium. I love this app and it's exactly what I need but I can't pay a subscription. If it was a one-time fee for premium forever then I could do that. Even if it was $20 as long as it was just once. Otherwise, this app is just about perfect for me.

In productive all I can see is if I had a perfect day or a partially complete day. But for me there’s a big difference between completing 10% of my habits for the day and 90%, but they both count as partially complete days!

The ads to subscribe are near ever present! Why not give consumers a way to buy it once for a higher price. It looks like they can raise the rate any old time they choose (fine print) meaning you will have to pay more or get a new app. Highly annoying for me as a consumer. It’s a good app. However the way they are forcing ads on you is annoying. 

DON’T SUPPORT THIS TREND. 
Please rate all these subscription type apps with one star and then just don’t buy them. If you support subscription apps soon that is all we will have. As consumers you have a voice. They won’t give you a choice later if they want to raise rates. This type of pricing is not consumer friendly and should not be supported by the marketplace.

Thing is, I’ve been using My Home Routines for several years and segment my days a bit more finely than three parts. Using emoticons to label my tasks is a bit more work but does add some fun and color. 

Not wanting to abandon Productivity just yet, I thought to use it just for new habits that I want to embrace. As I was deleting the tasks already put in and adding a new one, I found the ads for their subscription to be intrusive. At one point my work was interrupted by a new screen with one. Seems like half the menu is about subscribing. 

Even though I expect ads in a free app, I don’t expect them to interfere. And as a personal choice, I prefer a one time purchase to an ongoing subscription. I would likely buy a paid version of the app. Instead I’m uninstalling it 🙁

author: Lena_cruz

title: Hooray!
body:
Finally an app that actually motivates me to stick to my goals, whether they’re daily or yearly. I rarely write reviews on apps but I couldn’t not write one for this app. I wanted to give it 4 1/2 stars because my one complaint is pretty small but I either can’t figure it out or it’s not possible. 

As I said, this app has helped with my motivation to get things done quite a bit. I’m usually a procrastinator but the idea of breaking a streak because I’m feeling lazy drives me crazy, which encourages me to just get it done. It’s a really great psychological trick and it’s really what sets this app apart from other reminder apps (and I’ve tried quite a few because right now I’m still writing my to-do lists and reminders on paper every day and I’m trying to get away from that and switch to my phone and other Apple devices.  

As I said I do have one minor complaint, and it’s that you can’t add any notes or additional information until you’ve already completed the task. This frustrated me a couple times and left me having to keep the additional information in a separate app, which is not ideal. Pretty minor, but if it is possible and I’m just missing it could someone let me know? And if I’m correct about this... developers? :) could you maybe allow it in a future update? If Productive had that capability, it would be a 5 star rating from me. 

Overall though I’d highly recommend it. I’m only still in my week long trial but I intend to keep the paid full version (totally a reasonable cost for a year which says a lot about how worth it the app is because I’m super cheap when it comes to any purchases, especially electronic ones). 

So try it out, you’ve got nothing to lose. Try the upgraded paid version for at least the week’s free trial you’re offered to see if it’s worth it for you, too. And if it is, I think the cost for a year is pretty justifiable.
author: EhThroughZed

title: Nice app but subscription is ridiculous.
body: The user interface in Productive is laid out well and I actually prefer it to other apps like HabitBull but their subscription structure is ridiculous and I refuse to rent software rather than own it. This trend across the software industry is poisonous and in every instance that a developer has changed to a subscription only based fee structure I have sought an alternative app or, in cases like Adobe products, I’ve either downgraded to inferior versions like Photoshop Elements or have gone against my own ethical standards and pirated a piece of software because the developer took away my choice to own it.  I hate piracy, and in the case of Photoshop I have learned to settle using Photoshop Elements rather than a pirated full version, but the amount of revenue Adobe and other developers have missed out on from me is substantial due to their own greed. I understand that some consumers prefer a subscription model and they should certainly have that choice but it should be a choice rather than a requirement due to the choice of ownership being taken from them. Back to Productive... I would have definitely bought it for $4 when it was that price but I just learned about it. I would gladly spend $10-$20 or even more to own it now but since it is now only available to rent I have chosen to use HabitBull as my daily habit tracking app. I guess developers of apps like Productive feel that the revenue lost from driving away customers like me is outweighed by the increase in revenue from their subscription only fees. It’s a depressing trend and one that I hope dies out in favor of both purchase and subscription choices being the standard. The sad thing is that I’d have never even considered writing this review had they given me a choice of purchasing or renting the app.  I encourage every consumer to keep up the pressure on developers to offer that choice.  The developers of Productive have lost me as a potential customer as long as they do not offer a purchase option but the next company has a choice. Do they want my money or not? Thanks for reading.
author: AliasIris

title: Promising, but some definite flaws.
body:
I’ve been a premium user of this app for over 2 years and try to use it regularly, but it has a few flaws that don’t seem to be budging.

1. You can’t snooze a habit.
If you don’t get to a habit on it’s assigned day, you can either skip it or leave it incomplete. There’s no option to snooze for any amount of time (e.g., next day). A 3D Touch or long press on an active task to snooze until tomorrow would be great!

2. No option to hide completed habits.
If you have several habits on a given day (or in a given window, say, afternoon), there’s no way hide these. So you see your greyed out completed habits rather than those you have yet to do.
A simple toggle switch atop the interface to hide completed habits would solve this. Then if you wanted to view details or undo a completed habit, you could toggle the switch and do so, but by default, these should be hidden to avoid clogging up the interface.

3. Earlier incomplete habits vanish when the time window ends. (App badge and screen).
Say you’re running late, and some of your morning habits aren’t done by the time afternoon roles around. Those habits will vanish from the interface, and the badge icon counter for undone habits no longer includes them. There’s a small link to view them at the bottom, but if you have multiple prior periods (say it’s evening and you have a habit incomplete in both morning and afternoon), you have to view all habits, and this of course includes the completed ones (see above issue).
An option to always display incomplete habits after their time windows have passed would be much appreciated. The “do anytime today” is great, but there are tons of times users need “plan to do every morning, but even if the morning ends, I still want to do it”

4. No iPhone X support yet, but I didn’t dock points for this, it’s a new screen layout. Just would be nice (:

title: $4 total -> $12 -> $20 subscription?
body:
Overall, I like this app.  What I don’t like is the trend I am seeing (read the comments).  We have gone from a fixed price app, to an app that cost $12-13 a year to something that costs $20 a year using a subscription.  Has the value increased at the same pace?  Are new features added monthly?

If you paid for a subscription (especially one costing $20/year (that’s the new price)), help us out by sharing your experience in the comments.  Do you think this is worth that much?

Otherwise, if you want a fixed price app, check out Things.  You can create recurring tasks/todos that behave just like “habits” and synchronize that across all your devices.  Overall, I am left thinking that this app is overpriced for what you get and not worth the perpetual payments for the extra features.  The free version doesn’t do enough to be viable on its own.

***Developer Responses?***
The canned responses in all the comments don’t address the constant price increases as they relate to newly added value.  Share your thoughts to let people like me know if there is value based on your experience given the current price, $20/year recurring costs.

title: Nice app but lacking some important features.
body:
I’m a premium user of this app, and overall it’s nice looking and moderately functional. My biggest complaint is that it’s almost useless for data tracking. 

I meditate pretty much every day, but I consider doing it at least five days a week a success. So I went ahead and set the goal for five days a week. I meditated five days in a row, and suddenly I’ve lost the option to track it anymore for that week. Say I meditate every day for a week, I can’t track that under the five days setting. Meaning if I want to go back in time to see what days I usually miss, notice any patterns in the data—I’m out of luck. If I set it to the every day setting, and I miss a day, I lose my streak in the habit. 

Either I set it to five days, and I can’t keep accurate data records, or I set it to a week and I lose the motivation of maintaining a streak. It’s a really big flaw in the app and it would be nice to have it fixed. At least an option to allow a user to go over the set number of days would be nice, even if it wasn’t the default setting.

title: Lots of good, but one real flaw
body:
I love that the free version lets you get a real feel for the app before you buy.  I love that you can make your own habits, add notes to them, and order them how you want, with your day being divided into morning, afternoon and evening so you can see everything clearly.

I can't believe it doesn't have a function to allow you to see the habits you have to accomplish on any future days, only past days.

Also, you'd think they'd have a way for you to have tasks repeat every other day, and also on certain days of the month. It literally only lets you add tasks that repeat "at the beginning of the month or the middle of the month or the end of the month".

There's an app called motivated moms that is similar.  It allows you to look ahead at habits coming up for the future.  So, you can look at tomorrow and see: OK that's the day I'm trying to go to the gym to do weightlifting and then I'm also trying to meditate that day and I wanted to use that day to clean the living room.  It really helps to see all the things you plan to do on a regular schedule but not the same each day, or even each week (like, I'm trying to plan the next month's expenses on the last Sunday of each month). 

Motivated moms also allows you to schedule things for every other day.

The only thing I don't like about motivated moms is that you cannot rearrange the order of the habits. That's a real dealbreaker for me.

I also prefer the way this app looks over the motivated moms app. I hope they fix the above issues in a version in the future soon.

title: Beautiful and useful but missing a few things
body:
I really like this app in some ways, but it falls short in some important areas. I am not thrilled to have to pay $14 a year for an app that is missing features I think it should have but I am willing to support the developers for now hoping that the subscription model will work and the missing features are added. 

First what I like: 
* This is a beautiful looking app. That is important to me. 
* Helpful as a habit builder with the reminders, showing streaks, etc. 
* The morning, afternoon, evening layout works well
* Ability to set multiple reminders is great
* Ability to set multiple (up to 3) times a day is useful
* The boost feature to help you work on new habits

What is missing: 
* Setting specific times for habits would be nice 
* To set a weekly habit on a specific day, you need to actually set it as daily and then pick the day of week by deselecting all other days. That is not intuitive and I would like to be able to set something as "weekly" and pick the day. 
* Monthly habits should allow you to pick a specific day of the month. I do not see a way to do this. There is no work around like there is with weekly tasks. 
* The interface is beautiful but the flow relies too much on "back" and "menu". I think swiping (away from habits area) would be nicer, or a consistent menu on the bottom. 
* I would also like to see a way to click on a day through a calendar. (Similar to week view at the bottom but showing more days, and letting you look at future days.) 
* Syncing so I could use this app on my iPad or elsewhere and use the same data 
* Web interface 

The last 2 items are really important to me. Especially the syncing. This is what makes me willing to pay a subscription price for an app. Otherwise it should be a one-off price. If this does not change by the next time my subscription fee comes up, I will not be renewing.

title: I liked balanced better
body:
I appreciate the ability to schedule todos or habits on specific days of the week but balanced had the ability to actually set the frequency of a habit for seasonal and yearly tasks. Productive doesn't seem to do that. I thought it did once actually but it looks like it doesn't now either way. 
For me, i use this mainly to keep track of household chores. I like not setting a specific day but rather a frequency. I know i need to clean bedsheets once a week... other things once a month. Other things once a season and others like spring cleaning, once a year. 
So this doesn't work for me anymore and balanced is gone. Fortunately i can just download it still from the backup so I'm just going to continue using that instead. 
Also i like that theres functionality for the apple watch but i find that its a lot more useful to have a complication for these kinds if apps. Just a simple complication that tells me whats at the top of the list for today. Something like that. 
So yeah bring back seasonal and yearly frequencies and make a complication. :)

title: HORRIBLE Update
body:
Revised update:
Yet another silent update to the subscription payment. I was finally coming to terms from missing out on the one time lifetime access, to the low yearly cost. Today, I was notified that the price increased to nearly double the amount! I emailed customer support about all these constant price changes. Only to receive a semi-generic reply of "We do sales on various reasons. There might be another sale. Sorry. Thanks for using the app" -- all these silent backend changes to nickel & dime the customers. This developer seems to have gone over their head for what seems to be a simple todo list with a glorified calendar. Things that plenty of other apps do here for free or much lower cost. The app looks nice, but the price is far from worth it. I've officially given up on this app, pass. 

Original review:
Silent update to switch to a subscription based payment, not one mention even on the notes. 

I'm out. Greedy developers get no love.

Also, I have meds that I take 4 times a day but the app only gives me 3 timeslots.  I would prefer a "wakeup",  "lunch", "dinner", "bedtime" schedule for my meds but also keep the existing slots for other habits.

Finally, it would be more intuitive for me if I click on a habit with multiple times for it to take me to the screen where I can complete just one instance of that habit.  There is an icon at the bottom to do this but it would be more intuitive to click the main habit itself.

For both the young and the old alike. Plus they give you the option to write in your own personal habits, activities, etc. They even have a journal. I have not really played with it yet. But after looking at it and checking out the upgrade, I had paid the $3.99. Honestly I give away that amount on stuff I don't normally need. But this is an app that most ppl like myself can use. I give 5 stars based on the concept. I will be writing a second review next week. I will be utilizing this app all week as if my daily routine won't function without it, plus I will be adding some extra activities that I never seem to have time for or I just simple forget. Then I will rewrite a new review and let you know how well the app worked for me. I do say this much, if this app can help me, them this should be the next big thing.

I thought I would just try it out and probably give up on it within a week but it has completely changed my daily habits for the better. I've been using it for over a month now. It helped me remember when to go to bed so I got enough sleep, when to get ready for work so I would stop being late, when to take my medication so I could properly function, I am even sticking to a vegetarian diet (finally!!) after years of trying and failing to commit. Seriously, I highly recommend this app for people who have trouble keeping up with necessary, beneficial, daily routines (like my ADHD self).

title: Exactly what I have been looking for!
body:
Edit: I hope the app creator sees this! I have loved this app for a long time. There is one thing that I desperately wish it could do, however.  I really wish that I could see what's on the agenda for the next day.  I use this app not only for habits, but as a daily planner.  Not being able to see what exactly is on the agenda for the next day is a bummer.

Original review: I have spent the past year downloading (and often buying) habit/daily chore apps before then uninstalling them in disappointment. I really liked the idea of a gamified habit app, but after trying several, they just didn't have the deeper features I wanted which caused me to quit using them after some time. This app, is so much nicer. Its beautiful, so customizable, and a real joy to use. And it has features, such as streaks and graphs to help you visualize your success so that you will want to keep it up.  Really cool. The only thing I wish it had was a separate section where I could make one-time lists, such as a grocery list. Aside from working on habits, I usually have several separate lists going on, depending on if I need groceries, what bills are coming due, etc. I like to keep that separate from my habits. For now I either use notes or another list app, but it would be really cool to see that feature added in this app.  Aside from that, I am very impressed. I bought the full version because it is so worth it. Keep up the good work!

title: Changing my Life
body:
This app is wonderful, and for me, life changing! 

I love that it breaks habits into morning, afternoon, and evening habits, and it reminds me to do them. :D it shows me my success streaks, which encourages me to keep going. I'm having lots of success with this app.

It even helped me to break bad habits, like biting my nails. I set the habit "Don't bite nails" for three times a day, and after just a week of being reminded thrice daily, I was doing so much better! Just being reminded of my intention to not bite my nails was all I needed to break a 15 year bad habit. 

One thing I'd love to see added is a way to take notes on habits. When I miss a habit, I wish there was a way to take a memo of "why?" For example, if I bit my nails one day, it would be nice to take a memo: "got bored after lunch" or "feeling anxious about presentation."

title: Great motivation and excellent customer service!
body:
I downloaded productive because I was struggling to stay committed to doing my physical therapy for a torn hip labrum every day as my PT instructed. I downloaded the app a few days into my month long challenge of doing my therapy everyday, and I found it really helped me to stay motivated when I could check off and visualize my completed exercise routine on the well-designed and aesthetically pleasing app. I contacted their support team to see if there was a way to retroactively add in the days I had completed my exercise routine before I had downloaded the app, and they were very friendly and helpful in helping me get it all sorted out. I would definitely recommend this app as a way to stay motivated if you have goals you struggle to keep up with! 

My only recommendation would be to create more advanced goal setting features. For example, I would like to tell the app that my overall goal is to complete a month of doing PT every day, so it could provide me with information about how many more days I have to go and what percent of the goal I have achieved. It would also me nice to be able to put in and see information about why this is your goal (for me, it is life without chronic hip pin and avoiding hip surgery) and any rewards you plan to give yourself if you obtain the goal (I'm taking myself out to a nice dinner after my month-long challenge is complete). Obviously these are things I know already, but it would be fun to integrate them into the app and see reminders of why my goals are important to me.

If I have 7 for that day then completing six feels the same as one from the visual cues on the app. I'd personally like to see a partial circle when completing a portion of my goals and a full but empty circle when all but one is done and still have the full circle represent perfect days. title: Excellent — just want more customization
body:
This app is wonderful to help you stay on top of things you really want to make sure you're doing in a timely matter. It's truly excellent. My only qualm with it is the inability to truly customize the frequency of events — for example, I can't tell it to remind me to pay rent on the 1st of each month; only to remind me "at the beginning of the month." I also can't tell it I'd like to complete a habit, say, three times in each 2-week period; I can only say twice a week, and so on. (Disclaimer: I've not yet tried the other app by this maker, "Balanced." It may have more flexibility in that regard, but I'm not sure.) One other small issue: I would also like the ability to incorporate my own notification sounds, rather than be limited to the ones that come with the app (although they are all rather pleasant). Altogether, this app is delightful, and it's really helped me become a more responsible person overall. It is most certainly worth the little cost of upgrading to the full version.
Edit: I'd also like to see the purple icons remain purple when Floodlight is on. That is all. ;)

title: Give it a few days
body:
This app does things its own way: The look and feel of it is unique.

That may turn you off at first, but please trust me as someone who felt that way: Tinker with it and play with it, then just *try* it for a few days.

My friend raved about it to me so I gave it a shot, and once I "got the hang" of its specific UI and way of doing things, I'm totally in love with the app.

Will there little things here and there you wish were better? Yes. 

But as someone who has tried every sort of "habit tracker" app out there — almost literally — this is the *best one* I've used thus far, hands down. This app and "Strides" are the two best ones, though this one is a little simpler and..."cleaner" than Strides, so I prefer it now.

title: Leading a balanced, productive life
body:
If you've used Balanced, you'll think you're in the same app when you open Productive. That's because they're both from the same developer and do nearly the same thing.

Productive adds a feature that I'd wished Balanced had: custom reminders. And stats are better. Why these couldn't have been in Balanced is a mystery. Like some other apps, the app has a focus feature, but lacks the option to track bad habits.

The design is quirky, but in a good way; however, without a Today widget and the ability to skip days and quit habits (rather than build them) this app is not for me.

title: Thanks :)
body:
I very rarely pay for an app, but I paid for the full version and I am so glad I did. The app works great, and I've never come across a bug of any kind. I can't wait to see the results in my life. I used it for a while but then I needed space on my phone so I deleted it. Since I've re-downloaded it, I've realized what a mistake that was. I recommend this to anyone thinking about getting this. It's worth the money for the full version too.
The only question I have... the way I understand it, if you skip a habit, it doesn't hurt your streak. If that's correct, I would like a way to make it so it does hurt my progress. If I completely missed a habit, like brushing my teeth in the morning, for example, I would like to be able to skip it so it's out of my way but also have it hurt my streak for it. I can't make that up later in the day so there's no point in it staying there. Maybe you could change a setting for whether or not you want a skip to hurt your streak? Just a suggestion, but my rating remains at 5 stars. Great app.

title: Favorite app
body:
This has become my go to app for making sure I stick to my daily routine. It blocks of the list for time of day making things very manageable, but not micro managed. But, there is an option for setting specific times for specific task too, if I want that. It's very flexible in letting you set up when you want to see the tasks/routines you want to complete.

Most important for me is it keeps track of what I've accomplished. I log what I've completed with a swipe and then I can look back and see how successful I've been at which tasks. Not only does this make me feel good, but lets me see where I need to adjust for better success.

It also has a boost for one specific task, letting you devote extra attention to something you're struggling with.

All in all, the best app I've found for managing my day. It is one of my favorite apps and has quickly become an app I would't want to do without.

title: Almost perfect but needs more features
body:
4.99 is kinda steep for the full version. Especially since there's not a way to include dates for deadlines. If there was I would be 100% satisfied. 
I'd like it to remind me of whatever thing I have to do until the deadline and let me know when it's closing in and whatnot.  There's plenty of good habits in real life with deadlines. Like, get a birthday present, or pack your books for a move, or get an oil change, and those kinds of things. I like the way this app works and everything not being in one spot isn't conducive with brain fog. 
Anyway, this app keeps me on track, even with said brain fog. It's easy to let stuff slip though the cracks these days, even without nerve & pain disorders. And I need to do a better job of taking care of myself. 
I love that it doesn't show you everything at once so it doesn't get too daunting and I just shut down. Plus there are things I can look forward to, like hanging out with a friend or going out for a walk. Finding time for them can be hard but If I can do everything I can be happier and more functional. If I got working medication too, lord save us because I would CRUSH IT with this app. 
The icons are great, I love that the app is dark (I'm photosensitive and bright colors hurt my eyes), the sounds are cute, love the customization, and pretty much everything. Add those deadlines and I will change my review to five stars.

title: Gettin things DONE!!!
body: It’s an easy-to-do, interactive, and fun application! How it works is you choose a certain goal you want to accomplish. i.e. health, fitness, home, hobbies, social, efficiency, or write your own. The app then gives you options on what specific goal you’d like to accomplish. For example, if I were to choose health, it asks me if I want to eat some fruit, a good meal, brush my teeth, take a break, or take vitamins, etc. If I were to choose fitness, it would ask me different goals such as a running time, certain personal record for a lift, or a sport I’d want to play, and other things of that nature. It then asks me what days I want the goal to reoccur. Daily, weekly, etc. If  I don’t accomplish a goal, it will give me constant reminders that I need to do it. It’s interactive and fun for me. I was wanting to set a goal to go to the gym and I did! All because the app would remind me, according to my schedule. I enjoyed using it for the week, and I definitely keep it for the future. It was more than just a planner, it was almost a game for me. I knew I needed to get stuff done, so all I did was put it into the app and it helped me to accomplish tasks, goals, and my entire schedule. I really did enjoy this app.

title: Simple Yet Effective
body: This app is simple enough that you'll find no barrier to use, yet is feature rich enough to fit most of your basic habit-building needs. A little is left to be desired though, especially considering recent mainstream literature on the "science" of habit-building which encourages the use of "rewards" after completing a habit. I'd love to be able to plan my rewards via a note or annotation, but alas, notes are limited to use for already completed habits. Additionally, I'd love second "mode" or "profile" for when I am on a business trip or away from my more regular life activities. While I wouldn't expect this one of the development team, it would be  welcome addition. Despite these reservations, I've gone ahead and purchased the pro version for a few bucks ($3.99 I believe?) as the app is extremely well-developed and is likely the best product on the marketplace for my needs (simple habit tracking).

I needed to associate positive goals with rewards and the check list (and the routine for a smoothie agreed my workout) totally did the trick! Give it 3 consistent months and it truly becomes second nature! Though I love technologically, I realize it is a blessing and a curse. The more complicated life gets and technologically advanced-
It becomes increasingly difficult to juggle so many things in various mediums (paper, email, apps, podcasts, Facebook etc) and we are expected to be faster, more productive and stay on top of it all. This app is the tool to get you there. Combine it with the system provided by guidelines in "Getting Things Done" by David Allen and you're set! (I hope they come up with an app for that too!)

title: Highly customizable & clean
body:
I've tried several habit trackers, and this one is the best. There's nothing I dislike about it.
The best feature is how customizable it is with every feature you can think of to make it most convenient for you, all the while without busy clutter. You can make it as minimalist or as detailed as you want, without taking away from its beautiful design.

•Clean beautiful layout that's pleasing to the eye
•Intuitive navigation that is easy to figure out
•Ability to set a habit for daily, weekly, or monthly schedule, with Morning, Evening, or Anytime option
•Ability to set a habit to occur multiple times a day or multiple times per week
•Tracking feature allows to view each habit separately and all the habits at once for each day 
•Habits can be checked off for previous days, skipped, or reset
•Habits can be grouped by Morning, Evening, Anytime, or all 
•Each habit has its own reminder(s) that can be set at the time(s) most convenient to you
•There are no annoying pop-up ads and it doesn't crash! 

There are many more features that really make this app personal and enjoyable to use. 
The point is to focus on building habits, not spending time on the tracking process. This app makes it easy. Thank you to the developers; it's well thought out.

title: Well-conceived, well-executed
body: I wanted an app to help me trap aspirational goals. iCal works great for hard and fast deadlines and specific dates, but I wanted something more flexible: something that allows me to aim for working out five times a week but on no particular day. And I wanted to retain the fun of checking off what I achieved and keeping score over weeks or months. So far, Productive is perfect for that. It allows me to designate how many times per week, how many times per day (up to three: morning, afternoon, and evening), and has many, common aspirations already programmed for you to select so you don't have to type in every activity (but you do have the option to customize). You can swipe right when you complete an activity, swipe left to defer it. Honestly, it's a great app.

body: I'm a mother who stays home with two small kiddos. I have a horrible memory (permanent mom brain!) and this app is EXACTLY what I needed. I bought the full version so I could have unlimited habits and so I could customize how often I need to do something (Clean bathrooms 2x a week, sweep/mop the kitchen 3x a week on the days I'm not cleaning the bathrooms, etc) and it does exactly what I need it to do. It's also great for putting in habits that need to be done once a month, like cleaning the ceiling fans. The app it's maddenly limiting in it's quest to have the world's simplest UI, because it's not intuitive or useful, leaving the user just banging their head against the wall because it's missing basic navigation and functionality. 

This app misses the mark big time and I wish I had just used OURHOME which I downloaded at the same time because it does everything this app attempts to do plus more, and is more helpful and easy to navigate. title: Honest Review
body:
The Dev is gonna hate me for this, but I wanted my review to stand out from the rest. 

I recently bought OmniFocus, have used Things, todoist, wunderlist, trello, paymo, asana, gtasks, evernote, reminders, harvest, and about a million other 5 star apps/services and this app has been hands down the very first app that has actually forced me to take the first basic steps to productivity. The problem with the other apps is that many of the tools are so sophisticated that I was always struggling with where to start and how to map out my tasks because it always just seemed to make more sense in my head than wasting the time to write it down when I could just be doing it, but this app has almost forced me to focus on a few specific process forming habits that made me realize what I've been missing the whole time, where to begin with building a successful workflow. 

I added a few pre made habit templates and after a few days of being harassed by the notification on the icon I opened the app and checked off "create a to do list", after a few days of that I really started to think about what I was checking off and gradually started creating a small list of the stuff that was stressing me out the most, not everything I had to do, but just the big things, and that list continues to grow to where now I'm using OmniFocus and other tools to further build out my workflow structure and get in the habit of developing and creating a successful and productive to do list that somewhat forces you to move onto the next task. 

Two years of trying tons of apps, this app is truly remarkable. I feel like I'm ripping you off for only $3.99. I would recommend that you charge like $1.99 a month or something because I would be glad to give you recurring income for the way this is changing my life (and apparently several other reviewers) 

Thanks so much and sorry for the one star.

title: A helpful tool for personal growth!
body:
A lot of people may not know that habits are one of the foundational things that shape their life. Whether it's a good or a bad habit, it will determine your life ! This app makes up for it. It allows me to be reminded and be motivated to keep track of the things I want to do in order to be a better me. Whether it's being in a better shape through nutrition, making sure I stay on track with my goals, or just plain staying away from certain habits, this app proved to be most useful ! I recommend expanding the habits you can eliminate or form & just remind yourself.

So with that, it does require a few things I would love it to have:

1.) the ability to choose what time I can be reminded - I just found out this can be done.
A little more instruction should be utilized.

2.) tally marks ! For example, I want to drink 8 cups of water a day, I should be able to check off the amount each time I do the habit.

3.) more thumbnails? Maybe use emojis instead of custom made. It's a little limited.

4.) when creating the habit, I don't get the option to create notes on it unless I finish & click done, then skip or click done. It's also kind of time consuming to look for the notes.

5.) the option to put how long I must do a habit of have a limit off ? It would be great to set a timer & put on a counter to see if we surpass it or not.

6.) easier viewing of statistics and how well (or how poor I'm doing with a habit). it's harder to find it it !

7.) competition compatibility? I was talking to my friend how I need an accountability partner. What if you can connect with friends online or something and compare results? I'm gonna be looking for a partner to compete with, & whoever has the least average percentage of habits completed altogether (another thing that should be added) will buy something for the winner. Maybe allow prizes or accommodation or something that makes winning more exciting ? 

8.) average percentages of all the habits completed

I don't ask for this as a user that will not use if not improved but rather I believe it's a helpful improvement ! I hope the team of this app will be able to pull off some of these & it will be more than appreciated ! 

Thanks for this amazing app !

title: LIFE CHANGING!! ❤️👍🏼
body: I, myself, am very picky about apps. I feel as if it has to be "perfect" in my eyes and most of the time I find it hard for apps to exceed that expectation. I've tried to download apps that would help me with my busy schedule, trying to get in the normal life necessities, that at the time I would skip over. I could never find one like it till I was looking over the new "favorite apps." This is where I found this app. I downloaded it just to see if it would meet my standards, and it did! The app is very colorful and gives you a lot of free room. You can set times and days that you want to do something. You get an icon and can choose a color for each habit. I suggest keeping a color for certain things like eating and drinking stuff, I will always put as the color red. Notebooks, writing, and planning stuff I will always put in the color orange. If you're in school, this is a great tool to get on track with studying and homework for your classes. I upgraded within like 2 minutes of getting the app, just because of how good it works. Getting the upgrade allows you to have more than 5 habits, allows you to have a reminder sent to your phone, and multiple other things that are worth the upgrade! If you've always struggled with being organized, like myself, let me tell you this app absolutely changes your life. ❤️ Best app ever!!

author: Joe_from_TN_

title: Worth Every Cent
body:
The Productive app is one of those that you're going to find is truly useful. The interface design is clean, simple and easy to use. I've personally tried to use Google Calendar and the iPhone calendar to improve my productivity and just found them clunky and more prohibitive than anything else.

The primary reason is a calendar is right down to the date and time which is very limiting. Productive is about getting your habits in and making sure they happen at some point and morning, afternoon and evening is as defined as it gets. So it's more of a simple approach rather than accounting for every minute of the day which becomes cumbersome and interferes with productivity in my opinion.

Again it's not a to-do or a scheduler in the traditional sense. Instead, you set up habits, prioritize them and swipe them away when you're done. There are built in habits but habits are also customizable which gives real power to the user.

The other great feature is being able to visualize data and track your habits. Calendars and schedulers just fall way short in this area. Being able to track data and see progress really provides the empowerment element needed in a productivity tool. 

I also love being able to add notes to each habit. I follow a system where I note what it will cost me for not following through and what I'll gain if I do. Being able to see that and have it linked to my habits is a tremendous help.

If you have found calendars and schedulers are too clunky, messy and hard to visualize your data then this is the app for you.

body:

First of all it's got a great design, really colorful but simple. (and love the  pops and "rotation" of the screens) Actually everything about this app is simple which is crucial for actually wanting to use it. And it's customizable which is KEY. Think of any habit you would like to implement, pick a title and a cute little icon for it (and color), schedule it for either recurring daily (morning, afternoon, evening, or anytime), weekly 1-5 times a week, or monthly (beginning, middle, or end). You can see all your habits grouped by the time of day and it's amazing.
I've created over 30 habits already. Excessive? Maybe but I'm ADD and an entrepreneur and with this little app I was able to finally see all my habit goals in one place and found myself for the first time accomplishing EVERY SINGLE ONE. A perfect day on my first day! Can't beat that!! And a tip for maximum effectiveness: give this worthy app a place on your home screen. Trust me you won't be sorry!

I haven't bought pro version yet in the hopes the price goes down, but I plan to buy it. Free version shows you how it works and let's you run 4 or so events at once. 

It's a little addicting and that's a good thing. I hate doing mundane things like laundry and brushing teeth and all that; this app makes it less of a torture to remember what needs to be done, and then do it. Nothing excessive has been added, nothing crucial has been missed.

TL;DR Best time management app I have used to date, pro is a little too expensive though

I would speed an average of 4 hours on social media throughout the day. Sometimes I would randomly look down at my phone just out of habit. title: Absolutely Worth It!
body:
I've been "meaning to get" a daily goal app for awhile now. This morning I finally decided to begin the search. It was honestly one and done after seeing Productive.

What originally drew me in was the streamlined, clean design. What kept me around was how straightforward and simple things were. After quickly meeting the goal limit and seeing the pro prompt, I immediately purchased the full version.

Very rarely do I purchase apps. I didn't even read the reviews first which is completely unlike me. After just a few minutes of run time, I immediately somehow knew this one wouldn't disappoint me. I have never felt compelled to write a review before, but this app deserves praise.

I love that you can focus in on the most minute details or keep things vague and general - the choice is yours. The level of customization is admirable.

For those of you reading the reviews first and still debating the purchase: If you are looking to stay on top of tasks, feel accomplished, conquer new habits, or simply need to be reminded to not forget the small stuff, Productive is absolutely worth the minor investment.

The hardest part of anything is taking the first step. Don't "keep thinking about it." Start today! You can do this. :)

title: Great app!
body:
I'm a total spaz head 
And I'll remember the things I have to do hours in advance - but when it comes time for it I always forget - I like this app because It's very neat and modern - easy to use, basic setup and easy to review. I also like how it makes you feel all good inside by saying things like "Yay that makes 10 in a row" even if it's not 10 of the 'same' things and just 10 'completed' tasks - because sometimes we just need that little extra oomph 🙈)   It'll also keep a running number of your streaks of each task - which I like :) 

I've tried asking Siri to "Remind me to _____ "  but for some reason that never really worked lol
I also like that there are so many task options to choose from with so many colors and icons (hehe)

As of right now I have the free version - but considering I'm such a scatter brain lol I will need to be reminded of more than 5 things haha (which also unlocks a lot more features - woohoo🎉) 

So I will be getting the full app after typing out this review ☝🏼️

I definitely recommend for moms and/or people on a fitness journey because it'll remind you to get your little ones food prepped for school the night before, so that you can get your home workout in in the morning instead of frantically running around trying to wake your brain up enough to think of what to send him with. 

Remind yourself of everything until it becomes a habit ☝🏼️😊 

Like contacts out before I slip into a sleep coma, dishes done before I go brush my teeth - random stuff like that 

All I can say is that I've been on point since using this app 👌🏼👌🏼☺️

title: Best Paid For App!!❤️
body:
This is the most useful app on my iPhone!
It's a great way to clearly set daily, weekly, & monthly goals. It's a great reminder & motivation to stay on track with those goals/habits. It only has positive feedback--I am not made to feel guilty when I miss habits, but I am uplifted & encouraged when I accomplish my goals. I am a person who thrives on having to to-do lists & a huge motivator is getting to scratch completed tasks off my lists. That results in messy piles of half scribbled on paper scattered about my house. Now all my repeating to-do's stay organized in this app. In addition it almost makes a game out of accomplishing my habits by keeping track of how many days in a row I've completed them. Even more exciting when I accomplish all my goals for the day because it saves as a "perfect" day & keeps track of how many perfect days I have in a row. 
I'm also not overwhelmed by all that needs done in one day because it breaks the day up into morning, noon, & evening. That way I can focus only on what needs done now. 
Well worth the upgrade!!!

body: There is only one thing wrong with this app. The colors are nice, there are a lot of different options for when to fill in your chart, you can track progress daily, weekly or monthly and see how you're progressing. title: Incredibly Helpful and Well-made
body:
I've always wanted to keep up a habit of writing daily, but it wasn't until I picked up Productive that I realized my goal. For almost sixty days, Productive has helped me stay on track with all habits I'm interested in keeping.

Productive's intuitive design makes adding and taking care of habits simple and quick, meaning you'll spend more time doing what you want and less time trying to figure out how to remind yourself.

Productive's statistics and offered information gives further motivation to complete all the goals you can think to set, and customizable reminders are sure to keep you on track.

In a recent update, Productive added the ability to change what time your day starts, so if you're like me and sometimes don't finis a task until two AM, you've got nothing to worry about.

Everything considered, Productive is an excellent life-improvement tool that absolutely deserves your attention. If you're someone who hasn't been serious about properly establishing habits and accomplishing goals but you'd like to be, Productive should have you covered.

title: Wow Outstanding Kudos
body:
I would call myself OCD with ADD. So I want to be productive and organized, but I forget and get distracted; hell, I even need a reminder to take my ADD medication. Needless to say, I have been a junkie of sorts for apps like this and have spent my share of money on reminders/to do/pomodoro apps. This one is the real deal. It is extraordinary in its well thought out simplicity. Other apps may do similar things, but they are too busy; the visual aspect of an app is very important and this one nails it. I found it when I was searching apps that have a Watch supplement app because a  reminder that goes off when I am no where near my phone is useless. 

I am not someone motivated by stars and ‘atta girls (or boys)’. In fact they make me want to rebel and say ‘FU, I don’t need your praise.’ In this app, they are very subtle and for some reason don’t elicit that emotional response from me. All in all, I am very impressed and this app gets five stars for UI, aesthetics, execution. The only thing I would do is continue to add icons. I would like an RX symbol for medication and a pile of dishes. 

Even the method of entry is perfectly done: download the app, test it out, and then if you like it, buy it through upgrading (I really dislike the ‘lite’ versioning method). The free app is not crippled, what is missing is very clear (and very little). It would be quite useful in its free state for someone without a watch and just a few ‘habits’ to invite into one’s repertoire. I suspect this app has a very high conversion rate.
author: Practigal

title: Not sure what all the hype is about.
body:
1) There is no ability to sync between devices. That alone doesn't make this app worthwhile.

2) There is no way to skip a task/habit without being penalized. When you're held to such strict standards, an app that is supposed to be motivating becomes demotivating and discourages you. Let's face it: sometimes you can't reach your goal: Vacations (can't walk the dog 15 minutes every day when you're in another country), or illness (you're not gonna exercise when you have a stomach flu), etc. You should be able to skip a task and at that time, be prompted to explain why and NOT be penalized for it. You either completed a task and keep your streak alive, skip a task for a legitimate reason (as I've explained above) and keep a streak alive, or miss a task entirely and the streak ends. It's that simple.

3) The icons for the habits are childish looking. I would much rather use an icon from my emoji keyboard as it would look more crisp. Apps like "Momentum," "Habit Lists," "Done," and "Habitat" are MUCH more beautifully interfaced in this regard. I just feel like the icons and font in this app looks very "busy" and juvenile. If you're paying for this, you should be able to determine whether you want an icon or not and choose your own font. 

4) If you've already been tracking your habits with another app and then want to use this one, there is no way (even with the paid version) to go back and add  completed habits in retrospect. This is unacceptable and no user who has been using another habit app prior to downloading this one will be willing to deal with that fundamental flaw. 

If these things were changed, it could be the most complete habit tracking app out there. It just isn't right now.

I'm hoping either this app, or Habit List, Habit Streaks, Done, Momentum or Habitat can figure out a way to put all the things a user wants into one app so I can stop waiting and start tracking. I'll just hold onto all these apps and watch for updates until someone gets it right.

body: I've tried several habit/goal tracking apps, but after a few days of use I think this app is the best of them all. I found it more enjoyable to use than other apps of this type. The option to specify morning, afternoon, or evening habits is also very useful, allowing focus on habits in the right context.  Overall this is just a first-rate app and one I expect to be using for some time to come.

title: Very Good App
body:
I don't write reviews and this app is just so helpful that I'd like to support the devs and write a quick review. The features are great! I'm still learning about what makes a task "over due" but I've spent maybe 5 minutes figuring out the app and getting things set up. It's very quick and easy to do. 

Productive has helped me and my ADD rememeber that tomorrow is trash day and I need to take out the trash. It helps me remember that it's my turn to do the dishes in the house. It helps me remember exactly what I need to do on those days. It's much easier to use than simply setting up iCal reminders (which get diluted since I use my person calendar in conjuction with my work calendar)

I could see how this app would be helpful if I was still in college to remind me that it's time to study. It's easy for life to absorb us and suddenly it's 10:30 pm and nothing has been done. 

Thanks guys. Keep up the good work!

title: Beautiful solution to remembering the little things in life
body: I'm the type of person to get lost in focussing on the large events of the day/week. Not surprisingly, the little things in life tend to fall by the way-side. With Productive, you can create a custom item, choose the frequency with which you'd like to do it, and Productive with send you regular, non-intrusive reminders for the little things in life that are so easy to forget. For example, daily reminders to take a vitamin/medication (and keep track if you've already taken one earlier!), weekly reminder to water the plants or vacuum, or even monthly reminders to call an old friend or sibling. Wonderful and thoughtful evolution to the dev's previous app, "Balanced". Great job!

title: Perfect app to schedule your routine
body:
I'm using this as a complement to a traditional to-do list. Where an app like Any.Do can be a place where I write down the errands I need to run and tasks I need to knock out in the next day, week, or month, this app gives me a structure to my basic life. This app is the one that will remind you that you should vacuum today, or that you wanted to study coding twice a week in the evenings, but that it's Thursday and you haven't done it this week yet. 

This is the app that I think those of us that don't have a super structured life have been looking for. 

I'm very motivated by stats and streaks, and was delighted to see that the developer included that aspect. 

I'm looking forward to trying this app out long term. I think it's going to be a hit in the Productivity category in no time.

title: Some problems come up, but okay over all
body:
Dear Productive,

There are 2 issues that i found in the app that makes me distracted. 

Firstly, the all day list and the day part list are separated by the done tasks of list 1, so I cannot see the undone tasks in 1 screen. I had to scroll to see all the tasks which is not very convenient to quickly glance. 

Secondly, also lastly, I wonder that you guys can make functions to manage work project/ long term project in between. Like studying several subjects at the same time means having to do multiple projects to follow. Each subject lasts for few weeks or something. 

If you can solve these problems, it would help me a lot. 

Thanks for reading my letter. 

App version - 1.41

System - iPhone 7, 12.3.1, vi, D10AP

title: Phần mềm khá hữu ích nhưng còn một số điểm sau:
body:
1. Ý tưởng rất tốt nhưng còn chưa hoàn thiện, mới chỉ ở bước đầu ở việc nhắc nhở nhưng nhắc nhở ko có chuông báo, hay cảnh báo theo quy luật nào đó của khách hàng tự set hoặc chu kì cảnh báo 15p/lần nếu người dùng ko nhấn vào đã nhận cvieecj hay thói quen.
2 Giá quá mắc cho một phần mềm sơ khai, ko hợp lý ở chỗ thu phí hàng tháng quá cao! Nếu phần mềm này cỡ 150-200k cho một lần mu vĩnh viễn thì hợp lý hơn. Nếu ko vẫn có phương án dùng các app nhắc nhở trên điện thoại hoàn toàn coa thể thay thế được.

title: The latest release is buggy and not very good
body: I’ve been a Productive user for almost two years. The latest release is buggy (they’ve acknowledged it on my support request) and you will end up having streaks ruined even after you’ve completed contributing habits. The new user interface is also a classic case of making something look pretty...at the cost of usability. The old interface was straightforward and simple but now I have to deal with swiping across to see missed habits/activities and the top third of the screen is a silly graphic which stops being cute after the first use.

title: App is reactive not proactive
body:
This app is great, except: I cannot view future tasks for the week ahead. 
In the beginning of a week I like to know what my tasks are, as I want to be proactive, not reactive. 

This app makes the user reactive, which is not conducive to create longterm routines, which is why I want to use the app to get me into a routine. 

At this stage, if I add “end if the month”, when is end of the month? If something needs to be done on a work day end of the month, and end of the month falls on a Saturday the task is now not “relevant”? 

Suggestion
It would be great if dates can be added to tasks.
As well as a future calendar view.
